# Using a virtual mailbox address on a passport application
Short answer: The passport forms treat two addresses differently. The mailing address (item 8) is where the State Department sends your passport. It can be a street address or a P.O. Box, and the form expects that you may not live there. The permanent address is for where you actually live: "Do not list a P.O. Box." So a mailbox address can go in item 8, but your home goes in the permanent-address box. The forms don't mention private mailboxes (PMBs) either way. To be certain, ask the National Passport Information Center (NPIC) at 1-877-487-2778.

Below is the exact wording from the current DS-11 (first passport, in person) and DS-82 (renewal by mail), both the 04-2025 editions, plus the USPS summary of the online renewal rules. All read November 28, 2026.

## What the forms say

| Field | Form instructions | What it means for a mailbox address |
| Item 8: Mailing Address | "For line 1 enter applicant's Street/RFD #, or P.O. Box or URB." For line 2, "if you do not live at the address listed in this field, put the name of the person who lives at this address and mark it 'In Care Of'" [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds11_pdf.PDF) [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds82_pdf.PDF). On the DS-82, line 2 is labeled "Include Apartment, Suite, In Care Of or Attention if applicable" [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds82_pdf.PDF) | The form accepts addresses you don't live at, including P.O. Boxes. Nobody lives at a mailbox company, so the "In Care Of" wording doesn't really fit. The line-2 label lists "Suite", which is where a mailbox or PMB number would go |
| Permanent Address (item 19 on the DS-11, item 18 on the DS-82) | "Complete if P.O. Box is listed under Mailing Address or if residence is different from Mailing Address. Do not list a P.O. Box." The field asks for "Street/RFD # or URB" [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds11_pdf.PDF) [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds82_pdf.PDF) | If your mailing address is a mailbox, you fill this in with your actual home address |
| Delivery abroad | "We will not mail a U.S. passport to a private address outside the United States or Canada" [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds11_pdf.PDF) [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds82_pdf.PDF) | A U.S. mailbox address is inside the United States |
| Address changes | "If your mailing address changes prior to receipt of your new passport, please contact NPIC" [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds11_pdf.PDF) [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds82_pdf.PDF) | If you close or switch mailboxes mid-application, call NPIC |

## Renewing online
USPS lists the State Department's online renewal requirements. One of them: "You have a mailing address in a U.S. state or territory. You cannot renew online using an Army, Fleet, or Diplomatic Post Office address" [source](https://www.usps.com/international/passports.htm). Online renewal is routine service only, and if you need expedited service you must renew by mail [source](https://www.usps.com/international/passports.htm). The rule names APO, FPO and DPO addresses as the exclusions. It doesn't mention commercial mailbox addresses.

## If you live abroad
The DS-82 says "U.S. citizens residing outside the United States and Canada cannot submit this form to the domestic addresses listed above" and must follow their U.S. embassy or consulate's procedures [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds82_pdf.PDF). The DS-11 says that in most countries you must apply in person at an embassy or consulate [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds11_pdf.PDF). A U.S. mailbox doesn't change where you apply from. For setting up a mailbox from overseas, see getting a U.S. virtual mailbox while living abroad.

## Expect two or three envelopes
Both forms say: "You may receive your newly issued U.S. passport book and/or card and your citizenship evidence in two separate mailings. If you are applying for both a book and card, you may receive three separate mailings" [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds11_pdf.PDF) [source](https://eforms.state.gov/Forms/ds82_pdf.PDF). Citizenship evidence can mean your original birth certificate. At a mailbox, each envelope shows up as its own item.

## Receiving a passport at your mailbox safely

- Use the exact mailbox address, including the box or suite number, and the name on your Form 1583. See how to write a virtual mailbox address.
- Turn off automatic open-and-scan if your provider has it on, so the envelope is forwarded unopened. At Traveling Mailbox, automatic scanning "tells our team to open and scan incoming letters covered by that setting" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953).
- Forward it with tracking, or pick it up. Ship it as soon as it arrives, or collect it if your location allows pickup (pickup rules by provider).
- Watch the auto-shred clock. At Traveling Mailbox and Stable, paper you don't act on is shredded after 30 days [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing). See shredding policies.
US Global Mail says it logs, tracks and verifies "every single item" with a barcoding system: "Whether you're receiving a check or a passport, it's handled with care and documented at every stage" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022398-how-is-my-mail-protected-physically-and-digitally).

## Links

- Form DS-11 (State Department) · Form DS-82 (State Department)
- US Global Mail
- Traveling Mailbox

# Shopping U.S. stores from abroad: consolidation and forwarding fees
Short answer: Have your orders delivered to a U.S. mailbox address, let several packages pile up, then ask the provider to combine them into one box and ship it to you. Consolidating usually saves postage, but the repack fee varies: Traveling Mailbox charges nothing extra (postage + $2 per shipment), iPostal1 $1.95 per package, US Global Mail $5 per box, and Virtual Post Mail $3.75 per package handling. You fill out the customs declaration, and the provider may open boxes to check what's inside.

This page is about packages, meaning things you buy. For forwarding letters overseas and getting a mailbox with a foreign ID, see getting a U.S. virtual mailbox while living abroad. Every fee below is from the provider's own page, read November 28, 2026. Postage is always extra and depends on weight, size and destination.

## Consolidation and international package fees

| Provider | Consolidation / repack | Forwarding fee (plus postage) | Insurance | Other package services |
| Traveling Mailbox | "We can consolidate at no extra charge" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | $2 per shipment, not per piece; USPS, FedEx or UPS [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | — | Receives "any size package" and forwards it "anywhere in the world"; 30 days free package storage, then $0.10/lb/day [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| US Global Mail | $5 per box, $2 per letter [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) | No handling fee ("No Handling Fees") [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) | First $100 of package value free [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022398-how-is-my-mail-protected-physically-and-digitally) | You can ask that packages ship "as received unless you request inspection", and add packing instructions [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) |
| iPostal1 | Letters free; $1.95 per package or letter-pack consolidated; $1.95 for any number of magazines [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Live carrier rates; "International shipping not available at all locations" [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $4 per $100 requested [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Commercial invoice prepared at no extra cost; photos of invoice $2.95, contents $3.95, both $5.95 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Virtual Post Mail | Multiple packages are combined into one box by default [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/62-package-handling) | Handling $3.75 per package, $0.50 per mail piece; postage marked up 10% to 20% [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/362-shipping-prices) | — | Packing slips removed from international boxes; you declare items and values [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/62-package-handling) |
| PostScan Mail (Package Locker) | — | Basic Locker $4.95/mo: $3 processing + $2 forwarding per item. Premium Locker $9.95/mo: $2 + $1 per item [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | — | Package storage 7 days free (Basic) or 14 days (Premium), then $0.10/lb/day [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Stable | "Can also combine mail and packages going to the same address" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Postage only, shipped "anywhere in the world" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | — | — |
| Anytime Mailbox | — | Set by each mail center; ships internationally [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | — | "There may be taxes or duty fees involved depending on the contents" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) |

## Worked example: four orders in one box
Four small packages arrive from four U.S. stores, and you ship them together in one box. Repack and handling fees only, with postage left out:

- Traveling Mailbox: $2 (one shipment, consolidation free) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953)
- US Global Mail: $5 (one consolidated box) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained)
- iPostal1: 4 × $1.95 = $7.80 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php)
- PostScan Mail Basic Locker: 4 × ($3 + $2) = $20, plus the $4.95 monthly locker fee [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html)
Virtual Post Mail is left out because its help page lists handling as "$3.75 / package" without saying whether that's per package received or per box shipped [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/362-shipping-prices). The bigger number is usually postage. Combining four boxes into one is what lowers it, and Virtual Post Mail notes that shipping boxes unopened inside an "overpack" box "may increase the shipping cost" because of the extra weight [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/56-original-box).

## Customs: you're the one declaring

- You declare contents and value. Virtual Post Mail: "we are not a customs broker", and "it is your responsibility to ensure that what you ship is acceptable for the destination country" [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/129-not-customs-broker). Vague descriptions like "bag" "can result in the shipment being returned by Customs" [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/368-how-do-i-declare-items-when-shipping-internationally).
- Europe needs more data. VPM says most European countries now require a harmonized (HS) code for each declared item [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/368-how-do-i-declare-items-when-shipping-internationally). It also says EU customs began requiring an HS code plus product identifiers on shipments to non-VAT-registered recipients from November 1, 2026 [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/556-2026-mandatory-eu-product-identifiers-pids-customs-compliance).
- Boxes may be opened. VPM reserves the right to open packages to check for hazardous, illegal or customs-restricted items [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/56-original-box). iPostal1 opens packages "to ensure compliance with shipping regulations" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
- Batteries slow things down. Lithium batteries are hazardous materials to carriers. VPM pauses those shipments, and as a re-shipper it can't sign a Dangerous Goods Form for you [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/548-shipping-lithium-batteries-hazardous-materials).
- Duties are on you. Anytime Mailbox warns of taxes or duty fees depending on contents [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq).

## Before you start ordering

- Pick a location that ships internationally. At iPostal1 it isn't available everywhere [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
- Mind the storage clock while packages accumulate: 30 days free at Traveling Mailbox [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953), 7 or 14 days on PostScan lockers [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html). See storage fees by provider.
- Check size limits before buying furniture or anything large. See receiving packages.
- Keep receipts for the declared value, and insure anything expensive.

## Links

- Traveling Mailbox
- US Global Mail
- Virtual Post Mail
- iPostal1
- PostScan Mail

# Switching virtual mailbox locations, or when yours closes
Short answer: At most providers you can't just edit your address. Each address has its own Form 1583, so switching usually means opening a new mailbox at the new location, completing a new form, updating your senders yourself, and keeping the old box open until mail stops arriving. USPS rules don't allow a change-of-address order when a mailbox relationship ends, so there's no automatic forwarding from the old box.

This applies when you move to a closer location, want a different state, or your provider moves a location. Each provider's own policy, checked November 28, 2026.

## Why you can't file a change of address
USPS rules for mailbox companies (called CMRAs) say: "When the agency relationship between the CMRA and the addressee terminates, neither the addressee nor the CMRA will file a change-of-address order with the Post Office." The CMRA must instead remail your mail "for at least 6 months after the termination date", with new postage [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Virtual Post Mail says it plainly: "USPS will not allow you to file a Change of Address from one of our mailbox locations to another" [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/196-changing-locations). Anytime Mailbox: "a change of address form cannot be submitted for a digital mailbox" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/renter/faq).

## Switching locations, provider by provider

| Provider | How a switch works | New Form 1583? | Overlap advice |
| US Global Mail | No direct change once your Form 1583 is approved. Before approval you can change the address [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11272138-what-if-i-want-to-change-my-us-global-mail-virtual-mailbox-address). After approval: open a new account (with a different email address) at the new location [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/14009887-how-can-i-change-my-us-global-mail-address-to-a-new-location) | Yes, but "if you already have a notarized Form 1583 on file, you do not need a new notary appointment" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/14009887-how-can-i-change-my-us-global-mail-address-to-a-new-location) | Keep both accounts until no more mail is coming to the old one. Closing early gets a prorated refund for unused time [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/14009887-how-can-i-change-my-us-global-mail-address-to-a-new-location) |
| Traveling Mailbox | Open a new account at the new address. Accounts can be linked so you switch between them without signing out [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/change-traveling-mailbox-addresses?ref=3953) | Yes, for every recipient on the new account [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/do-i-need-a-new-usps-form-1583-when-switching-addresses/) | Keep the old one open until mail arrives at the new address; no fixed overlap period [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/can-i-keep-both-traveling-mailbox-accounts-open-while-switching-addresses/) |
| Virtual Post Mail | Sign up for a new plan at the new address, then email a cancellation request for the old one. A transfer feature lets you manage both under one login [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/196-changing-locations) | Yes. VPM waives the notary if you have an active, verified account, but you still provide current ID [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/196-changing-locations) | Wait "at least 1-2 months" before canceling the old mailbox [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/196-changing-locations) |
| iPostal1 | If a new location opens closer to you, "you will be able to request for your account to be transferred". You can also add locations to one account [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | Yes, "an updated notarized USPS Form 1583" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | — |

## Your old mail and scans don't move

- Traveling Mailbox: "Your mail and scans stay with your previous account." Download the scans you want and forward the originals you need before closing. After closure, it receives leftover mail for up to six months, and you can still sign in to request forwarding (shipping and handling charges apply) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/change-traveling-mailbox-addresses?ref=3953).
- US Global Mail: mail that arrives after you close the old account "will be securely shredded" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/14009887-how-can-i-change-my-us-global-mail-address-to-a-new-location).
- Virtual Post Mail: the new account needs a new username, but you can transfer the mailbox to your other login in Mailbox Settings [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/196-changing-locations).
Closing the old box follows each provider's normal cancellation rules. See canceling a virtual mailbox.

## When the provider closes or moves your location
Virtual Post Mail has published its own example. When it left its Walnut, California office, it gave customers until March 31, 2023, "about 6 months", to move to a new Covina address. The mailbox number stayed the same, staff processed mail at both addresses until the lease ended, and VPM said it now owns all the buildings its offices are in [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/348-walnut-address-move). Its disaster plan says that if a single site has to shut for days, letters may be sent to other locations for scanning (about 3 to 5 business days of delay), while packages stay on site until it reopens [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/248-contingency-disaster-plan).
US Global Mail says its own facilities are in California, New York, Las Vegas and Texas. Elsewhere, physical mail is handled at "the designated location or a Channel Partner" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022398-how-is-my-mail-protected-physically-and-digitally). At Anytime Mailbox and iPostal1, mail is handled by local businesses: Anytime calls them "operator mailing partners" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq), and iPostal1 says most of its locations are "professional retail pack and ship stores or business coworking centers" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php). Neither page says what happens if a partner location closes, so ask before you sign up.

## A switch checklist

- Open the new mailbox first and get its Form 1583 approved [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/do-i-need-a-new-usps-form-1583-when-switching-addresses/) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/14009887-how-can-i-change-my-us-global-mail-address-to-a-new-location).
- Update senders directly: banks, insurers, the IRS, your state, subscriptions. Traveling Mailbox's list: "your bank, insurers, subscriptions and personal contacts" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/change-traveling-mailbox-addresses?ref=3953). For the IRS and other senders, see changing your address.
- Overlap for a month or two. VPM suggests 1 to 2 months [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/196-changing-locations) [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/91-article-switch-your-mail-forwarding-service-without-losing-mail).
- Download scans and forward originals before closing [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/change-traveling-mailbox-addresses?ref=3953).
- If the address is on a state filing (an LLC's principal office or mailing address), update it with the state too. See virtual mailbox for an LLC.

## Links

- US Global Mail
- Traveling Mailbox
- Virtual Post Mail
- iPostal1

# Mail shredding at virtual mailboxes: fees and policies
Short answer: Most providers shred for free. Traveling Mailbox, US Global Mail, Virtual Post Mail, Stable, LegalZoom Virtual Mail (Earth Class Mail) and PhysicalAddress.com all list free shredding. iPostal1 charges $2.25 per shred order, with cheaper bundles, and PostScan Mail charges $1 per item. Some providers also shred paper you haven't acted on once free storage ends, so check that rule before you rely on them to keep originals.

A virtual mailbox scans the outside of each envelope, and then you decide what happens to it: open and scan, forward, or destroy. If you plan to throw away most of your mail, the shredding fee and the auto-disposal rule matter more than the plan price. Here's what each provider publishes, checked November 28, 2026.

## Shredding by provider

| Provider | Shred fee | What happens to mail you don't act on |
| Traveling Mailbox | Free, on site [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953) | Envelopes are kept free for 30 days, then "automatically" shredded on site unless you put an item on hold ($1 per envelope per month) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| US Global Mail | Free ("Free Shred & Recycle mail") [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | 30 days of free physical storage on Occasional and Scale, 60 on Teams, then $0.05 per letter per day [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) |
| Virtual Post Mail | Free: "There is no additional fee for mail shredding" [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) | Free 30-day physical storage is listed on every plan [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) |
| Stable | Included on every plan (scan, ship, shred are listed as basic mail actions) [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Mail you don't forward is stored for 30 days, then "securely shredded" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| LegalZoom Virtual Mail (Earth Class Mail) | Free ("Secure shredding: Free") [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) | Letters stored up to 30 days, packages 10 days [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/personal/virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| PhysicalAddress.com | Free secure shredding [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) | Envelopes, magazines and postcards stored free for 90 days [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) |
| iPostal1 | $2.25 per order (1 envelope, up to 10 pages), then $0.25 per page. Bundles of scan or shred orders: 5 for $10, 10 for $18, 20 for $30 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | 30 days free for letters, then $1.10 per item per month. A separate "discard mail items" service is included in every plan [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| PostScan Mail | $1.00 per item for the first 10 pages, then $0.15 per page [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | You can choose to recycle, shred or store each item [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) |
| Anytime Mailbox | Set by each mail center [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | Disposed mail is recycled; shredding is offered "as an additional option" for sensitive documents [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) |

Prices from each provider's own pricing page or FAQ, checked November 28, 2026. Anytime Mailbox locations are run by independent operators, so the shred fee, if any, is on each location's plan details.

## Shredding vs recycling vs discarding
Some providers offer two ways to get rid of mail. Anytime Mailbox says its operators "recycle all mail that is disposed of", and shredding is the option for "documents containing sensitive information" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq). iPostal1 includes a free "discard mail items" service, while a shred order costs $2.25 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php). PostScan Mail lets you choose recycle or shred for each item [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html). Anything with an account number, Social Security number or signature belongs in the shred pile.

## Where the shredding happens

- Traveling Mailbox: "Our team destroys the paper original at our processing facility" in Sanford, North Carolina [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953) [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-does-traveling-mailbox-protect-my-mail-and-personal-information/).
- Virtual Post Mail: mail is "shredded on-site using a mobile shredding service", so it "does not leave our facility for shredding" [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/161-is-my-mail-secure).
- LegalZoom Virtual Mail: unwanted mail "is securely shredded and recycled on-site" [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html).

## What 20 shredded letters a month costs
Say 20 letters a month arrive that you never want opened, each under 10 pages:

- Traveling Mailbox, US Global Mail, Virtual Post Mail, Stable, LegalZoom, PhysicalAddress.com: $0 in shred fees [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/).
- PostScan Mail: 20 × $1.00 = $20 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- iPostal1: 20 × $2.25 = $45 as single orders, or $30 with a 20-order bundle [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php). Using the free discard service instead costs nothing [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
Shredded items still count as received mail on plans with a monthly item limit, unless the provider excludes junk. See does junk mail count?

## Don't lose an original you need

- Know the auto-shred clock. At Traveling Mailbox and Stable, paper you leave alone is shredded after 30 days [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing). Put a hold on, or forward, anything you need to keep, like a car title, a birth certificate or a new passport.
- Save scans before you close an account. At US Global Mail, mail that arrives after you close an old account "will be securely shredded" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/14009887-how-can-i-change-my-us-global-mail-address-to-a-new-location).
- Request shredding carefully. Traveling Mailbox advises saving any digital copies or originals you want "before choosing a disposal action" [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-does-traveling-mailbox-protect-my-mail-and-personal-information/).

## Links

- Traveling Mailbox
- US Global Mail
- Virtual Post Mail
- iPostal1
- PostScan Mail

# Who opens your mail? Virtual mailbox security and privacy
Short answer: Staff at the mail center handle every piece and scan the outside of each envelope. They open a letter only when you ask for a content scan, or when an auto-scan setting you turned on covers it. Who those staff are depends on the model. Providers that run their own facilities, like Traveling Mailbox, Virtual Post Mail and US Global Mail's own locations, describe background-checked employees and on-site shredding. Network providers, like Anytime Mailbox, iPostal1 and US Global Mail's partner locations, have your mail handled by a local business.

Every claim below comes from the provider's own security, FAQ or help pages, read November 28, 2026. These are the providers' descriptions of themselves; we haven't audited them.

## When is your mail opened?

- Traveling Mailbox: "We scan the outside first. We open a letter when you request a scan or when your automatic scanning settings apply. You can also ask us to forward it unopened" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953).
- iPostal1: "We open your letter mail only if you specifically request us to scan the contents." Packages are opened only for a content photo or "to ensure compliance with shipping regulations" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
- Virtual Post Mail: "By default, we do not open and scan the content of mail arriving at our facility." For private contents it suggests skipping scans and having mail shipped instead [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/161-is-my-mail-secure).
- Anytime Mailbox: you choose open and scan, shred, forward or pickup for each item [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq).

## Who handles it, provider by provider

| Provider | Who handles physical mail | Facility security | Shredding |
| US Global Mail | At its own facilities, "only trained and background-checked employees", "no third-party contractors" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11250327-who-has-access-to-my-mail). Outside its owned locations in CA, NY, LV and TX, mail is handled "at the designated location or a Channel Partner" contracted to follow its protocols [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022398-how-is-my-mail-protected-physically-and-digitally) | HD surveillance, electronic doors, restricted access; every item barcoded and logged [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022398-how-is-my-mail-protected-physically-and-digitally) | Free shred and recycle [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) |
| Traveling Mailbox | Its own team at its Sanford, NC facility; "background checks and ongoing security training" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953) | Access controls, video surveillance, not open to the public; envelopes barcoded [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-does-traveling-mailbox-protect-my-mail-and-personal-information/) | Free, at its facility [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953) |
| Virtual Post Mail | "Mail processing is done exclusively by VPM staff"; "never stored or processed by any third-party facility" [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/196-changing-locations) | 24/7 security monitoring; only authorized people in storage and scanning rooms [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/161-is-my-mail-secure) | On site by a mobile shredding service; free [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/161-is-my-mail-secure) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) |
| LegalZoom Virtual Mail (Earth Class Mail) | "Background-checked technicians" [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) | "Secure, access-controlled facilities" [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) | Shredded and recycled on site; free [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Anytime Mailbox | Local "operator mailing partners" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | — | Recycling by default; shredding offered as an option [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) |
| iPostal1 | The mail center at the address you choose; most are retail pack-and-ship stores or coworking centers [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | — | $2.25 per shred order [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| PostScan Mail | — | Its security page covers data (AWS) security, not the mail facility [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/security.html) | $1 per item [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |

## Account and data security

| Provider | Two-factor sign-in | Audits and encryption, as stated |
| US Global Mail | Yes [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022398-how-is-my-mail-protected-physically-and-digitally) | "SOC 2 audited and HIPAA compliant"; card payments handled by Stripe, not stored by USGM [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022398-how-is-my-mail-protected-physically-and-digitally) |
| Virtual Post Mail | — | "Fully SOC2 Type II certified"; mail data on AWS U.S. East, encrypted at rest with AES-256; audit reports "available upon request"; breach notice within 30 days of confirmation [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/161-is-my-mail-secure) |
| Traveling Mailbox | Yes, by authenticator app or text; Face ID in the iOS app [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953) | Encrypted connection; customer data encrypted with multiple copies [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953) |
| Stable | — | SOC 2 security listed on the pricing page [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| PostScan Mail | Yes [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/security.html) | Hosted on AWS; data encrypted at rest with 256-bit AES [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/security.html) |
| Anytime Mailbox | — | 2048-bit SSL; mail images are left out of email notifications on purpose, so they're only viewable in the portal [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) |

## Who else sees your mail data

- Virtual Post Mail doesn't share personal information "unless we are served with proper documentation such as a subpoena or court order", and uses outside services such as AWS, CRM and email systems to run its service [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/161-is-my-mail-secure).
- Traveling Mailbox: "We don't sell or share personal information for third-party marketing," apart from limited sharing with service providers like payment processors [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953).
- USPS requires every mailbox company to keep your Form 1583 and ID on file and in the USPS CMRA Customer Registration Database [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). That's the law, not a provider choice. See Form 1583.

## How to keep sensitive mail private

- Leave auto-scan off for personal mail and choose open-and-scan one item at a time [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953).
- Ship sensitive items unopened. Traveling Mailbox ("Ship to Me") and VPM both suggest this [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/secure-solutions?ref=3953) [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/161-is-my-mail-secure).
- Turn on two-factor sign-in where it's offered.
- Shred, don't just discard, anything with account numbers. See shredding fees and policies.
- For patient mail, you need a Business Associate Agreement. See HIPAA-compliant virtual mailboxes.

## Links

- US Global Mail
- Traveling Mailbox
- Virtual Post Mail
- Stable

# Receiving packages at a virtual mailbox
Short answer: Yes. Because a virtual mailbox is a street address, it takes deliveries from UPS, FedEx, DHL and Amazon as well as USPS. US Global Mail and PostScan Mail name Amazon specifically [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11271996-can-i-send-packages-to-my-virtual-mailbox) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html). What varies is how long packages are stored free, size limits, and, at Traveling Mailbox, a separate package address [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/where-do-i-send-packages-so-that-they-can-be-forwarded-to-me/).

The practical questions are which carriers each provider accepts, whether big boxes are a problem, how long a package sits free, and what it costs after that. All from the providers' own pages, checked November 27, 2026. For shipping packages onward, see forwarding fees.

## Carriers and package rules by provider

| Provider | Carriers accepted | Free package storage | After that | Size and other rules |
| US Global Mail | "USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL, Amazon, and more" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11271996-can-i-send-packages-to-my-virtual-mailbox) | 30 days (Scale), 60 days (Teams) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11328326) | $0.10 per lb per day [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11328326) | Packages processed Monday to Friday; weekend shipment requests go out the next business day [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/14424304-what-is-the-package-processing-schedule-at-us-global-mail) |
| iPostal1 | USPS, "FedEx, UPS and other carriers" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | 30 days under 12×12×12 in; 10 days up to 24×17×12 in; 5 days at or over 24×17×12 in [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $1.10 per lb per month, per 10 days, or per 5 days by the same size bands [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Content photos $3.95; consolidation $1.95 per package [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Anytime Mailbox | "USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL, and any other shipping company" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | Set by each location | Set by each location | Locations "will sign for all your mail and package deliveries" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) |
| PostScan Mail | "USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL, and Amazon" [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) | 3 days, or 7 days on an annual plan [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | $0.10 per lb per day [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | Over 25 lbs or over 110 in length and girth: $0.25 per lb. Packages count toward the plan's item limit [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Traveling Mailbox | Parcel carriers; "does not accept freight deliveries" [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/what-is-the-largest-package-that-traveling-mailbox-can-receive-on-my-behalf/) | 30 days [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-long-can-you-hold-packages-for/) | $0.10 per lb per day [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-long-can-you-hold-packages-for/) | Ship packages to its Sanford, NC package address even if your letter address is elsewhere [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/where-do-i-send-packages-so-that-they-can-be-forwarded-to-me/) |
| Virtual Post Mail | "All couriers, including FedEx and UPS" [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/40-package-receiving-couriers) | 15 days (Starter, Plus, Business), 30 days (Premium) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) | — | Signs for items that need a signature [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/40-package-receiving-couriers). Perishable packages get 7 days of guaranteed storage [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/105-mail-storage) |
| Stable | "FedEx, UPS, DHL, and USPS" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Up to 15 days [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Disposed of after the storage period [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | — |
| PhysicalAddress.com | "UPS/FedEx Can Deliver" [source](https://physicaladdress.com/registered-agent-service/) | 1 week [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) | — | — |

Anytime Mailbox locations are independently run, so storage and fees are shown on each location's plan details [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq). See Anytime Mailbox pricing.

## Why a PO Box can't do this
Virtual Post Mail puts it simply: "A regular PO box only allows you to accept parcels from USPS itself" [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/40-package-receiving-couriers). Some Post Offices offer a street-address option for PO Boxes; see virtual mailbox vs PO Box for how that works.

## Addressing a package so it isn't refused

- Your name plus the mailbox number on every label. USGM: "be sure the sender includes your name and mailbox number on the label" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11271996-can-i-send-packages-to-my-virtual-mailbox). Traveling Mailbox says to replace the placeholder with your real mailbox number and use an authorized recipient name [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/where-do-i-send-packages-so-that-they-can-be-forwarded-to-me/).
- Only names on your Form 1583. If a CMRA has no Form 1583 on file for the addressee, USPS rules say it must return the mail marked "No Authorization to Receive Mail for this Addressee" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). See Form 1583 for a business for adding names.
- Check the format (PMB, # or Suite) in how to write a virtual mailbox address.

## Large and heavy items

- Traveling Mailbox: if an item "must arrive through a freight service, it is not eligible for delivery," and it asks you to check the seller's shipping method first. It doesn't repack [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/what-is-the-largest-package-that-traveling-mailbox-can-receive-on-my-behalf/).
- PostScan Mail: accepts oversized boxes, with a $0.25 per lb surcharge over 25 lbs or 110 inches in length and girth [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- iPostal1: big boxes get less free storage: 5 days at or over 24×17×12 inches, versus 30 days under 12×12×12 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).

## What a package costs to hold: one example
A 10 lb box left 10 days past the free period costs 10 × $0.10 × 10 = $10 at US Global Mail, PostScan Mail or Traveling Mailbox, which all charge $0.10 per lb per day [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11328326) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-long-can-you-hold-packages-for/). The difference is when that clock starts: day 4 at PostScan on a monthly plan, day 31 at Traveling Mailbox. For letters too, see how long mail is kept.

## Links

- US Global Mail
- Traveling Mailbox
- Virtual Post Mail
- iPostal1
- PostScan Mail

# Virtual mailbox addresses on a driver's license
Short answer: Usually only as a mailing address. Federal REAL ID rules require "at least two documents ... that include the individual's name and principal residence" [source](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-6/chapter-I/part-37/subpart-B/section-37.11), and states ask for a residential address. Texas says "A business address is not acceptable" [source](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/37-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-15-25), and Florida asks for two documents with your Florida residential address [source](https://www.flhsmv.gov/driver-licenses-id-cards/what-to-bring/u-s-citizen/). South Dakota is the main exception: full-time travelers can use a South Dakota mail-forwarding address with a residency affidavit [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=709bcdfa47406e10237fbd51026d43a9).

Mailbox companies often say customers use their address at the DMV. iPostal1's FAQ says "the vast majority of states permit this, but the laws vary by state" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php), and US Global Mail says "Many of our customers have used their US Global Mail addresses for their driver's licenses" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022325-what-can-or-can-t-the-us-global-mail-address-be-used-for). The states' own pages are stricter. Here is what the federal rule and three states with clear published rules say. Checked November 27, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the licensing office before you go.

## The federal baseline: REAL ID

- Proof of address: "To document the address of principal residence, a person must present at least two documents of the State's choice that include the individual's name and principal residence" [source](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-6/chapter-I/part-37/subpart-B/section-37.11).
- What's printed on the card: the "Address of principal residence," except where state law or DMV procedure allows an alternative address, or for people in address confidentiality programs and a few other listed groups [source](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-6/chapter-I/part-37/subpart-B/section-37.17).
So a mailbox address can only be printed where a state has chosen to allow an alternative address, and you still prove where you actually live.

## State by state

| State | Residence address | Where a mailbox address fits | Rule on forwarded mail |
| Texas | "The applicant's Texas residence address must be given. A business address is not acceptable" [source](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/37-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-15-25). Two documents with your name and Texas residential address, one showing 30 days in Texas [source](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/texas-residency-requirement-driver-licenses-and-id-cards) | As a separate mailing address "in addition to a Texas residence address" [source](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/37-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-15-25) | "Mail addressed with a forwarding label or address label affixed to the envelope or contents is not acceptable" [source](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/37-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-15-49) |
| Florida | Two different documents "with their Florida residential address," such as a lease, utility bill or bank statement (most dated within 60 days) [source](https://www.flhsmv.gov/driver-licenses-id-cards/what-to-bring/u-s-citizen/) | The application asks for both a "mailing address" and "proof of residential address" [source](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/322.08) | — |
| South Dakota | Full-time travelers using "a South Dakota mail forwarding address" complete a Residency Affidavit [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=709bcdfa47406e10237fbd51026d43a9) | The PMB itself, with a PMB contract, one document under a year old showing the PMB address, and a receipt for one night's stay in South Dakota within the last year [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=709bcdfa47406e10237fbd51026d43a9) | The affidavit says your PMB "is a mail forwarding service, and not a virtual only mail service" [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=49c27bd087a26250b81f0f280cbb3563) |

Texas exceptions: DPS waives the residency requirement for groups such as Address Confidentiality Program participants, judges and active-duty military [source](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/texas-residency-requirement-driver-licenses-and-id-cards). Florida CDL applicants have stricter lists, and those without a List A document need a Declaration of Domicile filed with the clerk of court [source](https://www.flhsmv.gov/driver-licenses-id-cards/what-to-bring/u-s-citizen/).

## Texas: why forwarded mail fails
Texas accepts bank, credit card and government statements as proof, but they must show your residential address [source](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/texas-residency-requirement-driver-licenses-and-id-cards). A statement sent to your mailbox shows the mailbox address, and anything re-addressed with a forwarding label is rejected outright [source](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/37-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-15-49). If you can't produce two documents, DPS says you "may be eligible to complete a Texas Residency Affidavit" [source](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/texas-residency-requirement-driver-licenses-and-id-cards).

## South Dakota: the full-timer route
South Dakota is the one state here that publishes a path for a PMB address, but only if you don't keep a home elsewhere: "if you maintain a residence in another state, you do not qualify as a full-time traveler" [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=709bcdfa47406e10237fbd51026d43a9). The affidavit also says a South Dakota license means jury duty notices from South Dakota [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=49c27bd087a26250b81f0f280cbb3563). Our mail guide for full-time RVers covers which providers have South Dakota addresses and the open question of what counts as "virtual only."

## What to do

- Keep your residence address on the license and use the mailbox for everything that only needs a mailing address. See changing your address to a virtual mailbox.
- For Form 1583, a driver's license is one of the accepted IDs; see Form 1583 and online notary.
- Full-time travelers who want South Dakota should read the affidavit wording before choosing a provider, and ask SD DPS if unsure.

## Links

- Traveling Mailbox
- US Global Mail
- iPostal1

# Virtual mailbox addresses on Stripe and Amazon seller accounts
Short answer: Not as your verified business address. Stripe's U.S. account rules ask for "the address of the physical location where the majority of your business activity is carried out," and its address-change page says "PO Boxes, HCs, and Private Mailboxes will not be accepted" [source](https://support.stripe.com/questions/requirements-for-having-a-us-stripe-account) [source](https://support.stripe.com/questions/update-your-business-address). A virtual mailbox address is a private mailbox in USPS terms [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Amazon asks for the registered business address on your business license plus proof of your residential address [source](https://sell.amazon.com/sell/registration-guide). Use the mailbox for mail, not for these verification fields.

People often get a virtual mailbox so their home address stays off a payment or marketplace account, then hit a verification wall. Here's what Stripe and Amazon publish about addresses, and where a mailbox address can still help. Checked November 27, 2026. This is a summary of the companies' own help pages, not legal advice, and each company makes its own review decisions.

## Stripe: three different rules

| Stripe product or field | What Stripe says | Mailbox address OK? |
| Business address, any U.S. account | "All businesses must provide the address of the physical location where the majority of your business activity is carried out (PO Boxes are not accepted)" [source](https://support.stripe.com/questions/requirements-for-having-a-us-stripe-account). When you edit it: "It must be a valid US address. PO Boxes, HCs, and Private Mailboxes will not be accepted" [source](https://support.stripe.com/questions/update-your-business-address) | No |
| Issuing, Treasury and Opal (since July 1, 2025) | Stripe screens the business and account representative addresses and no longer allows "addresses associated with mailbox services and virtual address services" [source](https://support.stripe.com/questions/physical-presence-requirement-faq). Its docs name UPS Stores, FedEx Office locations and "virtual mail services" as CMRA addresses it blocks, along with registered agent addresses [source](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/commercial-compliance/address-validation) | No, and the check is automatic |
| Stripe Atlas companies | For "Stripe payments: You can use a physical or virtual U.S. address," and Atlas points people without a U.S. address to its partner Stable [source](https://support.stripe.com/questions/which-address-should-i-use-for-atlas-incorporation). For Issuing, Treasury or Opal, an Atlas company still needs a physical U.S. address that "can't be your Atlas registered agent, nor can it be a mailbox or virtual address service" [source](https://support.stripe.com/questions/physical-presence-requirement-faq) | Payments only, per the Atlas article |

The two Stripe articles don't fully agree: the Atlas article allows a virtual U.S. address for payments, while the business-address page rejects private mailboxes. If you formed through Atlas, follow the Atlas article and keep your formation documents handy; everyone else should expect a private mailbox to be rejected.

### What happens if Stripe flags the address

- Payments keep working. Accounts with a mailbox or registered agent address lose Issuing, Treasury and Opal, but "will still be able to use Stripe for payment processing and other products" [source](https://support.stripe.com/questions/physical-presence-requirement-faq).
- Existing money-management accounts get 30 days. Stripe notifies them and gives "a 30-day grace period," then disables those capabilities until a valid address is added [source](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/commercial-compliance/address-validation).
- The error says so plainly: "The address you provided appears to be associated with a mailbox or virtual address service, which we can't accept" [source](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/commercial-compliance/address-validation).
- To appeal, Stripe says to update to "a physical location where you operate," or, if the address really is your location, submit a proof of address document [source](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/commercial-compliance/address-validation). For business-address checks it accepts a signed lease, utility bills, federal or state tax returns, or Articles of Incorporation showing the business or owner's name [source](https://support.stripe.com/questions/verifying-your-business-address).

## Amazon seller registration
Amazon's registration guide asks for two different addresses [source](https://sell.amazon.com/sell/registration-guide):

- Registered business address: "Enter the address that appears on your business license." [source](https://sell.amazon.com/sell/registration-guide)
- Proof of residential address: a document "dated from the last 180 days, like a bank or credit card statement," uploaded with a government-issued ID, followed by a photo check or a video call where you bring the ID and proof of residential address [source](https://sell.amazon.com/sell/registration-guide).
A mailbox address isn't a residence, so it can't fill the second field. Whether it can be the first depends on what's on your business license, and an LLC's state filing often needs a street address for the registered office anyway; see virtual mailbox for an LLC. Amazon's guide says identity verification "usually takes three business days or less" [source](https://sell.amazon.com/sell/registration-guide).

## What the mailbox providers say

- US Global Mail: most banks and card issuers accept its address, but "some banks have recently started asking for a personal address, which is not a CMRA" address; customers then give a personal address and use the USGM address for mail [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022325-what-can-or-can-t-the-us-global-mail-address-be-used-for).
- PostScan Mail: its pricing page warns, "A mail center is not ideal for use with financial institutions and/or business registration" [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- Virtual Post Mail: its pricing page says "The mailbox address is not a physical address" and points to TruLease, a leased office address it calls "ideal for satisfying compliance requirements for bank accounts, Amazon Store, and more" [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/trulease/pricing/). Costs are on our VPM pricing page. Whether Stripe or Amazon accepts a particular leased address is their call, not VPM's.

## Where a virtual mailbox still fits

- Mailing address on your accounts and invoices. Keep the physical address in the verification field and route paper mail (1099s, notices, checks) to the mailbox.
- Formation and IRS mail. A mailbox can go on IRS Form SS-4's mailing address line [source](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iss4). See virtual mailbox for a bank account for which bank fields take a PMB.

## Links

- US Global Mail
- Virtual Post Mail (TruLease)
- Stable

# Virtual mailbox addresses and Google Business Profile
Short answer: No. Google's guidelines say "P.O. boxes or mailboxes located at remote locations aren't acceptable," and "If your business rents a physical mailing address but doesn't operate out of that location, also known as a virtual office, that location isn't eligible for a Business Profile" [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en). If you work from home or travel to customers, set up a service-area profile and hide your address instead [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481?hl=en).

A virtual mailbox gives you a street address, so it's tempting to put it on Google Maps. Google's own rules close that door, and even the mailbox companies warn against it. Here is what the Business Profile guidelines say, what to do instead, and where a mailbox still fits. Checked November 27, 2026.

## What Google's guidelines say

| Address type | Allowed on a Business Profile? | Google's wording |
| Virtual mailbox or PO Box | No | "P.O. boxes or mailboxes located at remote locations aren't acceptable" [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en) |
| Rented mailing address you don't work from ("virtual office") | No | "that location isn't eligible for a Business Profile" [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en) |
| Office at a co-working space | Only with conditions | Needs "clear signage," must receive customers during business hours, and must be "staffed during business hours by your business staff" [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en) |
| Virtual office for a service-area business | Only if staffed | "Service-area businesses can't list a 'virtual' office unless that office is staffed during business hours" [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en) |
| Your real location with a suite number | Yes | Put the physical address on line 1 and the mailbox or suite number on line 2 [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en) |

Google also says businesses that show an address "should maintain permanent fixed signage of their business name at the address" [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en). A mailbox number at a shipping store or mail-scanning facility doesn't meet that.

## The mailbox companies say the same
Anytime Mailbox's FAQ: "If you plan to use a digital mailbox for GoogleMaps, GoogleAdSense, or for a Google Business profile, it's best not to order one, as Google may not recognize the address as valid" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq).

## If you work from home or go to customers
Google's answer is a service-area business: "A business that visits or delivers to customers directly but doesn't serve customers at their business address," like cleaning services or plumbers [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481?hl=en).

- Hide your address. "If you're a service-area business, you should hide your business address from customers," for example a plumber working from home [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en). Google: "If you don't serve customers at your business address, remove your address from your Business Profile" [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481?hl=en).
- Set service areas by city or postal code, up to 20, and keep the overall area within about 2 hours' drive of your base [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481?hl=en).
- One profile only. Service-area businesses "can only have one profile for the whole area that they serve" [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481?hl=en).
- Age-restricted products need a storefront. Alcohol, cannabis and weapons businesses aren't allowed as service-area businesses without one [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/9157481?hl=en).

## Where a virtual mailbox still fits

- On your website, invoices and business mail, so your home address isn't printed everywhere. See how to write a virtual mailbox address.
- As your LLC's mailing address, separate from the registered office; see virtual mailbox for an LLC.
- If you need a staffed address, a virtual office with real reception is a different product from a mailbox. It still has to meet Google's staffing rule above. Compare them in virtual office vs virtual mailbox and Opus vs Davinci.
Google says it "determines how best to display your business address based on your business information and information from other sources" [source](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en). This page summarizes Google's published guidelines; Google makes the final call on each profile.

## Mailboxes for your business mail

- Traveling Mailbox
- US Global Mail
- Virtual Post Mail

# Monthly vs annual virtual mailbox billing
Short answer: A yearly plan usually costs about ten months' worth of the monthly price, so it pays off only if you keep the mailbox at least 10 or 11 months. Before you prepay, check the refund rule: US Global Mail gives no refund for unused time after 30 days [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11139298-is-there-a-refund-policy-for-unused-service), Stable gives none after 30 days from the first invoice [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/15963199-what-is-stable-s-cancellation-and-refund-policy), while Traveling Mailbox prorates annual refunds monthly [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/understanding-pro-rated-refund-policies-for-annual-subscriptions-what-you-need-to-know/).

Most providers advertise "2 months free" or a percentage off for paying a year up front. Here's the dollar saving at each provider that publishes both prices, how many months you need to stay to come out ahead, and what happens if you cancel early. Prices from each provider's own page, checked November 27, 2026.

## Yearly savings by provider

| Provider and plan | Monthly billing, 12 months | Annual billing | You save | Annual wins if you stay |
| iPostal1, 30 items [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $9.99 × 12 = $119.88 | $99.00 | $20.88 | 10+ months |
| iPostal1, 60 items [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $14.99 × 12 = $179.88 | $149.00 | $30.88 | 10+ months |
| US Global Mail Occasional [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | $25 × 12 = $300 | $21/mo = $252 | $48 | 11+ months |
| US Global Mail Scale [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | $65 × 12 = $780 | $49/mo = $588 | $192 | 10+ months |
| US Global Mail Teams [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | $129 × 12 = $1,548 | $99/mo = $1,188 | $360 | 10+ months |
| Stable Grow [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | $59 × 12 = $708 | $49/mo = $588 | $120 | 10+ months |
| Stable Scale [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | $99 × 12 = $1,188 | $83/mo = $996 | $192 | 11+ months |
| PostScan Mail Starter, lowest-priced address [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | $10 × 12 = $120 | $100 | $20 | 10+ months |
| PostScan Mail Standard, lowest-priced address [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | $20 × 12 = $240 | $200 | $40 | 10+ months |
| PostScan Mail Premium, lowest-priced address [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | $30 × 12 = $360 | $300 | $60 | 10+ months |
| Traveling Mailbox Basic [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | $15 × 12 = $180 | — | "2 months free" | — |
| PhysicalAddress.com Plan 30 [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) | From $7.98 × 12 = $95.76 | — | "20% Off Annual Plans" | — |
| Virtual Post Mail Starter [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) | $20 × 12 = $240 | — | — | — |

"Annual wins if you stay" is the first month at which the monthly bills add up to at least the annual price, e.g. 9 months of USGM Scale is $585 and 10 is $650, against $588 up front. iPostal1 prices are for Standard locations; Select, Premium and Prestige addresses cost more [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php). US Global Mail prices are marked "*varies by address" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle). PostScan's prices rise with the address tier, up to $45, $55 and $65 a month [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html). Traveling Mailbox and PhysicalAddress.com describe the annual discount but don't print an annual dollar price on their pricing pages; Virtual Post Mail lists monthly prices only.

## Annual plans that include more, not just less

- PostScan Mail gives annual plans more: Starter 2 recipients instead of 1, Standard 10 free open-and-scans and 3 recipients instead of 5 and 2, Premium 20 and 6 instead of 10 and 4 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html). Free letter storage goes from 14 to 30 days and free package storage from 3 to 7 days [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- Stable shows "Save 16%" on yearly billing [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing), and offers 50% off Grow for businesses under $1 million in annual revenue or those using a Stable address to incorporate [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing).

## If you cancel before the year is up

| Provider | First 30 days | After 30 days |
| US Global Mail | Full refund: "30-day money-back guarantee on all plans" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11139298-is-there-a-refund-policy-for-unused-service) | "We do not offer refunds for unused time." USGM itself suggests a monthly plan "if you're unsure about long-term needs" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11139298-is-there-a-refund-policy-for-unused-service) |
| Stable | Full refund within 30 days of your first invoice, base subscription and one seat only [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/15963199-what-is-stable-s-cancellation-and-refund-policy) | No refund; access continues to the end of the billing cycle [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/15963199-what-is-stable-s-cancellation-and-refund-policy) |
| Traveling Mailbox | — | Prorated refunds "handled on a monthly schedule"; contact support for the amount [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/understanding-pro-rated-refund-policies-for-annual-subscriptions-what-you-need-to-know/) |
| iPostal1 | "Full refund within first 30 days upon request, if account not used" [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Plans renew unless canceled before the billing date [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Virtual Post Mail | 30-day money-back guarantee [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) | — |

Traveling Mailbox is the one provider here that publishes a partial refund on annual plans after the first month, which makes its yearly plan the lowest-risk prepay. More on closing an account in how to cancel a virtual mailbox.

## Which to choose

- Start monthly if you're not sure of your mail volume. Traveling Mailbox, for one, lets you "Change Plans Anytime" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953), and a wrong-sized plan can cost more in overage fees than the annual discount saves. Size it first with the virtual mailbox chooser.
- Switch to annual after a month or two once you know the plan fits. USGM says you can "start off with the Monthly plan and upgrade at any time" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022328-what-payment-terms-do-you-have-for-all-the-different-plans).
- Prepay right away only if you're sure you'll keep the address for a year, for example an LLC address already on state filings. See virtual mailbox for an LLC.

- PostScan Mail

# Anytime Mailbox vs PostScan Mail
Short answer: They're built differently. Anytime Mailbox is a marketplace: each address is run by an independent mail center that sets its own plans and fees, so you compare location by location. PostScan Mail sells the same Starter, Standard and Premium plans everywhere, with one fee list, and only the base price changes by address. If you open few letters and find a cheap Anytime location with fair per-page scan fees, Anytime can cost less. If you want predictable fees, PostScan is easier to price in advance.

Both offer street addresses in hundreds of cities, envelope scans, forwarding and in-person pickup at most locations. Here's how the pricing compares, using Anytime Mailbox's location pages and FAQ and PostScan Mail's pricing page and FAQ, checked November 25, 2026.

## How each one prices

| | Anytime Mailbox | PostScan Mail |
| Who sets the price | The mail center operator at each address. Plans list what's included and the fees for extra actions before you sign up [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) | PostScan. Same three plans at every address; the price depends on the address's tier [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Starting price | "Our cheapest virtual mailbox plans are $4.99. On average, our plans cost $9.99 per month." Vanity addresses "can cost up to $50" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) | Starter "as low as" $10 to $45/mo, or $100 to $450/yr, by address [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Mail included on the entry plan | Varies: 15 or 30 items a month at the locations below, or none on "Just an Address" plans [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/austin-605-w-9th-street) | 30 items a month (letters or packages) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Opening and scanning | Set per location: $0.18 to $1.00 per page or item at the locations below, or a few pages a month included [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/austin-605-w-9th-street) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/astoria-2509-astoria-boulevard) | $2.00 per envelope for up to 10 pages, then $0.25 a page. Standard includes 5 free open-and-scans a month (10 on annual), Premium 10 (20 on annual) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Mail over your limit | Set per plan by the operator, shown under "Full Details" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) | $0.50 per extra envelope or package [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Junk mail | — | "Junk mail counts towards your account limit"; discarding it is free and unlimited [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Forwarding | Set per location: "No handling fees," $3.00 or $5.00 each, or $5.00 per shipping bundle at the locations below [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/washington-712-h-street-ne) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue) | $2.00 for the first item, then $0.50 per additional item, plus shipping [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Free storage | "Varies by location" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | Mail 14 days on monthly plans, 30 on annual; packages 3 days, or 7 on annual. Then $0.05 per envelope per day and $0.10 per pound per day [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Recipients | Set per plan: 1 to 5 on the entry plans below [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/washington-712-h-street-ne) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/astoria-2509-astoria-boulevard) | Starter 1 (2 on annual); Standard 2 (3); Premium 4 (6). Extra names $5/mo each, and each needs a Form 1583 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Check deposit | Offered at some locations (shown on each location page) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/washington-712-h-street-ne) | — |
| In-person pickup | "The majority" of mail centers allow pickup during business hours; check the location's Full Details [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | Free at most locations; some "may charge a nominal fee per pickup" [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Form 1583 | Online notary partner "for a nominal fee," or sign in person with your operator [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583) | Notarized, online or in person. Its online notary partners charge $20 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) |
| Refunds | Full refund within 30 days of sign-up only if the mailbox hasn't been used to receive mail [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | — |
| Extras | — | HIPAA option ($25/mo billed annually + $0.50 per item), AI mail summaries, developer API [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |

## Five Anytime Mailbox locations, side by side
Here is the cheapest plan at five locations, copied from each location page on November 25, 2026. Plan names don't mean the same thing everywhere.

| Location (operator) | Cheapest plan | Mail included | Open & scan | Forwarding | Recipients |

| Astoria, NY (Astorias Hub) | Bronze $9.99/mo or $109.99/yr | 15/mo | 10 pages/mo included | Unlimited | 5 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/astoria-2509-astoria-boulevard) |

For the starting price of every U.S. Anytime Mailbox location, see Anytime Mailbox pricing and every address, state by state.

## Worked example: 20 letters a month, 5 opened (3 pages each), one forwarded batch of 5

- PostScan Starter (cheapest tier): $10 + 5 × $2.00 opens + $2.00 + 4 × $0.50 forwarding = $24 plus shipping [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html)
- PostScan Standard (cheapest tier): $20, with the 5 opens included, + $4 forwarding = $24 plus shipping [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html)
- Anytime Mailbox, Omaha Bronze: $9.99 + 15 pages × $0.50 + one $5.00 bundle = $22.49 plus shipping [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue)
- Anytime Mailbox, Austin "Just an Address": 20 × $1.44 = $28.80 for receiving alone, on top of the $7.99 fee. At that volume, the same location's $12.99 "Address Pro" plan (60 items and 60 open-and-scans included, $4.95 per forward) is the better buy [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/austin-605-w-9th-street)
At PostScan, a higher-tier address raises every line above by the same plan-price difference (up to $35 a month more on Starter) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html). At Anytime Mailbox, the result depends entirely on the location you choose, so run your own numbers on two or three nearby ones.

## Leaving either service

- Anytime Mailbox: close the account under Settings. Mail that arrives afterward is stored by the operator for up to six months, "and storage fees may apply"; forwarding costs extra [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq).
- PostScan Mail: close it under Subscription & Billing. Stored mail is discarded, and mail received over the next 6 months is held, then returned to the sender [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).
Full provider-by-provider details: how to cancel a virtual mailbox.

- Anytime Mailbox
- PostScan Mail
