# Picking up mail in person from a virtual mailbox
Short answer: Only at some providers. Mailboxes run through local mail centers, like Anytime Mailbox, iPostal1 and PostScan Mail, usually let you collect mail during business hours, sometimes for a small fee. PhysicalAddress.com includes free local pickup at each of its company-run locations. US Global Mail allows scheduled pickups at most of its locations for a fee. Stable and Virtual Post Mail don't offer pickup at all, so you have them ship your mail instead.

USPS rules allow either approach: a CMRA (the postal term for a virtual mailbox company) "accepts delivery of the mail and holds it for pickup or remails it to the addressee" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Whether you can walk in depends on the company. Here's each provider's own policy, checked November 25, 2026.

## Pickup by provider

| Provider | In-person pickup? | Fee | How it works |
| US Global Mail | At most locations, but not Concord CA, Las Vegas NV, Long Island City NY or Wilmington DE [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11322218-can-i-pick-up-my-mail-or-packages-in-person) | Letters $5 flat; packages $15 for the first pound + $1 per additional pound; expedited pickup (1 PM to 3 PM, where offered) +$5; $5 no-show fee [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11322218-can-i-pick-up-my-mail-or-packages-in-person) | Schedule in advance by choosing "Pickup at Warehouse" as the shipping option. Hours vary by location. Photo ID required, and items not collected within 5 days go back to your inbox [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11322218-can-i-pick-up-my-mail-or-packages-in-person) |
| iPostal1 | Yes, during business hours [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | "Some locations charge a small fee" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | Schedule in the app. Someone else can collect if you add them to your account [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) |
| Anytime Mailbox | "The majority" of mail centers allow it during business hours [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | Set by each operator, shown under "Full Details" on each plan [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | Schedule a pickup in your account where available [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq). All five locations we checked list Local Pickup [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/austin-605-w-9th-street) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/washington-712-h-street-ne) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/astoria-2509-astoria-boulevard) |
| PostScan Mail | At most locations [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | Free at most locations; some "may charge a nominal fee per pickup" [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | — |
| PhysicalAddress.com | Yes, at any of its locations [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/can-i-pickup-my-mail/) | Free [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/can-i-pickup-my-mail/) | In your account, select the items, click Local Pickup, and say who will collect and when [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/can-i-pickup-my-mail/) |
| Stable | No: "In-person pickup is not available from your Stable address" [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8236324-can-i-pick-up-my-mail-in-person) | n/a | Forward instead; Stable recommends FedEx and supports overnight shipping [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8236324-can-i-pick-up-my-mail-in-person) |
| Virtual Post Mail | No. Its locations "are not open to the public" [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/252-pick-up-my-mail-at-location) | n/a | Create a shipping request. If you're nearby, it says mail normally arrives in 1 business day [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/252-pick-up-my-mail-at-location) |

Traveling Mailbox's pricing and Form 1583 pages describe scanning, forwarding and storage but don't mention in-person pickup [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953).

## Why some charge for pickup
iPostal1 explains it: "Since digital mailboxes are not self-service like physical mailboxes, some mail centers charge a nominal fee for processing and retrieving your mail when you come in to pick it up" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php). Staff have to find your items and hand them over, unlike a PO Box you open with a key.

## What it costs: one visit at US Global Mail

- A stack of letters: $5 flat [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11322218-can-i-pick-up-my-mail-or-packages-in-person).
- A 4 lb package: $15 + 3 × $1 = $18 [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11322218-can-i-pick-up-my-mail-or-packages-in-person).
For comparison, having letters shipped costs postage plus a handling fee at most providers. See mail forwarding fees compared.

## Picking a mailbox for pickup

- Choose a location you can reach during its business hours. Pickup happens at the specific address you sign up for [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq).
- Check the location's pickup fee before signing up. At Anytime Mailbox it's in each plan's Full Details; at iPostal1, on the locations page [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
- Bring photo ID, and if someone else is collecting, add them to the account or notify the provider first [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11322218-can-i-pick-up-my-mail-or-packages-in-person) [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
- Watch the storage clock. Mail you plan to collect still counts against the free storage period; see how long mail is kept.
If you only want a place to collect mail locally and don't need scans, compare a USPS PO Box: virtual mailbox vs PO Box.

# How long virtual mailboxes keep your mail
A virtual mailbox stores the paper original of each letter and package for a set number of days. After that, it either starts charging storage or shreds the item. The scans stay online much longer. Here are the free periods and the fees after them, from each provider's own pages on November 23, 2026, with PhysicalAddress.com added on November 25, 2026.

## Letters

| Provider | Free storage | After the free period |
| US Global Mail | 30 days (Scale), 60 days (Teams) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11328326-why-do-i-have-storage-fees-on-my-invoice) | $0.05 per letter per day [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11328326-why-do-i-have-storage-fees-on-my-invoice) |
| Traveling Mailbox | 30 days [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | Shredded on site unless you put it on hold: $1 per envelope per month [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| PostScan Mail | 14 days on monthly plans, 30 days on annual plans [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | $0.05 per envelope per day [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| iPostal1 | 30 days [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $1.10 per item per month [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| LegalZoom Virtual Mail (Earth Class Mail) | 30 days [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) | $1.50 per month [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Stable | 30 days [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Securely disposed of [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| Virtual Post Mail | 30 days, all plans [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) | — |
| Anytime Mailbox | Varies by location [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | Varies by location |
| PhysicalAddress.com | 90 days for non-parcel mail (envelopes, magazines and postcards) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/what-is-long-term-storage/) | $0.25 (Plan 30), $0.20 (Plan 50), $0.15 (Plan 100) or $0.10 (Plan 200) per item per month [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) |

PostScan Mail's FAQ gives 30 free days for mail without mentioning the plan type [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html); its pricing page says 14 days, or 30 with an annual plan [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).

## Packages

| Provider | Free storage | After the free period |
| US Global Mail | 30 days (Scale), 60 days (Teams) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11328326-why-do-i-have-storage-fees-on-my-invoice) | $0.10 per package per day; from January 1, 2027, $0.10 per lb per day (under 1 lb counts as 1 lb) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11328326-why-do-i-have-storage-fees-on-my-invoice) |
| Traveling Mailbox | 30 days [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | $0.10 per lb per day [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| PostScan Mail | 3 days on monthly plans, 7 days on annual plans [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | $0.10 per lb per day [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| iPostal1 | 30 days under 12×12×12 in.; 10 days up to 24×17×12 in.; 5 days larger [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $1.10 per lb per month, per 10 days or per 5 days by size (greater of actual or dimensional weight) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| LegalZoom Virtual Mail | 10 days [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) | $15 per lb per month [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Stable | 15 days [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Disposed of [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| Virtual Post Mail | 15 days (Starter, Plus, Business), 30 days (Premium) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) | — |
| Anytime Mailbox | Varies by location [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | Varies by location |
| PhysicalAddress.com | 1 week [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) | $1 per week [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) |

## What a forgotten box costs
A 5 lb package left 30 days past its free period:

- Traveling Mailbox or PostScan Mail: 5 lb × $0.10 × 30 days = $15 [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- US Global Mail: $0.10 × 30 days = $3 today; from January 1, 2027, 5 lb × $0.10 × 30 = $15 [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11328326-why-do-i-have-storage-fees-on-my-invoice).
- LegalZoom Virtual Mail: 5 lb × $15 = $75 for the month [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html).
- iPostal1 (small box, monthly rate): 5 lb × $1.10 = $5.50 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
- PhysicalAddress.com: $1 a week after the first free week, so 30 extra days is $4, and the fee is not by weight [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/).
For letters, the difference is smaller but adds up if you keep originals: 20 letters held one extra month cost $20 at Traveling Mailbox ($1 each) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953), $22 at iPostal1 ($1.10 each) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php), and about $30 at US Global Mail or PostScan Mail ($0.05 × 20 × 30 days) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11328326-why-do-i-have-storage-fees-on-my-invoice) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).

## Scans last longer than paper

- US Global Mail: scans kept 180 days on Scale, unlimited on Teams [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle).
- Traveling Mailbox: scans stay "until you delete them" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- Stable, LegalZoom, iPostal1, Virtual Post Mail, PhysicalAddress.com: unlimited digital storage [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-much-online-storage-does-physicaladdress-com-provide/)
- Anytime Mailbox: scans are available "as long as your account remains active" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq).

## When you cancel
USPS rules require a commercial mail receiving agency (the legal category for virtual mailboxes) to keep remailing mail for at least 6 months after your service ends, to the address on your Form 1583, with new postage. Neither you nor the provider files a USPS change-of-address order, and you can tell the provider in writing not to remail [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). In practice:

- PostScan Mail discards any stored mail when you close the account and holds newly received mail for 6 months, then returns it to the sender [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).
- So before canceling, forward or download anything you want to keep, and update your address with senders. Every provider's policy is in how to cancel a virtual mailbox. More in living abroad and full-time RVers.

## Avoiding storage fees

- Shred or recycle what you've read: shredding is free at Traveling Mailbox, US Global Mail, LegalZoom and PhysicalAddress.com [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/); PostScan Mail charges $1.00 per item for up to 10 pages [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- Batch your forwarding before the free period runs out; see mail forwarding fees compared.
- If you get a lot of packages, the free package period (3 to 60 days above) matters more than the plan price.

- US Global Mail
- Virtual Post Mail
- Traveling Mailbox
- iPostal1
- PostScan Mail

# How to cancel a virtual mailbox
Short answer: Update your senders first, because you can't file a USPS change of address away from a virtual mailbox. Download the scans you want to keep and forward or shred the paper you still have stored. Then cancel from your account before the renewal date. Mail will keep arriving for months. Depending on the provider, it gets held, forwarded for a fee, shredded or returned to the sender.

Closing a virtual mailbox is easy. Getting your mail to follow you is the hard part. Below are the USPS rule behind that and each provider's own cancellation policy, checked November 25, 2026.

## The USPS rule: no change of address, 6 months of mail

- When you leave a commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA, the USPS term for a virtual mailbox company), "neither the addressee nor the CMRA will file a change-of-address order with the Post Office" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).
- The CMRA "must remail mail intended for the addressee (customer) for at least 6 months after the termination date," with new postage, to the remail address on your Form 1583 [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).
- That obligation doesn't apply if you give the CMRA written instructions not to remail, and those instructions can be in its service agreement [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Many providers' terms do exactly that, which is why policies differ below.
- A CMRA may not refuse mail for a former customer within the past 6 months. After the 6 months, it returns First-Class Mail, Priority Mail and similar classes to the Post Office endorsed "Undeliverable, Commercial Mail Receiving Agency, No Authorization to Receive Mail for this Addressee" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).
If you filed a USPS change of address to the mailbox when you signed up, that's a separate request. A temporary one ends on its own date, and you can cancel or edit it with the confirmation code USPS sent you [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022359-how-do-i-close-my-usgm-mailbox) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/account-closure-reactivation?ref=3953). More on that in changing your address to a virtual mailbox.

## Provider by provider

| Provider | How to cancel | Mail already stored | Mail that arrives after you close | Coming back |
| US Global Mail | Settings › Subscriptions & Billing › Plan & Billing Details › Cancel Subscription. Pending invoices must be paid first; closure takes effect immediately [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022359-how-do-i-close-my-usgm-mailbox) | Handle every item first: scan, ship, shred or return to sender [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022359-how-do-i-close-my-usgm-mailbox) | Shredded, "No exceptions," unless you pick the Wind-down Plan offered when you close. Its terms let you prepay postage, packaging and forwarding fees to have mail remailed for up to 6 months [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022359-how-do-i-close-my-usgm-mailbox) [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/terms-of-service) | Reactivate within 6 months of closing; after that you need a new account and address [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11322035-can-i-pause-my-account) |
| Virtual Post Mail | Contact support to close. Service runs to the end of the billing cycle, then your login is disabled and leftover credits are refunded [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/70-cancel-account) | Shredded unless you ask for something else, such as packing and forwarding it. The shipping fee comes out of your credit balance [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/70-cancel-account) [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/71-mail-after-cancel) | "Rejected and returned to the sender." Its terms say it won't remail after termination [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/71-mail-after-cancel) [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/182-re-mail-for-closed-box) | It can hold your mailbox number for up to 6 months if you ask when canceling (conditions apply) [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/73-account-on-hold) |
| Traveling Mailbox | On the website (not the app): Billing › Subscriptions › cancel [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/account-closure-reactivation?ref=3953) | Arrange forwarding before you close [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/account-closure-reactivation?ref=3953) | Received for up to six months; you can sign in and request forwarding, with shipping and handling charges [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/account-closure-reactivation?ref=3953) | Reactivate your old account within one year [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/account-closure-reactivation?ref=3953) |
| iPostal1 | Mailbox Settings › Cancel Mailbox, before the next billing date. No cancellation fee [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | — | — | — |
| Anytime Mailbox | Settings › Close account [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | — | Stored by the local operator for up to six months, "and storage fees may apply." Forwarding costs extra [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) | — |
| PostScan Mail | Settings › Subscription & Billing › Close Account [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) | Discarded [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) | Held 6 months. After that, held mail is discarded and new mail goes back to the sender [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) | — |
| Stable | Billing › Cancel subscription. A registered agent service must be canceled separately [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/15963199-what-is-stable-s-cancellation-and-refund-policy) | — | You get an email with a photo of the envelope front, but Stable won't scan or forward it unless you reactivate [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8292017-how-can-i-cancel-my-stable-account) [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/15963199-what-is-stable-s-cancellation-and-refund-policy) | Reactivate through support and keep your mailbox number; mail received meanwhile becomes available again [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/15963199-what-is-stable-s-cancellation-and-refund-policy) |
| PhysicalAddress.com | Call (844) 888-6364, email support@physicaladdress.com, or open a support ticket in your account. Give your name, address and suite number [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/cancelling-your-account/) | — | If Form 1583 was completed, it keeps accepting mail for 6 months and scans and uploads each piece for free; "forwarding requests will incur additional fees" [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/cancelling-your-account/) | — |
| Earth Class Mail (LegalZoom Virtual Mail) | Two options: close at the end of the billing cycle (no fee), or keep 6 months of account access for a $50 cancellation fee [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034846614-Cancellation-FAQ-s) | Shredded when the account closes [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034846614-Cancellation-FAQ-s) | Closed now: shredded for 6 months, then returned to the sender. With 6 months' access: you can manage it, paying $3 per received item, and $5 per domestic shipment plus postage and $1 per item ($10 international) [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034846614-Cancellation-FAQ-s) | Reopen within 3 months for a $99 reactivation fee [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034846614-Cancellation-FAQ-s) |

## Refunds when you cancel

- US Global Mail: 30-day money-back guarantee; after 30 days, no refund for unused time [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11139298-is-there-a-refund-policy-for-unused-service).
- PhysicalAddress.com: 30-day money-back guarantee [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/).
- Stable: 30-day money-back guarantee on your first invoice only. Add-ons like check deposits and mail forwarding aren't covered [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/15963199-what-is-stable-s-cancellation-and-refund-policy).
- iPostal1: prepaid yearly plans are non-refundable after the first 30 days, and unused scan or shred bundles are non-refundable [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
- Anytime Mailbox: a full refund only within 30 days of sign-up and only if the mailbox was never used to receive mail [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq).
- Traveling Mailbox: annual plans are "refundable on a monthly schedule" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- Virtual Post Mail: remaining account credits are refunded [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/70-cancel-account).

## Checklist before you close

- Get the new address working first. Traveling Mailbox suggests waiting until mail is actually arriving at the new place [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/account-closure-reactivation?ref=3953).
- Tell senders directly, starting with banks, the IRS and state agencies. The IRS uses Form 8822 for individuals and 8822-B for businesses [source](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-8822) [source](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-8822-b). Virtual Post Mail recommends starting at least a month before you close [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/182-re-mail-for-closed-box).
- Cancel any USPS forwarding that points to the mailbox, as Stable recommends [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/15963199-what-is-stable-s-cancellation-and-refund-policy).
- Download your scans. At Virtual Post Mail you can't log in after termination [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/70-cancel-account).
- Forward or shred the paper you still have there. PostScan discards it and US Global Mail asks you to handle every item first [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022359-how-do-i-close-my-usgm-mailbox).
- Cancel before the renewal date. US Global Mail and iPostal1 renew automatically [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022359-how-do-i-close-my-usgm-mailbox) [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
- If you need late mail, choose a provider option that covers it: US Global Mail's Wind-down Plan, Earth Class Mail's 6-month access, or Traveling Mailbox's six months of residual-mail forwarding [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022359-how-do-i-close-my-usgm-mailbox) [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034846614-Cancellation-FAQ-s) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/account-closure-reactivation?ref=3953).

## Links

- PhysicalAddress.com
- US Global Mail
- Virtual Post Mail

# How to write a virtual mailbox address
Short answer: Put "PMB" (or "#") and your box number either on its own line above the street or at the end of the street line: 10 MAIN ST PMB 234. If the building's address already has a suite number, keep it and add PMB after it, 10 MAIN ST STE 11 PMB 234, and never merge the two into "STE 11-234." For a USPS change of address, use PMB.

Every virtual mailbox is a commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA) under USPS rules, and USPS has specific addressing rules for them. Here's what the Domestic Mail Manual and Publication 28 (Postal Addressing Standards) say, and how providers present their addresses, checked November 25, 2026.

## What USPS requires

- "A CMRA must represent its delivery address designation for the intended addressees by the use of 'PMB' (private mailbox) or the alternative '#' sign" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).
- Publication 28 goes further: mail to a CMRA customer "must include either the PMB identifier or the #, followed by the appropriate private mailbox number. Use of any other identifier is prohibited" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/pub28/pub28c2_040.htm).
- "POST OFFICE BOX" or "PO BOX" can't be used with your private mailbox number on the delivery line. "Only the Postal Service is entitled to provide delivery to a PO Box" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/pub28/pub28c2_040.htm).
- Mail without a proper address can be returned to the sender endorsed "Undeliverable as Addressed, Missing PMB or # Sign" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).

## The two correct formats

| Four-line format (preferred) | Three-line format (alternate) |
| JOE DOE
PMB 234
10 MAIN ST
HERNDON VA 22071-2716 | JOE DOE
10 MAIN ST PMB 234
HERNDON VA 22071-2716 |

Both formats and the examples are from DMM 508.1.8, which lists the four-line layout as the preferred format and the three-line layout as the alternate. "#234" works in place of "PMB 234" in either [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Publication 28 adds that when "#" is used as a unit designator, there must be a space between it and the number, and notes that the pound sign "might be prohibited" with some CMRA addresses that carry PMB information [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/pub28/28c2_003.htm).

## When the building already has a suite number
Many mail centers sit in a suite of a larger building. In that case, "the CMRA customer must use 'PMB' in the three-line format," and "it is not permissible to combine the secondary address element of the physical location of the CMRA address and the CMRA customer private mailbox number, e.g., 10 MAIN ST STE 11-234" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).

| Write it like this | Not like this |
| 10 MAIN ST STE 11 PMB 234 | 10 MAIN ST STE 11-234 |
| 10 MAIN ST STE 11 PMB 234 | 10 MAIN ST STE 11 # 234 (in the three-line format, the rule calls for PMB) |
| RR 12 BOX 512 PMB 234 | RR 12 BOX 512-234 |

Examples follow DMM 508.1.8, which gives 10 MAIN ST STE 11 PMB 234 and RR 12 BOX 512 PMB 234 as the required three-line forms [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).

## Why your provider's address may say "Suite" or "Unit"
Provider pages don't all follow the USPS wording:

- US Global Mail lists its addresses with "Suite ####" (for example "1321 Upland Dr. Suite ####, Houston, TX 77043") and says you can replace PMB with Suite, Apt. or Unit "when sharing your address, except when changing the address with USPS" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022324-what-will-my-virtual-address-be). For the USPS change-of-address form, it says the only accepted format is "Street Address PMB NNNN," with no # signs, periods or commas [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022326-why-does-usps-s-website-say-your-address-is-invalid).
- iPostal1 says the box number "will most often appear on the same line as the street address" and that "some locations are suite addresses," with samples like "123 Main Street #1001" and "400 Rella Blvd. Suite 123" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
- Anytime Mailbox location pages show the box line as "Unit # MAILBOX" (Omaha, Austin) or "Ste 1 # MAILBOX" (Astoria, NY) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/astoria-2509-astoria-boulevard).
Mail addressed with "Suite" often still arrives, because the mail center sorts it. But Publication 28 says any identifier other than PMB or # "is prohibited" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/pub28/pub28c2_040.htm), and USPS can return mail that's missing the PMB or # [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Using "Suite" also doesn't make the address something other than a CMRA, as our bank account page explains.

## Where to use which format

- USPS change of address: PMB, in the exact format your provider gives for USPS [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022326-why-does-usps-s-website-say-your-address-is-invalid) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11322295-how-do-i-notify-senders-about-my-new-address).
- Your Form 1583: the CMRA "must write the complete CMRA delivery address" for each addressee on the form [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Use the same address everywhere else.
- Senders, banks and government forms: the USPS format with PMB or # is always correct for delivery. Whether a bank or state agency accepts a mailbox address at all is a separate question; see bank accounts and LLC filings.
- Every piece of mail should carry a name on your account plus the box number. US Global Mail says an item without them becomes a "Lookup Item," delayed while staff match it, and may be returned to the sender if several customers share that name [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022364-how-do-i-start-getting-mail-at-my-usgm-address).

## Links

- US Global Mail
- Virtual Post Mail

# iPostal1 vs Traveling Mailbox
Short answer: iPostal1 is cheaper if you mostly look at envelope images and open only a letter or two a month. Traveling Mailbox is cheaper once you open more than about two letters a month, because its $15 Basic plan includes 35 page scans, while iPostal1 charges $2.25 for each letter it opens. iPostal1 also has far more addresses to pick from and lets you collect mail in person. Traveling Mailbox skips the notary for Form 1583.

Both give you a street address, show you a picture of every envelope, and scan or forward on request. They charge for it in opposite ways: iPostal1 has a low monthly fee plus pay-per-use scans, and Traveling Mailbox has a higher fee with scans included. Here's the comparison from both companies' own pages, checked November 25, 2026.

## Fee by fee

| | iPostal1 (personal plans) | Traveling Mailbox |
| Entry plan | $9.99/mo or $99/yr for 30 mail items a month [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Basic: $15/mo for 40 envelopes and 35 page scans a month [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Higher plans | 60 items $14.99 · 120 items $24.99 · 240 items $39.99 a month [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Extended $25 (100 envelopes, 80 page scans) · Small Business $55 (200 envelopes, 180 page scans) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Address price differences | About 90% of locations are Standard. Select, Premium and Prestige addresses cost +$10, +$20 or +$30 [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | One price list. Most customers use the Sanford, NC address [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Yearly billing | Pay 10 months, get 12: $99/yr on the entry plan. Prepaid yearly plans are non-refundable after the first 30 days [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | "2 months free" on annual plans, which are "refundable on a monthly schedule" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Envelope images | Included for every item [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Included. Envelope scans don't use up page scans [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Opening and scanning a letter | $2.25 per envelope for up to 10 pages, then $0.25 a page. Prepaid bundles: $10 for 5, $18 for 10, $30 for 20 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Included up to your page-scan allowance (35 a month on Basic) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Over the limit | $0.35 per mail item over your plan [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $0.25 per extra envelope, $0.50 per extra page scan [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Junk mail | — | Mark it as junk and it doesn't count toward your limits [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Names on the mailbox | Up to 6 recipient names, but no company name on personal plans. Business plans start at $14.99 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | 3 recipients on Basic, 5 on Extended, 10 on Small Business. Business names can be added to any plan [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Forwarding | Real-time shipping price for the carrier you choose. Consolidating letters is free; $1.95 per package or letter-pack consolidated [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Postage + $2 per shipment, not per item. Consolidation is free [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Free physical storage | 30 days for mail and packages under 12×12×12 in.; 10 days for medium packages; 5 days for large ones [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Envelopes 30 days, then shredded unless you put them on hold. Packages 30 days [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Storage after that | Letters $1.10 per item per month; packages $1.10 per pound per 30, 10 or 5 days by size [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $1 per envelope per month to hold; packages $0.10 per pound per day [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Scan storage | Unlimited cloud storage [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Unlimited cloud storage [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Check deposit | $4.95 for up to 5 checks, plus check scans and trackable shipping (most locations) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $4.95 per check + postage [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Form 1583 | Notarized. Online notary $25, or sign in person at many mail centers, some for a small fee. Customers living outside the U.S. must use the online notary [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | No notary needed: a video call with staff verifies your ID and e-signs the form [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953) |
| In-person pickup | Yes, during business hours. Some locations charge a small fee [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | — |
| Discounts | — | 10% monthly discount for active-duty military and veterans [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |

iPostal1 business plans (which add one company name) cost $5 a month more at each tier, $14.99 to $44.99 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php); see iPostal1 pricing explained. Traveling Mailbox's plan cards say scans roll over on every plan, while its footnote says only Extended and higher roll over [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).

## Worked examples (Standard iPostal1 address, monthly billing)

### Light use: 15 letters a month, 2 opened, nothing forwarded

- iPostal1: $9.99 + 2 × $2.25 = $14.49 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php)
- Traveling Mailbox Basic: $15, since 15 envelopes and a few pages fit in 40 / 35 [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953)

### Typical household: 25 letters, 10 opened (3 pages each), one forwarded batch

- iPostal1: $9.99 + 10 × $2.25 = $32.49 plus shipping. With a prepaid 10-order bundle ($18), it's $27.99 plus shipping [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php)
- Traveling Mailbox Basic: $15 + $2 for the shipment = $17 plus postage. 25 envelopes and 30 pages fit inside 40 / 35 [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953)
The break-even is low: at Standard addresses, three opened letters a month ($9.99 + 3 × $2.25 = $16.74) already cost more than Traveling Mailbox's $15. If you want a Select, Premium or Prestige iPostal1 address, add the surcharge before you compare [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).

## Pick iPostal1 if

- You want a specific city or neighborhood. iPostal1 lists 4,250+ addresses [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
- You mostly need to see who wrote and rarely need letters opened.
- You live near the mail center and want to collect mail in person [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
- You receive several checks at once: $4.95 covers up to 5 checks in one deposit, plus scans and shipping [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).

## Pick Traveling Mailbox if

- You read most of your mail as PDFs. 35 page scans a month are included on Basic [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- You get a lot of junk mail. Marked junk doesn't count toward your limits [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- You'd rather skip the notary. Traveling Mailbox handles Form 1583 by video call [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953).
- You want a business name without changing plans [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).

- iPostal1
- Traveling Mailbox

# PhysicalAddress.com pricing
Short answer: The cheapest published plan is Plan 30 at $7.98 a month, with 30 envelope scans and 10 content scans. Additional scans are $0.20. Starting prices are higher in some cities: Las Vegas is $8.98, several others are $9.98, Laguna Beach is $10.98 and the Wall Street address is $19.98. Annual billing is advertised at 20% off, but the pricing page does not list the annual dollar amounts. [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/locations/)

PhysicalAddress.com runs its own mail locations instead of using third-party mail centers, and it says mail is scanned on site the same business day [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/where-is-my-mail-processed-do-you-forward-my-mail-to-another-location-to-have-it-processed/). Every figure below is from its own pages, checked November 25, 2026.

## The plans on the pricing page

| Plan | Monthly price | Envelope scans / month | Content scans / month | Letter storage after 90 days | Also included |
| Plan 30 | $7.98 | 30 | 10 | $0.25 per item per month | Unlimited recipients; free local pickup, registered agent and shredding |
| Plan 50 | $10.98 | 50 | 25 | $0.20 per item per month | The Plan 30 extras, plus multi-user admin |
| Plan 100 | $16.98 | 100 | 50 | $0.15 per item per month | The Plan 50 extras, plus suite numbers ending in 0 |
| Plan 200 | $26.98 | 200 | 100 | $0.10 per item per month | The Plan 100 extras |

Source: PhysicalAddress.com pricing page [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/). Content scans are "pages inside envelopes or packages that you request to be scanned." After you reach the plan limit in envelope or content scans, additional scans are $0.20. Every plan includes 90 days of free storage for non-parcel mail (envelopes, magazines and postcards), one week of free package storage, then $1 a week, and unlimited free storage for scanned (digital) mail [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-much-online-storage-does-physicaladdress-com-provide/). The page advertises "20% Off Annual Plans" without listing the resulting prices. You can change plans at any time [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/can-i-change-plans/).
The same pricing page says "there are six plans to choose from" and that Plan 600 includes 600 monthly envelope scans, and a help article mentions switching to a Plan 300, but neither page publishes prices for those plans [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/can-i-change-plans/). For more than 300 mail items a month, it tells you to call (844) 888-6364 for a custom plan [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/do-you-have-high-volume-corporate-plans-available/).

## Starting price by location
The locations page lists a monthly starting price at each of the eight company-run addresses [source](https://physicaladdress.com/locations/):

| Location | Address as published | Starting monthly price |
| Boise / Garden City, ID | 9169 W State St, Garden City, ID 83714. You can address mail to Boise or Garden City; they share a ZIP code [source](https://physicaladdress.com/locations/) | $7.98 |
| Las Vegas, NV | 304 S Jones Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89107 | $8.98 |
| Wilmington, DE | 1207 Delaware Ave, Wilmington, DE 19806 | $9.98 |
| Atlanta, GA | 1445 Woodmont Ln NW, Atlanta, GA 30318 | $9.98 |
| Dallas, TX | 539 W Commerce St, Dallas, TX 75208 | $9.98 |
| Orlando, FL | 1317 Edgewater Dr, Orlando, FL 32804 | $9.98 |
| Laguna Beach, CA | 1968 S Coast Hwy, Laguna Beach, CA 92651 | $10.98 |
| Wall Street, New York, NY | 99 Wall Street, New York, NY 10005 | $19.98 |

The $7.98 Plan 30 price on the pricing page matches the Boise starting price. The locations page does not break out Plan 50, 100 or 200 prices in each city, so those are not shown here. Every location card also lists a 30-day money-back guarantee, free local pickup, a free registered agent, unlimited shredding, multi-user plans, suite numbers ending in 0 on some plans, and phone support 7 days a week (Monday–Friday 6 AM–7 PM, Saturday 8 AM–3 PM, Sunday 10 AM–2 PM Pacific) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/locations/).

## Other fees

| Item | What PhysicalAddress.com publishes |
| Additional envelope or content scans | $0.20 after the plan limit [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) |
| Opening mail | Only if you click Scan; it will not open mail or packages automatically [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/will-physicaladdress-com-open-and-scan-my-mail-automatically/) |
| Mail and package forwarding | USPS, FedEx, UPS or DHL at "competitive commercial prices"; no separate handling fee is listed [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/what-are-my-options-for-forwarding-mail-and-packages/) |
| Check deposit | No check-handling fee; you pay the forwarding postage. It generates a deposit slip and mails the check to your bank [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-does-your-check-deposit-service-work/) |
| Local pickup | Free. Schedule it in your account and say who will collect and when [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/can-i-pickup-my-mail/) |
| Registered agent | "Free Registered Agent Service with Account" [source](https://physicaladdress.com/registered-agent-service/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) |
| Shredding | Free [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) |
| Sign-up fee / contract | No sign-up fees; no contract; cancel anytime [source](https://physicaladdress.com/) |
| Recipients | Unlimited on every published plan [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) |

## Form 1583
You can start using the address right away, but PhysicalAddress.com cannot scan, forward or upload mail until USPS Form 1583 is completed [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/what-is-the-usps-1583/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-do-i-sign-up-for-physicaladdress-com/). After you sign up, it emails a pre-filled form and a link to a partner online notary that "supports international clients." You can also sign with a notary or at one of its locations. It does not publish the online notary's fee [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-do-i-sign-up-for-physicaladdress-com/).

## A 30-letter example
If you receive 30 letters a month and open 10 of them, Plan 30's allowance (30 envelope scans and 10 content scans) covers that volume, so the monthly plan price is $7.98 at the Boise rate published on the pricing page, before any forwarding [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/). The same mail volume on Traveling Mailbox Basic is $15, and on PostScan Mail Starter it is from $10 plus $2.00 for each of the 10 open-and-scans [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html). In New York the published starting price is $19.98, which already costs more than Traveling Mailbox Basic before scans are counted [source](https://physicaladdress.com/locations/).

## Canceling
Cancel by phone at (844) 888-6364, by emailing support@physicaladdress.com, or by opening a support ticket in your account. If Form 1583 was completed, it will keep accepting mail for 6 months after you cancel and will scan and upload each piece for free; forwarding in that period "will incur additional fees." There is a 30-day money-back guarantee [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/cancelling-your-account/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/).
Go to PhysicalAddress.com.

# The cheapest virtual mailbox
Short answer: Anytime Mailbox advertises the lowest price, from $4.99 a month, but each location sets its own plans. PhysicalAddress.com Plan 30 starts at $7.98, PostScan Mail at $8.33 a month billed yearly, and iPostal1 at $9.99. If you open several letters a month, PhysicalAddress.com Plan 30 includes 10 content scans, and Traveling Mailbox Basic ($15 with 35 page scans and no notary) can still cost less overall once you outgrow those allowances. [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) [source](https://ipostal1.com/) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953)

The lowest advertised price is Anytime Mailbox: "Our cheapest virtual mailbox plans are $4.99" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/). But the cheapest plan only stays cheapest if you rarely open mail. Prices below were checked on November 19, 2026, with PhysicalAddress.com added from its own pages on November 25, 2026.
Want your own number? The virtual mailbox chooser works out a monthly cost for your mail volume, scans and checks.

## Lowest advertised prices

| Rank | Provider | Lowest advertised price | The catch |
| 1 | Anytime Mailbox | $4.99; "on average, our plans cost $9.99 per month" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) | Each location sets its own plans and fees, so the $4.99 address may not be in your city [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) |
| 2 | PhysicalAddress.com | Plan 30 $7.98/mo [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) | The $7.98 price matches its Boise location. Other cities start higher (Las Vegas $8.98, several $9.98, Laguna Beach $10.98, Wall Street $19.98). Plan 30 includes 10 content scans; additional scans are $0.20. Form 1583 needs a notary or an in-person signing; the online notary fee is not published [source](https://physicaladdress.com/locations/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-do-i-sign-up-for-physicaladdress-com/) |
| 3 | PostScan Mail | $8.33/mo Starter, billed annually; "as low as $10/mo" monthly [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | No free open-and-scans on Starter. Each one is $2.00 for up to 10 pages, and junk mail counts toward your 30-item limit [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) |
| 4 | iPostal1 | From $9.99/mo (Virtual Mailing Address) [source](https://ipostal1.com/) | Plan allowances vary by location. The online notary for Form 1583 is $25 unless your mail center lets you sign in person [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) |
| 5 | Traveling Mailbox | $15/mo Basic [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | Highest sticker price of these five, but 35 page scans a month are included, and Form 1583 needs no notary [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-do-i-complete-the-usps-form-1583/) |

## Cheapest for your situation

### You just need an address
An Anytime Mailbox or iPostal1 location is often cheapest when you mostly recycle mail and only look at envelope images. PhysicalAddress.com Plan 30 at $7.98 is in the same range if you want one of its eight company-run addresses [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/).

### You open 5+ letters a month
PhysicalAddress.com Plan 30 includes 10 content scans in the $7.98 price [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/). Traveling Mailbox Basic includes 35 page scans for $15 [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953). At PostScan, five open-and-scans on Starter add $10 to the bill [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).

### You want to skip the notary
Traveling Mailbox, Stable and US Global Mail handle Form 1583 without a notary [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-do-i-complete-the-usps-form-1583/) [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8236356-why-are-my-ids-being-verified-for-the-usps-1583) [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/usps-form-1583/?via=michelle). That saves the $20–$25 online notary fee charged elsewhere [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).

## How much does Form 1583 add to the cost?
Some providers require a notarized USPS Form 1583 before they'll handle your mail. iPostal1's online notary costs $25 [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) and PostScan's partner notary costs $20 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html). Over a year on a $9.99 plan, a $25 notary fee adds about 20%. See Form 1583 and online notarization.

# Virtual mailbox check deposit fees, compared
If customers or clients still mail you paper checks, the deposit fee can cost more than the mailbox itself. Usually the provider endorses the check and mails it to your bank, and you pay a handling fee plus postage. Here's what each provider publishes, as of November 20, 2026, with PhysicalAddress.com added on November 25, 2026.

| Provider | Handling fee | Plus | How it's deposited |
| US Global Mail | None. "We don't charge any additional handling fees for check deposit" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11321978-how-do-i-handle-business-check-deposits) | Standard shipping (trackable methods only), and optional repacking [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11321978-how-do-i-handle-business-check-deposits) | They print a deposit slip and mail the check to your bank. Or you deposit the scanned image through your bank yourself [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11321978-how-do-i-handle-business-check-deposits) |
| PhysicalAddress.com | None. "our check deposit feature does not have an additional fee; all you'll pay is the cost of forwarding, no check handling fee is included" [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-does-your-check-deposit-service-work/) | Forwarding postage [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-does-your-check-deposit-service-work/) | It generates a deposit slip and mails the check to the bank of your choice [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-does-your-check-deposit-service-work/) |
| Stable | "Volume-based plans as low as $3/check" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | A separate check-deposit purchase; "you must have an existing Stable account" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Electronic and mail-in options [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| Traveling Mailbox | $4.95 per check [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | Postage [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | Endorsed "For Deposit Only" and mailed to your bank [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| iPostal1 | $4.95 to deposit up to 5 checks (most locations) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | "The cost of check scan(s) and trackable shipping." U.S. only [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | By mail [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Earth Class Mail (LegalZoom Virtual Mail) | $10 per check without a subscription. Or the check deposit subscription: $39/mo with 5 checks included, then $2 per check [source](https://www.earthclassmail.com/pricing) | Expedited: $20 per check, with free overnight shipping to Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo. Other deposits go by USPS [source](https://www.earthclassmail.com/pricing) | Mailed to your bank [source](https://www.earthclassmail.com/pricing) |
| PostScan Mail | Not listed on the pricing page [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | | |
| Anytime Mailbox | Set by each location's operator [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) | | Listed as a service on location pages [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue) |

Want your own number? The virtual mailbox chooser works out a monthly cost for your mail volume, scans and checks.

## What three checks a month costs
Handling fees only. Postage or shipping is extra everywhere except where noted, and it depends on the carrier you pick.

| Provider | 3 checks, mailed together | Math |
| US Global Mail | $0 + shipping | No handling fee [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11321978-how-do-i-handle-business-check-deposits) |
| PhysicalAddress.com | $0 + postage | No handling fee [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-does-your-check-deposit-service-work/) |
| iPostal1 | $4.95 + scans + shipping | One $4.95 deposit covers up to 5 checks. The page doesn't say how scans of checks are charged [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Stable | from $9 | 3 × "as low as $3." The rate at low volume isn't published [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| Traveling Mailbox | $14.85 + postage | 3 × $4.95 [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Earth Class Mail | $30, or $39 on the subscription | 3 × $10 without a subscription. The $39 subscription only pays off from the 4th check a month (4 × $10 = $40) [source](https://www.earthclassmail.com/pricing) |

## Things to check before relying on mailed deposits

- Will your bank take checks by mail? US Global Mail tells customers to call their local branch first and ask, "Do you accept checks by mail?" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11321978-how-do-i-handle-business-check-deposits)
- Mobile deposit from a scan depends on your bank's own rules. US Global Mail offers it as an option [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11321978-how-do-i-handle-business-check-deposits), but whether your bank accepts a deposit from a scanned image is up to the bank.
- The deposit fee usually comes on top of your plan. Earth Class Mail lists the check deposit subscription ($39/mo) separately from its MailBox plans, which start at $39/mo [source](https://www.earthclassmail.com/pricing). LegalZoom's FAQ now says check depositing "can be added for an additional fee" [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html), so 5 checks a month on the Starter plan costs $78 a month in total (rechecked 2026-11-21). Full fee list: Earth Class Mail pricing.

# Mail forwarding fees compared
Every virtual mailbox charges postage when it ships your mail. What differs is the handling fee on top: some charge once per box, some charge for every item inside it, and a few charge nothing but postage. If you forward a stack of letters once a month, that structure matters more than the plan price. Fees below are from each provider's own pricing page, checked November 23, 2026, with PhysicalAddress.com added on November 25, 2026.

## Handling fee on top of postage

| Provider | Forwarding fee (plus postage) | Charged per | Consolidating items |
| Traveling Mailbox | $2 [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | Shipment ("not per piece") | No extra charge [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| PostScan Mail | $2.00 for the first item, $0.50 for each additional item [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | Item | Items can be bundled into one package [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| LegalZoom Virtual Mail (Earth Class Mail) | Domestic $1.25 per shipment + $1 per item; international $5 per shipment + $1 per item; expedited $10 per shipment + $1 per item [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) | Shipment + item | Medium box $5, large box $10 [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| US Global Mail | No handling fee; discounted carrier rates [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) | — | Repack fee $5 per box, $2 per letter [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) |
| PhysicalAddress.com | No separate handling fee published; "competitive commercial prices" through USPS, FedEx, UPS and DHL [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/what-are-my-options-for-forwarding-mail-and-packages/) | — | — |
| Stable | "Add cost of postage" (no separate fee listed) [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | — | Can combine mail and packages going to the same address [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| iPostal1 | Real-time shipping prices; no separate forwarding fee listed [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | — | Letters free; $1.95 per package or letter-pack consolidated [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Virtual Post Mail | Varies with destination, weight and size [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) | — | — |
| Anytime Mailbox | Set by each location [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) | — | — |

Postage is extra everywhere. US Global Mail says its rates are up to 80% off retail for most carriers [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained), and that the rate shown before packing is an estimate [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022385-how-much-does-it-cost-to-ship-my-mail). Traveling Mailbox says it passes its shipping discounts on [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953). PostScan Mail's package lockers have their own fees ($2 or $1 per item forwarded) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).

## Worked example: 10 letters in one domestic box
Handling fees only, before postage:

| Provider | Math | Handling fee |
| iPostal1 | Letters consolidated free [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $0 |
| Stable | Postage only [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | $0 |
| PhysicalAddress.com | No separate handling fee published [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/what-are-my-options-for-forwarding-mail-and-packages/) | $0 |
| Traveling Mailbox | $2 per shipment [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | $2 |
| PostScan Mail | $2.00 + 9 × $0.50 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | $6.50 |
| LegalZoom Virtual Mail | $1.25 + 10 × $1 [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) | $11.25 |
| US Global Mail | No handling fee; if the $2-per-letter repack fee applies to all 10 letters, 10 × $2 [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) | $0 to $20 |

Ship one letter at a time instead and the order flips: PostScan Mail charges $2.00 per single-item shipment [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html), the same as Traveling Mailbox [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953), and LegalZoom charges $2.25 ($1.25 + $1) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html). Per-item pricing gets expensive with big batches; per-shipment pricing rewards batching.

## Ways to cut forwarding costs

- Batch. With a per-shipment fee, one monthly box costs the same handling as one letter [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953). iPostal1 lets you schedule shipments weekly, bi-weekly or monthly [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
- Don't forward what you can scan. Most mail only needs to be read. Compare scan allowances in virtual mailbox pricing compared.
- Watch storage clocks. Waiting to batch is free only until the free storage period ends; see how long virtual mailboxes keep your mail.
- Checks are a separate service. Mailing a check to your bank has its own fee at most providers; see check deposit fees.

## If you're away for months
For long trips, compare a virtual mailbox's forwarding against USPS Premium Forwarding Service, which packs up your mail at your Post Office and sends it weekly by Priority Mail for a $26.40 online enrollment fee plus $29.70 a week [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward-premium.htm). Our mail for full-time RVers page covers both, and living abroad covers international shipping.

- Traveling Mailbox
- iPostal1
- PostScan Mail
- Virtual Post Mail

# Virtual mailbox pricing, compared
Short answer: Entry plans start at $4.99 (Anytime Mailbox, varies by location), $7.98 (PhysicalAddress.com, in Boise), $9.99 (iPostal1), $10 (PostScan Mail) and $15 (Traveling Mailbox). Scans and forwarding decide the real bill: at 30 letters with 10 opened and scanned, PhysicalAddress.com Plan 30 stays at $7.98 and Traveling Mailbox Basic stays at $15, while PostScan Mail Starter comes to $30 or more. [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) [source](https://ipostal1.com/) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953)

The sticker price is the smallest part of the bill. What decides the real cost is how many pieces of mail are included, what each scan past that costs, and what forwarding costs. Here are the published numbers for nine services, copied from each provider's own page on November 19, 2026. US Global Mail's entry plan was rechecked on November 24, 2026, and PhysicalAddress.com was added from its own pages on November 25, 2026.
How to read this: "from" prices vary by location for iPostal1, Anytime Mailbox and PostScan Mail, because independent mail centers set them. PhysicalAddress.com runs its own locations, and its starting price still varies by city. The table shows the lowest price each provider advertises. Annual billing is cheaper at several providers, and both prices are shown where the page lists both.
Want your own number? The virtual mailbox chooser works out a monthly cost for your mail volume, scans and checks.

## Entry plans side by side

| Provider | Cheapest plan (as published) | Mail included | Scans / overage | Forwarding | Form 1583 signing |

It emails a pre-filled form and a link to a partner online notary; the notary fee is not published [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-do-i-sign-up-for-physicaladdress-com/) |

| Stable | Grow $59/mo monthly or $49/mo billed yearly; Scale $99/mo or $83/mo yearly [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Grow: 30 pieces a month (360/yr on yearly); junk excluded [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Open & scan free; $3 per piece over the plan limit [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Postage cost (add-on) [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | No notary; Stable verifies your IDs in-house [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8236356-why-are-my-ids-being-verified-for-the-usps-1583) |
| US Global Mail | Occasional $25/mo monthly or $21/mo billed annually; Scale $65/mo or $49/mo; Teams $129/mo or $99/mo. Prices marked "*varies by address" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | Occasional: exterior envelope scans, $2 per interior scan, 5 recipients. Scale: 360 envelopes opened and scanned a year, 10 recipients [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | $2 per mail on Occasional; included on Scale, subject to fair use [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | — | "No need to find a notary separately" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/usps-form-1583/?via=michelle) |
| Opus Virtual Offices | All-inclusive virtual office $99/mo (address, live call answering, phone/fax, mail receipt) [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/) | — | — | — | — |

Virtual Post Mail also publishes plans on its pricing page. We weren't able to load those prices, so it isn't in the table yet.

## What does a virtual mailbox really cost per month?
Say you get 30 letters a month and want 10 of them opened and scanned (about 3 pages each), with nothing forwarded.

- PhysicalAddress.com Plan 30: $7.98 at the price published on the pricing page (the same as its Boise starting price). 30 envelope scans and 10 content scans are included, so this example stays at the plan price [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/).
- Traveling Mailbox Basic: $15. 30 envelopes and 30 page scans fit inside the 40-envelope / 35-page allowance [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- PostScan Mail Starter: from $10, plus $2.00 for each of the 10 open-and-scans ($20), so from $30. The Starter plan lists no free open-and-scans; Standard includes 5 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- Stable Grow: $59 monthly ($49 if paid yearly). 30 pieces is the monthly limit, and open-and-scan is free [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing).
- Earth Class Mail Starter: $39 covers 5 digitized items, so 30 items is well past the allowance. The overage rate wasn't clearly listed.
Someone who scans very little and mostly wants an address does best with a cheap Anytime Mailbox or iPostal1 location. Anyone who wants most of their mail opened pays less with a plan that includes page scans.

## Is a virtual mailbox a street address or a P.O. Box?
Every provider above gives you a street address at a Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA), not a USPS P.O. Box. USPS requires every CMRA customer to sign Form 1583 before the CMRA can handle their mail [source](https://about.usps.com/postal-bulletin/2024/pb22648/html/updt_001.htm). Some banks and agencies won't accept a CMRA address. Anytime Mailbox, for example, says it doesn't recommend using its address as your official business address because "some states and institutions may have restrictions" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/).

## Go to a provider

- iPostal1
- Anytime Mailbox
- PostScan Mail
- US Global Mail
- Stable
- Earth Class Mail / LegalZoom Virtual Mail

# Does junk mail count toward your virtual mailbox limit?
Short answer: At most providers, no. Traveling Mailbox, Stable, LegalZoom Virtual Mail and Virtual Post Mail exclude junk from your monthly limit, most iPostal1 locations discard it without counting it, and US Global Mail has no mail-piece limit. PostScan Mail is the exception: junk counts, and every item over your plan costs $0.50.

Most plans cap the pieces of mail you can receive each month, and catalogs and credit card offers can eat that cap fast. Here's how each provider treats junk, and what an extra piece costs once you're over, from each provider's own pages on November 24, 2026.

## Which providers count junk mail?

| Provider | Does junk count? | How junk is handled | Cost per piece over the limit |
| Traveling Mailbox | No, once you mark it as junk | You mark it as junk, and it's shredded for free [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | $0.25 per envelope [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Stable | No | Obvious junk (advertisements, coupons, magazines) is filtered out and never uploaded [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | $3 [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| LegalZoom Virtual Mail (Earth Class Mail) | No | Plan limits are listed with "junk mail excluded from limit" [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) | $3 per item [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Virtual Post Mail | No, for obvious junk | Obvious junk is sorted out automatically. If staff aren't sure, the item is uploaded [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) | $0.50 on Starter; Plus and up have unlimited envelopes [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) |
| iPostal1 | No, at most locations | "Most iPostal1 locations" discard USPS Standard Mail (flyers, circulars, catalogs), and discarded junk doesn't count [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | $0.35 per item [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| US Global Mail | No limit to count against | Obvious junk is pre-sorted out and shredded for free [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11272791-do-you-pre-filter-junk-mail) | No cap on mail pieces [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/14081430-is-there-a-limit-to-the-number-of-mail-pieces-i-can-receive) |
| PostScan Mail | Yes | Counts toward your limit "so that no desired mail is mistakenly destroyed"; some addresses may filter Presorted Standard mail [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) | $0.50 per item [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |

Anytime Mailbox plans are set by each location, and its FAQ doesn't publish one junk mail rule [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq). Check the plan details for the address you choose.

## The fine print

- Traveling Mailbox: "anything you mark as 'Junk' is shredded for free and does not count towards your plan limits" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953). So it's your click that keeps it off the count.
- Virtual Post Mail: an older help article says "any mail that shows up in your online mailbox counts toward your quota." Mail addressed to "Current Resident/Occupant" is trashed automatically, but things like a bank's debit card offer get uploaded to be safe [source](https://help.virtualpostmail.com/article/35-does-junk-count). This only matters on Starter, which caps envelopes at 25 [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/).
- Stable: Grow allows 30 pieces a month (360 a year on yearly billing) and Scale 50 (600 a year). Junk "will be filtered out" before counting [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing).
- US Global Mail: doesn't limit incoming mail, but says accounts with "unusually high volumes" may be reviewed [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/14081430-is-there-a-limit-to-the-number-of-mail-pieces-i-can-receive).
- iPostal1: the rule applies at "most" locations, not all [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).

## What does junk cost on a capped plan?
Say you get 40 pieces a month and 15 of them are junk.

- PostScan Mail Starter (30 items, from $10/mo): all 40 count, so 10 over × $0.50 = $5 a month extra [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).
- Stable Grow (30 pieces): 25 count, so no overage [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing).
- iPostal1 $9.99 plan (30 items): if your location discards the junk, 25 count and there's no overage. If it doesn't, 10 × $0.35 = $3.50 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
- Traveling Mailbox Basic (40 envelopes): within the limit either way [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).

## How can you cut junk at the source?

- Prescreened credit and insurance offers: the CFPB says you can opt out at OptOutPrescreen.com or by calling 1-888-5-OPTOUT. A phone or online opt-out lasts five years; a permanent opt-out needs a signed form by mail [source](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/can-i-make-issuers-stop-sending-me-credit-card-offers-in-the-mail-en-1377/).
- Don't forward advertising: a USPS change of address doesn't forward USPS Marketing Mail unless the sender has paid for forwarding [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm). If you move your mail to a virtual mailbox that way, most bulk advertising stays behind.

## Links

- US Global Mail
- Virtual Post Mail
- Traveling Mailbox
- Stable
- iPostal1
