# Form 1583 rejected: reasons and fixes
Short answer: Most rejections come down to a mismatch or an unreadable document. USPS rules say that if the information on the form doesn't match the ID, the mail center must deny the application. Fix the specific item (name, home address, expired or blurry ID, wrong document type), upload again, and re-sign if the form changed. Re-review takes 1 to 3 business days at iPostal1 and about 2 to 3 at US Global Mail.

Your virtual mailbox can't accept mail until Form 1583 is approved, and some providers bill you whether or not it's approved. Below are the reasons USPS rules and providers' help pages give for rejections, with the fix for each, checked November 24, 2026.

## Why was my Form 1583 rejected?

| Reason | The rule | Fix |
| Name doesn't match the ID | The mail center must deny the application if the form doesn't match the ID [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). US Global Mail: the name on the ID must match the recipient name on the mailbox [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516585-my-id-was-rejected-why-and-what-do-i-upload-instead) | Use your legal name exactly as on the ID. If your name changed, have the account corrected first [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516585-my-id-was-rejected-why-and-what-do-i-upload-instead) |
| Home address doesn't match the address ID | The home address in item 4f must match the address document in 9b [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf) | Enter the address exactly as it appears on your address ID. If you moved, update the address and upload a document showing the new one [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516580-the-information-on-my-regenerated-form-1583-is-wrong) |
| Expired ID | IDs must be current (not expired) [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) | Upload a current ID. At US Global Mail, a "flagged as expired" result often means the date wasn't readable; retake the photo with the date clearly visible [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516585-my-id-was-rejected-why-and-what-do-i-upload-instead) |
| Blurry, dark or cropped image | Illegible or unclear ID images are "not in compliance" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) | Good light, no glare, all four corners in frame [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516585-my-id-was-rejected-why-and-what-do-i-upload-instead) |
| Only one side uploaded | The address ID must show the address on the form [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf) | Upload the back too if your address is printed there [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516585-my-id-was-rejected-why-and-what-do-i-upload-instead) |
| Driver's license used for both IDs | A driver's or non-driver's ID can be the photo ID or the address ID, not both [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf) | Add a second document: lease, mortgage or deed of trust, voter or vehicle registration, or home or vehicle insurance policy [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf) |
| Document type not accepted | USPS doesn't accept Social Security cards, birth certificates or credit cards [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/608.htm) | Pick from the form's photo ID and address ID lists. US Global Mail also rejects utility bills, corporate ID cards and non-U.S. driver's licenses [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11329217-acceptable-id-s-for-form-1583-verification) |
| Business box checked, section 7 blank | Business/Organization use requires item 7, signed by an officer with their title [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf) | Complete section 7; see Form 1583 for a business |
| Form altered or signed wrong | A modified or altered Form 1583 is invalid [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). A notary, if used, must be commissioned in a U.S. state, territory, possession or D.C. [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf) | Ask the provider to regenerate the form and sign again [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516579-i-signed-my-form-1583-but-did-it-wrong-can-i-sign-it-again) |

## Provider-specific rules that catch people

- Earth Class Mail (LegalZoom): both IDs must be valid, not expired, and "in a language that uses the Latin alphabet," and the secondary ID must show your name "exactly as listed on the primary ID" [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/17815150891799-How-to-re-authorize-recipients).
- PostScan Mail: documents must be "in English or English-translated." Foreign driver's licenses, national ID cards and foreign university IDs aren't accepted [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).
- US Global Mail: a document it accepted when you signed up can be flagged now, because the 2024 USPS update "revised the list of document types accepted as secondary ID." Your secondary ID also can't be the same document type as your primary [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/15460453-usps-form-1583-update-what-s-changing-and-why).
- Stable: if documents are rejected (Stable's examples are poor image quality, expired IDs and mismatched information), the signature packet is deleted. You upload new documents and sign again [source](https://docs.usestable.com/docs/create-and-onboard-a-new-location).
- iPostal1: forms are reviewed by its 1583 team, then sent to the mail center for final approval, which takes 1 to 3 business days [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).

## How do I resubmit?

- Read the rejection email. US Global Mail emails the reason and reopens the upload step [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/15460453-usps-form-1583-update-what-s-changing-and-why), and reviews new documents in about 2 to 3 business days [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516585-my-id-was-rejected-why-and-what-do-i-upload-instead).
- Fix only what was flagged. If the problem is wrong information on a pre-filled form, US Global Mail says "Do not sign a Form 1583 that contains incorrect information"; ask for a corrected form instead [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516580-the-information-on-my-regenerated-form-1583-is-wrong).
- Re-sign if the form changed. Stable asks you to sign a new signature packet [source](https://docs.usestable.com/docs/create-and-onboard-a-new-location). US Global Mail regenerates the form and sends a new e-signature request, at no charge [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516579-i-signed-my-form-1583-but-did-it-wrong-can-i-sign-it-again).
- If a notary is required again, iPostal1's online notary is $25 and PostScan Mail's partner notary is $20 [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html). Providers that verify you on video without a notary are compared in Form 1583 and online notarization.

## Does a rejection pause billing or deadlines?

- Billing: iPostal1 says the charge "will process and auto-renew whether or not you choose to complete the Form 1583" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
- Deadlines: at US Global Mail, your 30-day window keeps running while a correction is in progress [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516580-the-information-on-my-regenerated-form-1583-is-wrong). If required documents aren't approved by the deadline, mail receipt is suspended until the account is compliant [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/15460453-usps-form-1583-update-what-s-changing-and-why).
- Mail in the meantime: a mail center with no Form 1583 on file for you must return your mail to the Post Office [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Hold off on your change of address until you're approved.

## Living outside the U.S.?
A foreign passport works as the photo ID, but a non-U.S. driver's license doesn't. For the address ID, US Global Mail says documents showing your foreign home address (a lease, mortgage, vehicle registration, insurance policy or voter card) are "generally workable" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/16516585-my-id-was-rejected-why-and-what-do-i-upload-instead). More in getting a U.S. mailbox from abroad.

## Links

- US Global Mail (no notary needed)
- Traveling Mailbox (video verification, no notary)
- BlueNotary (online notary)
- Notarize (online notary)

# HIPAA-compliant virtual mailboxes
Short answer: If a mail service will open and scan mail that contains patient information, you'll want it to sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA). Four providers publish one: Virtual Post Mail on its Business plan ($60/mo) and up, PostScan Mail as a $25/mo add-on (billed annually) plus $0.50 per item, Stable on request (listed on its Custom plan), and US Global Mail on its Enterprise plan only.

"HIPAA compliant" on a pricing page and a signed BAA aren't the same thing. Below is what each provider actually offers, which plan you need, and what it costs, from each provider's own pages on November 24, 2026. This is a price and feature reference, not legal advice; your own compliance review still applies.

## Why does a virtual mailbox need a BAA when USPS doesn't?
HHS says covered entities don't need business associate contracts with the U.S. Postal Service or private couriers that act "merely as conduits." A conduit "transports information but does not access it other than on a random or infrequent basis" [source](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/245/are-entities-business-associates/index.html). A virtual mailbox that opens your envelopes and uploads the contents does more than carry them. That's why the providers that market to healthcare offer a BAA, and why Stable's FAQ says a provider "should be willing to sign a Business Associate Agreement" [source](https://www.usestable.com/use-cases/hipaa-compliant-virtual-mailbox).

## Which providers sign a BAA?

| Provider | BAA offered? | Plan you need | Published price |
| Virtual Post Mail | Yes [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/security/) | Business plan or higher [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/customers/healthcare-providers/) | Business $60/mo, Premium $90/mo [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) |
| PostScan Mail | HIPAA Compliance add-on [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | Add-on to a mailbox plan (plans from $10/mo) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | $25/mo billed annually, then $0.50 per received mail item [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Stable | Yes, "available on request" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | "HIPAA BAA" is listed under the Custom plan [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Custom: "Contact us for details" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| US Global Mail | Yes [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/virtual-business-mailbox/digital-mailroom/healthcare) | Enterprise only; the Occasional, Scale and Teams plans don't include it [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | Enterprise: custom [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) |

Traveling Mailbox, iPostal1, Anytime Mailbox and LegalZoom Virtual Mail don't mention HIPAA or a BAA on the pricing pages we checked [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html). Ask them directly before sending patient mail there.

## What does each one include?

### Virtual Post Mail

- Says it "will also sign a BAA to satisfy HIPAA requirements" and that mail is processed in-house "by HIPAA and SOC 2-trained staff—never by a third party" [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/security/).
- Unwanted mail is shredded on site, and destruction certificates are available on request [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/security/).
- Claims to be the only provider offering a BAA "at every location"; the BAA is available "only on Business Plans or higher" [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/customers/healthcare-providers/).
- The Business plan includes unlimited envelope scans, 100 content scans, 10 users and 10 recipients [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/). Full plan table: Virtual Post Mail pricing.

### PostScan Mail

- HIPAA is a paid add-on: "$25.00 per month, billed annually, then $0.50 per received mail item" [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- That per-item charge stacks on the plan. The Starter plan is from $10/mo with 30 items, and PostScan counts junk mail toward your limit [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).
- More fees: PostScan Mail pricing.

### Stable

- Says it is "fully HIPAA-compliant and BAAs are available," with mail data "encrypted in transit and at rest" and every action logged [source](https://www.usestable.com/use-cases/hipaa-compliant-virtual-mailbox).
- Signs a BAA "on request for healthcare clients" [source](https://www.usestable.com/use-cases/hipaa-compliant-virtual-mailbox). Its pricing page lists "HIPAA BAA" among the Custom plan's features [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing); the self-serve plans are Grow ($49/mo billed yearly) and Scale ($83/mo billed yearly) [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing).
- Stable says you can keep your current address and forward mail to its processing centers instead of taking a new address [source](https://www.usestable.com/use-cases/hipaa-compliant-virtual-mailbox).

### US Global Mail

- Describes itself as "SOC 2 Type II audited and HIPAA compliant" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/virtual-business-mailbox/compliance).
- The BAA is offered "on our custom plans" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/virtual-business-mailbox/compliance). Its healthcare page says "HIPAA support and the Business Associate Agreement are part of our Enterprise offering" and that the team reviews your scope before you send PHI [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/virtual-business-mailbox/digital-mailroom/healthcare).
- In the plan comparison, "HIPAA with BAA" is checked only for Enterprise. Occasional ($25 a month, or $21 billed annually), Scale ($65 or $49) and Teams ($129 or $99) don't include it [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle).

## What does it cost at 100 pieces of mail a month?
Example: a small practice getting 100 pieces a month, using only published prices.

- Virtual Post Mail Business: $60/mo. Incoming envelopes are unlimited on Business, and 100 content scans are included [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/).
- PostScan Mail: the HIPAA add-on alone is $25 + 100 × $0.50 = $75/mo, before the mailbox plan. The Premium plan covers 120 items and starts at $30/mo, so the total starts around $105/mo [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- Stable and US Global Mail: BAA plans are quoted individually [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle).

## Before you sign up

- Get the BAA signed before the first piece of PHI arrives. US Global Mail says to review the agreement and covered services "before US Global Mail receives or processes PHI" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/virtual-business-mailbox/digital-mailroom/healthcare).
- A BAA covers the vendor, not your whole workflow. US Global Mail notes your organization "must also assess its own policies, permitted uses, and connected systems" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/virtual-business-mailbox/digital-mailroom/healthcare).
- Every person and business name that gets mail still needs its own USPS Form 1583. See Form 1583 for a business.

## Links

- Virtual Post Mail
- US Global Mail
- PostScan Mail
- Stable

# How to change your address to a virtual mailbox
Short answer: Wait until your Form 1583 is approved, then file a USPS change of address to your new address with its PMB number (online, with a $1.25 identity check). After that, give the new address to your bank, the IRS and anyone who sends sensitive mail, because USPS forwarding won't move those. Form 1583 on its own doesn't forward anything.

There are two separate pieces: the USPS form that lets the mail center accept your mail, and the change of address that sends mail there. Here are the steps in order, with the rules from USPS and the providers' own pages, checked November 24, 2026.

## Step 1: Get Form 1583 approved first

- Form 1583 "only gives permission to your mail center to receive mail on your behalf." It doesn't change your address [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php). Traveling Mailbox says the same thing: the form "does not forward your mail" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953).
- Mail that arrives before your form is approved can be sent back. iPostal1 says mail before approval is "subject to be returned to sender" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php), and USPS rules tell a mail center with no Form 1583 on file to return the mail to the Post Office [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).
- Choose the address carefully. At US Global Mail, the address can be changed only until your Form 1583 is approved. After that, you need a new account and a new form [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11272138-what-if-i-want-to-change-my-us-global-mail-virtual-mailbox-address).

## Step 2: File a USPS change of address
A change of address isn't required. Anytime Mailbox and PostScan Mail both call it optional but recommended; without it, you have to tell every sender yourself [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).

- Online: on the official USPS site, you pay a $1.25 identity verification fee, and the card's billing address must match your old or new address [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm).
- In person: fill out PS Form 3575 from a Mover's Guide packet at a Post Office, with photo ID [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm).
- Timing: allow at least 7 to 10 business days after approval for it to take effect [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm).
- Your PMB number: use the full address the provider gives you, with "PMB" or "#" and your number. USPS can return mail without it as "Undeliverable as Addressed, Missing PMB or # Sign" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).

## Temporary or permanent change of address?

| | Temporary | Permanent |
| Meant for | Relocating for 15 days up to 1 year [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm) | Moving [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm) |
| How long forwarding lasts | 15 to 185 days on the first order; a second order can extend it to 364 days total [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/507.htm) | 12 months; paid Extended Mail Forwarding adds 6, 12 or 18 months [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm) |
| Notices to senders | No address-correction notices for temporary orders [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/507.htm) | — |

iPostal1 tells customers to file a temporary change of address and says "We do not recommend filing a Permanent Change of Address form with the USPS" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php). With a temporary order, you still get to decide later whether the virtual mailbox becomes your long-term address.

## What won't a change of address forward?

- Sensitive documents: USPS says government agencies and financial institutions "do not allow forwarding" of identity documents, credit cards, bank statements, insurance information and medical information [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm). Update those senders directly.
- Advertising: USPS Marketing Mail isn't forwarded unless the sender paid for forwarding [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm). That helps if your plan counts junk; see junk mail rules by provider.
- Media Mail: forwarded, but you pay the shipping from your local Post Office [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm).
- Periodicals: forwarded free for 60 days if fully prepaid by the sender [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm).

## Step 3: Update senders directly
USPS says a change of address "only changes your mailing address with the Post Office," and you're responsible for telling government agencies, companies and other senders [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm).

- IRS, personal: Form 8822 notifies the IRS of a change to your home mailing address [source](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-8822).
- IRS, business: Form 8822-B is for entities with an EIN that change their business mailing address, business location or responsible party [source](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-8822-b).
- Banks: check what your bank accepts first; some address fields don't take a mailbox address. See using a virtual mailbox for a bank account.
- State filings for a company: a mailbox can be the mailing address, but Texas, Florida and California require a registered agent at a real in-state street address. See virtual mailbox for an LLC.
Some providers help with this step. Stable includes "change of address guidance" on all plans, with a tailored checklist and pre-filled paperwork [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing), and US Global Mail lists "change of address guidance" on every plan [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle).

## Can you forward mail from a virtual mailbox later?
Not with USPS. Under the Form 1583 agreement, neither you nor the mail center may file a change of address with USPS when the service ends [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf). The mail center instead has to remail your mail for at least 6 months, with new postage, to the address on your form, unless you tell it in writing not to [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).

- Anytime Mailbox: "a change of address form cannot be submitted for a digital mailbox"; mail is stored up to six months after you cancel, and storage and forwarding fees may apply [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq).
- PostScan Mail: USPS "does not allow a Change-of-Address request to redirect mail from a CMRA"; you have to contact your senders [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).
So if you might leave the mailbox one day, keep a list of everyone you gave the address to. More in how long mail is kept.

## Moving abroad?
If you're moving outside the U.S., USPS requires you to file the change of address in person at a Post Office, and identity can only be verified in person in the 50 states and Puerto Rico. From outside the U.S., you can't file one at all [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward.htm). File it before you leave. See getting a U.S. mailbox from abroad.

## Links

- US Global Mail (change of address guidance on every plan)
- Stable (change of address checklist)
- Virtual Post Mail
- Traveling Mailbox

# US Global Mail vs Traveling Mailbox
Both scan your mail, forward it worldwide and skip the notary for Form 1583. The gap is price. Traveling Mailbox starts at $15 a month. US Global Mail's cheapest current plan is Occasional, at $25 a month or $21 billed annually. Prices are marked "*varies by address." Here's what that money gets you, using both companies' own pages on November 24, 2026.

## Fee by fee

| | US Global Mail | Traveling Mailbox |
| Entry plan | Occasional: $25/mo monthly, or $21/mo billed annually. Prices are marked "*varies by address" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | Basic: $15/mo. Annual plans "get 2 months free" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Higher plans | Scale $65/mo, or $49/mo billed annually; Teams $129/mo, or $99/mo annually; Enterprise custom [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | Extended $25/mo; Small Business $55/mo [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Envelope (outside) scans | "Always free and unlimited on every plan" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | 40 incoming envelopes/mo on Basic. Junk you mark doesn't count [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Opening and scanning contents | $2 per mail on Occasional. Scale includes 360 envelopes opened and scanned a year, "subject to our fair use policy" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | 35 page scans/mo on Basic. Envelope scans don't use up page scans [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Overage | On Occasional, interior scans are $2 each. On Scale, $3 per extra open-and-scan after the included allowance; discounted scan bundles available [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | $0.25 per extra envelope, $0.50 per extra page scan [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Recipients (names) | 5 on Occasional, 10 on Scale, 25 on Teams; $5 each after that [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | 3 on Basic, 5 on Extended, 10 on Small Business [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Extra logins | $25 per user (billed monthly) [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | Not listed on the pricing page |
| Forwarding fee | No handling fee. You pay the shipping rate, which the company says is discounted up to 80% off retail (USPS isn't discounted). Repacking is $5 per box or $2 per letter [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022385-how-much-does-it-cost-to-ship-my-mail) | Postage + $2 per shipment, not per piece. Consolidation is free [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Free mail storage | 30 days on Occasional and Scale, 60 on Teams. After that, $0.05 per mail item per day; packages $0.10/day (and $0.10 per lb per day from Jan 1, 2027) [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | Envelopes 30 days, then $1 per envelope per month to hold (otherwise shredded). Packages 30 days, then $0.10 per lb per day [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Digital scan storage | 180 days on Occasional and Scale, unlimited on Teams [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | Unlimited [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Check deposit | No handling fee, by mail or by uploading the scan to your bank; you pay shipping [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11321978-how-do-i-handle-business-check-deposits) | $4.95 per check + postage [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Form 1583 | Pre-filled. "No need to find a notary separately" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/usps-form-1583/?via=michelle) | Video call with staff. Asked whether the form must be notarized, the company answers "No!" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953) |
| Refund / contract | No long-term contract; 30-day money-back guarantee [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | Month to month. Annual plans are "refundable on a monthly schedule" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Other | SOC 2 audited; HIPAA with BAA on Teams; AI summaries; API on Teams [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | 10% monthly discount for active-duty military and veterans [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |

Traveling Mailbox's plan cards list "Your Scans Rollover" on Basic too, but the footnote says only "Extended, Small Business, and Enterprise Plans rollover unused Envelope and Page Scans" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).

## Worked example: a typical household
25 letters a month, 10 opened (about 3 pages each, so 30 pages), one forwarded batch a month:

- Traveling Mailbox Basic: $15 + $2 for the shipment = $17 + postage. 25 envelopes and 30 pages both fit inside 40 / 35 [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- US Global Mail Occasional: $25 + 10 × $2 = $45 + shipping monthly, or $21 + $20 = $41 + shipping billed annually, because interior scans are $2 each [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle). Scale, at $65 + shipping monthly or $49 billed annually, includes those opens in its 360-a-year allowance [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained).
At this volume, Traveling Mailbox is still cheaper than Occasional, because Occasional charges $2 to open each letter. Scale includes the opens, but starts at $65 a month (or $49 billed annually). Add 3 paper checks a month and Traveling Mailbox goes up by 3 × $4.95 = $14.85 plus postage, while US Global Mail adds only shipping [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11321978-how-do-i-handle-business-check-deposits). Traveling Mailbox remains the lower bill in this example.

## When US Global Mail is worth it

- Several businesses or family members on one box. Scale includes 10 recipients, against 3 on Traveling Mailbox Basic and 5 on US Global Mail Occasional [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- You need HIPAA with a BAA, SOC 2, team permissions or an API [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle).
- You ship lots of packages internationally and want the consolidation and carrier discounts US Global Mail advertises [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained). Compare quotes. The discount claim is the company's own.

## When Traveling Mailbox is the better buy

- You mainly want letters scanned and the occasional batch forwarded. $15 covers most single households, and the company says most customers fit on Basic [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- You want to keep scans forever without paying for a higher tier (unlimited cloud storage on every plan) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- You're military or a veteran (10% off) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).

- US Global Mail
- Traveling Mailbox

# Form 1583 for a business
Short answer: Check "Business/Organization Use," fill in section 7 (business name, type, street address, phone and place of registration), and have a company officer sign with their title. The business doesn't need its own ID: the officer's photo ID and address ID cover it. Every business name on the mailbox needs its own Form 1583.

USPS Form 1583 works the same for a company as for a person, with a few extra boxes. Here's what the current form (June 2024 edition) and the USPS rules say, and how providers handle business names, checked November 24, 2026. For notary options and the basic ID list, see Form 1583 and online notarization.

## Who signs Form 1583 for a business?
An officer. The form's instructions say: "for Business/Organization Use, an officer must sign the application and provide his or her title" [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf). Like any applicant, the officer signs in front of the mail center's staff (in person or on a live video call) or a U.S.-commissioned notary [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf).
That's why your personal name appears on a company's form. iPostal1 explains that "the USPS requires a responsible party on each mailbox," and that your name is kept confidential to the mail center and USPS [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php). US Global Mail requires "1 primary name" on every business account, an officer of the company who signs Form 1583 [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11272074-do-i-need-a-form-1583-for-family-members-or-my-business).

## Which IDs does a business need?
The officer's. The business itself provides none:

- Two IDs for the applicant: a government-issued photo ID and a second document showing the address on the form [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf).
- US Global Mail: "Business names don't require their own IDs but the company officer must be on the account with two IDs" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11329217-acceptable-id-s-for-form-1583-verification). It also lists a corporate identification card as not acceptable [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11329217-acceptable-id-s-for-form-1583-verification).
- One driver's license can't count as both the photo ID and the address ID [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf).

## What goes in section 7?
If you check "Business/Organization Use" in item 3, you must complete item 7 [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf):

| Field | What to enter |
| 7a Name of business | The name mail will be addressed to |
| 7b Type of business | What the business does |
| 7c–7g Business street address | The business's own address. Anytime Mailbox notes this "cannot be the mailbox address you are currently signing up for" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583) |
| 7h Telephone | The business phone |
| 7i Place of registration | "The county and state (if domestic), or the country (if foreign)" [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf) |

- Not registered yet? Anytime Mailbox says to enter N/A for place of registration if the business is new or not yet registered [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583). Earth Class Mail has a "Check if not applicable" box for cases like a sole proprietorship [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/17815150891799-How-to-re-authorize-recipients).
- Verification: USPS may check that you conduct business at the address in 7c [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf).

## Employees and partners who get mail (item 12)
For a business mailbox, item 12 lists the members who will receive mail there. Each person listed must present two forms of valid ID to USPS on request [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf). That's different from personal use, where each adult files a separate Form 1583 [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf).
Providers handle this in different ways. US Global Mail separates recipients (people whose mail it receives; each adult needs their own two IDs and Form 1583) from users (people who log in to manage mail; no form or ID needed) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/15460453-usps-form-1583-update-what-s-changing-and-why).

## How many business names can one mailbox have?
Each business name needs its own form. US Global Mail says "every mailbox name on your account (including any company or trust names) requires its own Form 1583," each listing you as the account holder [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/15460453-usps-form-1583-update-what-s-changing-and-why). The cost per extra name varies:

| Provider | Business names | Price per extra name |
| iPostal1 | One business name per account, on Virtual Business Address or Virtual Office plans; a second business needs a second mailbox [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | One business name per account; business plans start at $14.99/mo [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) |
| Stable | Unlimited individual or business names [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Included [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| Virtual Post Mail | Recipients: 2 (Starter), 5 (Plus), 10 (Business), 20 (Premium) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) | $10/mo each ($5 on Premium) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) |
| PostScan Mail | Add names or businesses; each needs a Form 1583 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) | $5/mo per extra recipient or user [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| LegalZoom Virtual Mail | Recipients: 2 (Starter), 5 (Essentials), 15 (Premium) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) | $5/mo each [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Traveling Mailbox | Recipients, including business names: 3 (Basic), 5 (Extended), 10 (Small Business) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | — |
| US Global Mail | Recipients: 5 on Occasional, 10 on Scale [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | — |

US Global Mail generates a Form 1583 for each company or trust name and sends one e-signature request per name; your ID is uploaded once [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/15460453-usps-form-1583-update-what-s-changing-and-why).

## When do you need a new form?

- When information on the form changes. The applicant "must file an updated application" [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf), for example when the officer changes or the business moves.
- When an ID expires. IDs must be current, and mail centers certify every quarter that no ID on file is expired [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Anytime Mailbox gives an expired ID as an example of when you'll need a new form [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583).
- For each new location. iPostal1 requires a new Form 1583 for each mailbox location [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
If yours was sent back, see Form 1583 rejected: reasons and fixes.

## Where can you use the business address?
A mailbox address works as a company's mailing address, but Texas, Florida and California require a registered agent at a real in-state street address for the registered office. See virtual mailbox for an LLC and virtual mailbox for a bank account. If you're switching an existing business, the IRS change form is 8822-B [source](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-8822-b); see changing your address to a virtual mailbox.

## Links

- US Global Mail (no notary needed)
- Virtual Post Mail
- Stable (unlimited business names)
- BlueNotary (online notary)
- Notarize (online notary)

# Cheapest virtual mailbox by state
If you want a mailing address in a particular state, the cheapest option is usually an Anytime Mailbox location, because each local operator sets its own price. We went through every location Anytime Mailbox lists in Texas, Florida, Delaware, Wyoming, California and New York on November 23, 2026, and pulled out the lowest "starting from" price in each state and in the big cities.

## Lowest starting price in each state

| State | Locations listed | Cheapest location | Half of locations start at or below | Most expensive |
| Florida | 242 | $5.99/mo, Fort Walton Beach (Lewis Turner Blvd) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/florida) | about $10.50/mo | $69/mo |
| Delaware | 18 | $6.99/mo, Newark (Polly Drummond Shopping Center) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/delaware) | $9.99/mo | $15.99/mo |
| Texas | 290 | $7.99/mo, Austin (605 W 9th Street) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/texas) | $11.99/mo | $59.99/mo |
| Wyoming | 6 | $7.99/mo, Cheyenne (South Greeley Hwy) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/wyoming) | $9.99/mo | $19.99/mo |
| California | 397 | $7.99/mo, at several locations including Anaheim, Fresno and Laguna Niguel [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/california) | $9.99/mo | $75/mo |
| New York | 99 | $8.99/mo, East Setauket, Glen Cove and Plainview (all Long Island) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/new-york) | $11.99/mo | $84.99/mo |

Source: the "Starting from" price on each location card of Anytime Mailbox's state pages, checked November 23, 2026 (linked in each row). The middle and high columns use monthly prices only; one California location and three Brooklyn locations show only a yearly price ($149.99 to $399.99 a year) and are left out of those columns. "Starting from" is the location's cheapest plan; mail allowances and per-item fees differ by location, so open the location page before you sign up [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/).

## Big-city ranges
A big-city address costs more at the top end, but every one of these cities has locations around $10 a month.

| City | Locations | Starting prices |
| Austin, TX | 17 | $7.99 to $49.99/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/texas) |
| Houston, TX | 50 | $9.49 to $49.99/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/texas) |
| Dallas, TX | 25 | $9.99 to $49.99/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/texas) |
| Orlando, FL | 15 | $7.00 to $30/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/florida) |
| Tampa, FL | 9 | $8.99 to $26.99/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/florida) |
| Miami, FL | 22 | $9.99 to $49.99/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/florida) |
| Wilmington, DE | 6 | $8.99 to $14.99/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/delaware) |
| Cheyenne, WY | 4 | $7.99 to $19.99/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/wyoming) |
| Los Angeles, CA | 28 | $8.97 to $33/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/california) |
| San Francisco, CA | 10 | $9.99 to $19.99/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/california) |
| New York (Manhattan listings) | 17 | $9.99 to $54.99/mo [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/new-york) |
| Brooklyn, NY | 16 monthly + 3 yearly-only | $9.99 to $19.99/mo; yearly-only locations $149.99 to $399.99/yr [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa/new-york) |

Why the spread? Anytime Mailbox doesn't run the mailrooms; each location is an independent operator that sets its own plans and fees. More on that in Anytime Mailbox pricing.

## A cheap address isn't a registered office
People often want a Delaware, Wyoming or Texas address because they're forming an LLC there. A virtual mailbox can be the company's mailing address, but each state sets its own rules for the registered office, and they ask for more than a mail drop:

- Texas: the registered office "must be a physical address in Texas where the registered agent can be personally served with process during business hours. It cannot solely be the address of a mailbox service" [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/corp/formationfaqs.shtml).
- Wyoming: the registered office must be "a street address in Wyoming which shall be a physical location" where the registered agent, or a person with an agency relationship with the agent, "is physically present" to accept service [source](https://wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title17.pdf).
- Delaware: every LLC must maintain a registered office in Delaware and a registered agent "having a business office identical with such registered office" [source](https://delcode.delaware.gov/title6/c018/sc01/index.html).
- Florida: the registered agent's business address must be "identical to the address of the registered office" [source](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/605.0113), and the articles must give the agent's "street address in this state" [source](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/605.0201).
- California: the agent must be a California resident or a registered corporate agent, and the agent's "physical street address" is public record [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/business-programs/business-entities/faqs).
So the cheapest setup in these states is usually a registered agent plus a separate mailbox, or a mailbox plan that includes an agent. Virtual Post Mail has business addresses in Keller (TX), Brandon (FL), Claymont (DE) and Covina (CA), and includes a free registered agent in California, Delaware, Florida, Nevada and Texas on plans from $20 a month [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/). Details in Virtual Post Mail pricing and virtual mailbox for an LLC.

## Before you pick the $5.99 address

- Check the plan, not just the price. A low starting price often comes with a small mail allowance and per-scan fees. Compare what you'll actually open each month with the cheapest virtual mailbox guide.
- Add the Form 1583 cost. Every provider needs USPS Form 1583 before it can handle your mail; some charge for the notary. See Form 1583 and online notarization.
- Some providers publish one price list. Traveling Mailbox's pricing page shows a single $15 Basic plan with 35 page scans included [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953), and most of its customers use its home base in Sanford, NC [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) (Traveling Mailbox pricing).
- PhysicalAddress.com also has company-run addresses in several of these states, with starting prices of $9.98 in Dallas, Orlando and Wilmington, $10.98 in Laguna Beach and $19.98 on Wall Street, plus $7.98 in Boise and $8.98 in Las Vegas. It includes a registered agent with the account [source](https://physicaladdress.com/locations/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/registered-agent-service/). Details: PhysicalAddress.com pricing.

- PhysicalAddress.com

# Opus Virtual Offices vs Davinci Virtual
Both sell a business street address in an office building, with mail receipt and optional phone answering. The pricing models are opposite: Opus charges the same flat price at every location, while Davinci prices each building separately and adds a setup fee. Here's what each publishes, checked November 23, 2026.

## Side by side

| | Opus Virtual Offices | Davinci Virtual |
| Address only | $59/mo, 100+ locations [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/business-address/) | Priced per location; "starting at $50" [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/) |
| Address + live receptionist | $99/mo "all-inclusive," 650+ locations [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/business-address/) | Receptionist plans sold separately; the FAQ refers to Business and Premium plans and per-minute overage [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) |
| Setup fee | None: "no setup fee" on its Houston page [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/texas/houston/location-1323/) | Address setup fee "starts at $150," includes an online notary; location listings show "+ Discounted setup fee" [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/loc/us/texas/houston-virtual-offices/) |
| Minimum term | 3-month initial term, then month to month [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/texas/houston/location-1323/) [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/california/los-angeles/location-1362/) | 6-month commitment for location services, then month to month; 30 days' written notice to cancel [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) |
| Mail | "Professional Mail Receipt" and "Digital Mail Notification"; staff sign for UPS, FedEx and DHL packages [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/texas/houston/location-1323/) [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/business-address/) | Mail and package receipt; forwarding on request, postage extra, "rates vary by location" [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) |
| Mail forwarding fee | — | Varies by location [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) |
| Form 1583 | Required: two IDs and a notary; online notarization accepted [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/business-address/) | Notarized form required before setup; online notary included in the setup fee [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) |
| Registered agent | $10/mo add-on, in the state of your office [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/services/) | — |

## Davinci address prices in three cities
Davinci's city pages list every building with its monthly address price. On November 23, 2026:

| City | Davinci listings | Davinci address price | Opus address / all-inclusive |
| Houston | 57 | $50 to $199/mo; 17 of the 57 at $50 [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/loc/us/texas/houston-virtual-offices/) | $59 / $99 (3050 Post Oak Blvd) [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/texas/houston/location-1323/) |
| Miami | 34 | $50 to $200/mo [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/loc/us/florida/miami-virtual-offices/) | $59 / $99 (848 Brickell Ave) [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/florida/miami/location-1285/) |
| Los Angeles | 30 | $50 to $185/mo [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/loc/us/california/los-angeles-virtual-offices/) | $59 / $99 (626 Wilshire Blvd) [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/california/los-angeles/location-1362/) |

Davinci prices exclude the setup fee and any receptionist plan [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq). Opus's New York (26 Broadway) page shows the same $59 and $99 prices [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/new-york/new-york/location-1450/).

## First-year cost, Houston

- Davinci, cheapest Houston address: $50 × 12 = $600, plus the setup fee (the FAQ says it starts at $150) [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/loc/us/texas/houston-virtual-offices/) [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq). That's $750 or more, with no phone answering.
- Opus address only: $59 × 12 = $708, no setup fee [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/texas/houston/location-1323/).
- Opus all-inclusive: $99 × 12 = $1,188, including a live receptionist on weekdays, a business phone and fax number, and voicemail and fax to email [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/services/).
If you only need an address, the cheapest Davinci building and Opus come out close in year one, and Davinci gets cheaper from year two because the setup fee is one-time. If you want calls answered, Opus's flat $99 is simpler to price; Davinci quotes receptionist service separately [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq).

## Opus add-ons
Opus lists these upgrades on its services page [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/services/): toll-free number, outbound calling app, texting, conference bridge, custom business email, registered agent and call recording at $10 a month each; extra extensions at $25 a month each; supervised transfer and message taking at $50 a month each. Receptionist hours are 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. weekdays (8 to 5 in the Pacific time zone) [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/services/).

## Do you need a virtual office at all?
Both of these cost several times what a virtual mailbox does. If you need a street address and scanned mail but not a receptionist or a lobby listing, a virtual mailbox starts under $10 a month (see virtual office vs virtual mailbox and the cheapest address by state). Neither Opus nor Davinci publishes mail scanning prices on the pages we checked; if you want mail opened and scanned, see virtual mailbox pricing compared.

## How the estimate works

- For each service we try every plan with published allowances and pick the cheapest for your numbers: plan price plus extra-item, extra-scan, check and extra-name fees. Monthly billing, standard address, before postage and sales tax.
- Checks are assumed to go to your bank together in one shipment a month.
- iPostal1, PostScan Mail and Anytime Mailbox prices are "from" prices: the mail center you pick can charge more. Anytime Mailbox lets each location set its own plans and fees, so we can only show its starting price.
- Where a provider doesn't publish a fee (for example PostScan Mail's check deposit), the estimate says so and leaves it out.
- Fee sources: price table, check deposit fees, forwarding fees and each provider page linked above.

# Virtual office vs virtual mailbox
Both give you a real street address that isn't your home. A virtual mailbox is built around mail: it scans envelopes, opens letters on request and forwards what you need. A virtual office is built around looking like an office: a business phone number, someone to answer it, a name in the building lobby, and rooms you can book. Here's what that difference costs, from the providers' own price lists on November 23, 2026.

## The same company, both products
iPostal1 sells both, so it's the cleanest comparison. Same addresses, same mail handling; the virtual office adds a company name, phone and fax:

| iPostal1 plan | Monthly | Yearly | Mail items / month | Adds |
| Virtual Mailing Address | $9.99 | $99 | 30 | Up to 6 recipient names, no company name [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Virtual Office | $39.99 | $399 | 60 | 1 company name, local phone and fax number, voicemail [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php) |
| Virtual Office | $49.99 | $499 | 120 | Same, more mail [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php) |
| Virtual Office (toll-free) | $59.99 / $69.99 | $599 / $699 | 120 / 240 | Toll-free phone and fax [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php) |

Prices are iPostal1's starting prices; they vary by Standard, Select, Premium or Prestige location [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php). Calls and faxes on the virtual office plans are billed per minute and per page (for example, $0.015 a minute for inbound calls to a local number), with 250 voicemail minutes a month free [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php).

## What each kind of product includes

| | Virtual mailbox | Virtual office |
| Street address | Yes, with a PMB or suite number | Yes, usually an office building suite [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/business-address/) |
| Mail scanning | Core feature; e.g. 35 page scans included on Traveling Mailbox Basic [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | Mail receipt and notification; scanning prices aren't published by Opus or Davinci on the pages we checked [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/texas/houston/location-1323/) [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) |
| Phone number and receptionist | No (iPostal1 offers call answering as an add-on from $49/mo) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Included at Opus's $99 tier (live receptionist on weekdays) [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/services/); separate plans at Davinci [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) |
| Meeting rooms, lobby listing | No | Davinci: lobby and directory listings at most locations, day offices and conference rooms by the hour [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq). Opus: meeting rooms available [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/texas/houston/location-1323/) |
| Drop-off and pickup in person | Depends on provider: Virtual Post Mail offers no pickup [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/); some iPostal1 locations charge a pickup fee [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Davinci locations act as a "drop off & pick up point for clientele" [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) |
| Setup fee and term | Usually none; Traveling Mailbox is month to month [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | Davinci: setup fee from $150 and a 6-month commitment [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq). Opus: no setup fee, 3-month initial term [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/virtual-office/texas/houston/location-1323/) |
| Form 1583 | Required for both: anyone receiving mail through a commercial mail receiving agency signs USPS Form 1583 [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Opus asks for two IDs and a notary [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/business-address/); Davinci includes an online notary in its setup fee [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) |

## Price ladder, per year

| Option | What you get | Cost for 12 months |
| iPostal1 Virtual Mailing Address | Address, 30 items/mo, envelope images | $99 paid yearly [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Traveling Mailbox Basic | Address, 40 envelopes and 35 page scans/mo | $15 × 12 = $180 [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Virtual Post Mail Starter | Address, 25 envelopes and 10 content scans/mo, free registered agent in 5 states | $20 × 12 = $240 [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) |
| iPostal1 Virtual Office | Address + company name + phone/fax | $399 paid yearly [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php) |
| Davinci, cheapest Houston address | Office-building address, mail receipt | $50 × 12 = $600 + setup fee from $150 [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/loc/us/texas/houston-virtual-offices/) [source](https://www.davincivirtual.com/faq) |
| Opus address only | Office-building address, mail receipt | $59 × 12 = $708 [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/business-address/) |
| Opus all-inclusive | Address + live receptionist + phone/fax | $99 × 12 = $1,188 [source](https://www.opusvirtualoffices.com/business-address/) |

Going from a basic virtual mailbox to a virtual office costs roughly $300 to $1,000 more a year. That money buys phone service and a more office-like address, not better mail handling: the mailbox plans above publish more detail on scans and forwarding than the virtual offices do.

## Which one you need

- Virtual mailbox: you need an address for mail, an LLC's mailing address, or to read mail while traveling. Start with the cheapest virtual mailbox or the cheapest address in your state.
- Virtual office: clients call you, visit you, or look you up, and you want a receptionist or a room to meet in. Compare Opus vs Davinci.
- Neither replaces a registered agent in states that require the agent to be physically present at the registered office; see virtual mailbox for an LLC.
- Bank account? Banks have their own address rules; see can I use a virtual mailbox for my bank account?

# Can you use a virtual mailbox for a bank account?
Usually yes as a mailing address, and usually no as your home address or your company's street address. Banks have to collect a real street address under federal rules, and a virtual mailbox is easy to spot because every one carries a "PMB" or "#" number. Here's what the rule says, what one business-banking platform publishes, and what mailbox companies tell their own customers.

## What federal law asks banks to collect
Under the Customer Identification Program rule, a bank must get an address from each new customer before opening an account [source](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1020/subpart-B/section-1020.220):

- For a person: "a residential or business street address." Someone with no street address can give an APO/FPO box or the street address of next of kin or another contact person.
- For a company (corporation, LLC, partnership, trust): "a principal place of business, local office, or other physical location."
The rule also has banks set "risk-based procedures" to verify identity, so each bank decides how to treat a commercial mail address [source](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1020/subpart-B/section-1020.220). That's why answers differ from bank to bank.

## Why a bank can tell it's a virtual mailbox
Virtual mailbox companies are Commercial Mail Receiving Agencies (CMRAs) under USPS rules. Each CMRA registers with its Post Office, and mail to its customers must show "PMB" (private mailbox) or "#" and a box number, for example "10 MAIN ST PMB 234" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). So the address itself tells a bank it isn't where you live or work.

## Address field by address field: one business-banking platform's published rules
Mercury, a business-banking platform, publishes unusually specific rules, so it's a useful example of how the fields get split. Mercury notes it is a fintech company, with banking services provided by partner banks [source](https://support.mercury.com/hc/en-us/articles/28769699533588-Company-address-requirements):

| Field | Virtual mailbox accepted? | What Mercury says |
| Company legal address | Not a P.O. box | Must be a physical U.S. address, such as the one on your formation documents. If it's a "virtual address, mail center, or registered agent," Mercury may ask you to verify your physical address [source](https://support.mercury.com/hc/en-us/articles/28769699533588-Company-address-requirements) |
| Company physical address (where you work) | No | "We don't accept a P.O. box, virtual address, commercial mail receiving agency, mail center, or registered agent address." A residential address is fine if you don't have an office [source](https://support.mercury.com/hc/en-us/articles/28769699533588-Company-address-requirements) |
| Beneficial owner's home address | No | "PO boxes, mail drops, and commercial mail-receiving or virtual address services can't be used" [source](https://support.mercury.com/hc/en-us/articles/28770467511060-Eligibility-and-requirements-for-opening-a-Mercury-account) |
| Mailing address (for cards) | Physical, deliverable address | Must be "a physical address" deliverable by USPS; statements are digital, not mailed [source](https://support.mercury.com/hc/en-us/articles/28769699533588-Company-address-requirements) |

Stable, a virtual mailbox provider, tells its customers the same thing for Mercury: don't use the Stable mailbox address as your legal address or where you work, but you can enter it as the company mailing address and use it as your mailing address once the account is open. Stable's separate registered agent address is accepted as the legal address [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/9330705-using-your-stable-address-with-mercury).

## What mailbox providers tell their customers

- US Global Mail: "Yes and No!" Most banks and card companies let customers use the address as a personal address, but "some banks have recently started asking for a personal address, which is not a CMRA" address. In that case customers give a friend's, family member's or company's address as the personal address and the US Global Mail address as the mailing address [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022325-what-can-or-can-t-the-us-global-mail-address-be-used-for).
- Virtual Post Mail: "A virtual mailbox won't work for banking, lease agreements, or utility bills." It sells a leased office address (TruLease, $400 to $700/mo) and a residential address (TruResidence, $300 to $600/mo) for those cases [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/trulease/pricing/) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/truresidence/pricing/).
- Stable: treats its mailbox address as "a mail-forwarding address" for Mercury's legal-address field, but fine for the mailing-address field [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/9330705-using-your-stable-address-with-mercury).

## A setup that usually works

- Home or physical address: use where you actually live (or your real office). For a remote LLC, Mercury accepts a residential address as the company's physical address [source](https://support.mercury.com/hc/en-us/articles/28769699533588-Company-address-requirements).
- Legal address for an LLC: the address on your formation documents. A registered agent address is one option some banks accept; see virtual mailbox for an LLC for what states require, and Virtual Post Mail, which includes a free registered agent in five states [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/registered-agent/pricing/).
- Mailing address: your virtual mailbox, if the bank allows it, so statements, cards and checks get scanned.
- Ask first. Banks set their own procedures under the federal rule [source](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1020/subpart-B/section-1020.220), so ask the bank which fields can hold a PMB address before you apply.
Don't paper over the address. Writing a mailbox address as "Suite" instead of "PMB" doesn't make it a street address. USPS rules say a CMRA address can't combine the building's suite number with your box number, and mail without the PMB or # can be returned to the sender [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).

## Receiving bank mail at a virtual mailbox: what it costs
Once the account is open, the mailbox handles statements, new cards and checks. Check deposit fees range from no handling fee at US Global Mail (you cover shipping) [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) to $10 per check at Earth Class Mail without its subscription [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html); the full table is on virtual mailbox check deposit fees. Virtual Post Mail charges $10 per deposit plus $1.50 per extra check [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/), and Traveling Mailbox $4.95 per check plus postage [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).

- US Global Mail
- Virtual Post Mail

# PostScan Mail pricing, every fee explained
PostScan Mail's Starter plan is advertised "as low as $10" a month, but that's the price at its cheapest addresses. The same plan costs up to $45 at its most expensive ones, and opening a letter costs $2 on top. Here is the full price list as PostScan published it on November 22, 2026.

## The three personal and small-business plans
PostScan sells the same three plans everywhere, but the price depends on which address (location tier) you pick. The lowest and highest prices on the pricing page are below [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).

| Plan | Monthly billing | Annual billing | Mail items / month | Free open-and-scans / month | Recipients |
| Starter | $10 to $45/mo | $100 to $450/yr ($8.33 to $37.50/mo) | 30 | None (monthly) · none (annual) | 1 (monthly) · 2 (annual) |
| Standard | $20 to $55/mo | $200 to $550/yr ($16.67 to $45.83/mo) | 60 | 5 (monthly) · 10 (annual) | 2 (monthly) · 3 (annual) |
| Premium | $30 to $65/mo | $300 to $650/yr ($25 to $54.17/mo) | 120 | 10 (monthly) · 20 (annual) | 4 (monthly) · 6 (annual) |

All from PostScan Mail's pricing page [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html). "Mail items" means letters or packages. Free open-and-scans cover up to 10 pages each, then $0.25 per extra page. Annual billing is advertised as "2 months free," and on this page it also adds recipients and free scans.
Which price will you pay? PostScan shows the price after you pick an address. Use the cheapest tier's numbers ($10 / $20 / $30) only if your chosen address is in that tier. Our comparison table uses the lowest advertised price for every provider, so it shows the $10 figure.

## Every per-use fee

| Fee | Price |
| Mail item over your plan's limit | $0.50 per envelope or package |
| Open and scan (beyond free ones) | $2.00 per envelope up to 10 pages, then $0.25 per page |
| Forwarding | $2.00 for the first item, $0.50 per additional item, plus shipping |
| Mail storage | Free for 14 days (30 days on an annual plan), then $0.05 per envelope per day |
| Package storage | Free for 3 days (7 days on an annual plan), then $0.10 per pound per day |
| Shredding | $1.00 per item for the first 10 pages, then $0.15 per page |
| Extra recipient or user | $5.00/month each |
| Extra mailbox (address) | $5.00/month each |
| Oversized package (over 25 lb or 110" length + girth) | $0.25 per pound |
| AI mail summaries | 10 free a month, then $0.25 each |
| HIPAA compliance | $25.00/month billed annually, then $0.50 per received item |
| Local pickup | Free at most locations; "some may charge a nominal fee" |

Source: PostScan Mail pricing page, "Additional Fees" [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html). Discarding junk mail is free and unlimited [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
The storage numbers differ by page. The pricing page says mail is free for 14 days on monthly plans (30 on annual). The FAQ says "the first 30 days of mail storage are free" and packages get 7 days, without mentioning the billing period [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html). If you're on monthly billing, plan around the shorter window.

## Junk mail counts toward your limit
"Yes, junk mail counts towards your account limit," PostScan's FAQ says, adding that some addresses may filter out "Presorted Standard" mail [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html). That matters on Starter: 30 items includes catalogs and credit card offers. Traveling Mailbox and Virtual Post Mail both leave junk out of the count (see Traveling Mailbox pricing and Virtual Post Mail pricing).

## What it costs at real mail volumes
At the cheapest location tier ($10 / $20 / $30 monthly), counting junk in the item total, with each opened letter under 10 pages [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html):

| Items / month (incl. junk) | Opened | Starter $10 | Standard $20 | Premium $30 |
| 20 | 3 | $10 + 3 × $2 = $16 | $20 | $30 |
| 40 | 10 | $10 + 10 × $0.50 + 10 × $2 = $35 | $20 + 5 × $2 = $30 | $30 |
| 80 | 15 | $10 + 50 × $0.50 + 15 × $2 = $65 | $20 + 20 × $0.50 + 10 × $2 = $50 | $30 + 5 × $2 = $40 |

If you open more than about 5 letters a month, Standard usually beats Starter. Shredding and forwarding are extra in every row. At a higher-priced address, add the tier difference (up to $35/month) to each column.

## Business and enterprise plans

| Plan | Price | Incoming mail / month | Free open-and-scans | Recipients |
| Startup | $100/mo, or $1,000 billed annually | 360 | 60 | 10 |
| Business | $300/mo, or $3,000 billed annually | 1,200 | 200 | 20 |
| Enterprise | $600/mo, or $6,000 billed annually | 3,000 | 500 | 30 |

Source: PostScan Mail pricing page [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).

## Package lockers (no mail scanning)

- Basic Locker, $4.95/month: $3 processing per item, $2 forwarding per item, packages stored free for 7 days, then $0.10 per pound per day [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- Premium Locker, $9.95/month: $2 processing per item, $1 forwarding per item, 14 days free storage, then $0.10 per pound per day [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).

## Signing up, Form 1583 and canceling

- Notary: you fill out and notarize USPS Form 1583 and provide two IDs. PostScan's online notary partners charge $20 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html). Compare no-notary providers on our Form 1583 page.
- Each extra name needs its own Form 1583, and the $5/month fee applies [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).
- Canceling: close the account under "Subscription & Billing." Stored mail is discarded, received mail is held for 6 months "per CMRA regulations," and after that new mail is returned to sender [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).
- USPS change of address can't redirect mail away from a CMRA, so you'll need to tell senders yourself when you leave [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).

## Who PostScan Mail fits
People who want a specific city address with free local pickup [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html), who mostly look at envelope images, and who don't get much junk mail. If you want most letters opened, the $2 scans add up fast. See Traveling Mailbox vs PostScan Mail for a side-by-side.

- PostScan Mail

# Traveling Mailbox pricing: which plan to pick
Traveling Mailbox has three flat-priced plans: $15, $25 and $55 a month. Unlike most providers, it doesn't charge per open-and-scan. Each plan includes a set number of page scans, and you pay small overage fees past that. Here's what each plan covers and the point where upgrading saves money, from the pricing page as of November 22, 2026.

## The three plans

| Plan | Price | Incoming envelopes / month | Page scans / month | Mailbox recipients |
| Basic | $15/mo | 40 | 35 | 3 |
| Extended | $25/mo | 100 | 80 | 5 |
| Small Business | $55/mo | 200 | 180 | 10 |

Source: Traveling Mailbox pricing page [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953). All plans include free shredding, unlimited cloud storage, and plan changes at any time. Junk mail you mark as junk "won't count towards your plan limits" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).

- Envelope scans vs page scans: every envelope that arrives is scanned on the outside, and that doesn't use your page-scan allowance. Page scans are for opening and scanning the contents [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- Rollover: the plan cards say "Your Scans Rollover" on all three plans, but the footnote limits rollover of unused envelope and page scans to the Extended, Small Business and Enterprise plans [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953). Count on rollover only if you're on Extended or higher.
- Annual billing: the FAQ says there are no contracts. You can pay month to month, or "subscribe to an annual plan to get 2 months free," and annual plans "are refundable on a monthly schedule" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- Minors can be added to an account and don't count toward the recipient limit [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).

## Every other fee

| Fee | Price |
| Extra envelope over the allowance | $0.25 each |
| Extra page scan over the allowance | $0.50 per page |
| Mail and package forwarding | Postage + $2 per shipment (not per piece) |
| Check deposit by mail | $4.95 per check + postage |
| Envelope storage | Free for 30 days, then shredded unless you put it on hold; holds are $1 per envelope per month |
| Package storage | Free for 30 days, then $0.10 per pound per day |
| Shredding | Free |
| Military discount | 10% off monthly for active-duty military and veterans |

Source: Traveling Mailbox pricing page and FAQ [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953). The page also mentions "Membership Plans" to keep an account open when you're not traveling, without listing a price.

## When to upgrade: the break-even points
Monthly cost = plan price + $0.25 per envelope over the allowance + $0.50 per page over the allowance [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953). Junk you mark as junk is excluded.

| Envelopes / pages per month | Basic $15 | Extended $25 | Small Business $55 |
| 30 / 25 | $15 | $25 | $55 |
| 50 / 45 | $15 + 10 × $0.25 + 10 × $0.50 = $22.50 | $25 | $55 |
| 60 / 55 | $15 + 20 × $0.25 + 20 × $0.50 = $30 | $25 | $55 |
| 150 / 130 | $15 + 110 × $0.25 + 95 × $0.50 = $90 | $25 + 50 × $0.25 + 50 × $0.50 = $62.50 | $55 (within limits) |

In the 150-envelope row Small Business ($55) is the cheapest. Rule of thumb: if you regularly go over Basic by more than about 13 envelopes and 13 pages, Extended costs less. Rollover on Extended (but per the footnote, not Basic) helps if your mail comes in uneven months [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).

## Form 1583 without a notary
After you subscribe, you complete USPS Form 1583 inside your account, then "schedule an appointment with us to verify your form. A notary is not required" [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-do-i-complete-the-usps-form-1583/). That saves the $20 to $25 online-notary fee charged at some other providers (see our Form 1583 guide).

## How Traveling Mailbox compares

- Versus PostScan Mail: PostScan's Starter starts at $10 but charges $2 for each open-and-scan and counts junk mail [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html). See PostScan Mail pricing and the head-to-head.
- Versus Virtual Post Mail: VPM's Starter is $20 with 25 envelopes and 10 content scans [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/). Details on Virtual Post Mail pricing.
- Versus US Global Mail: see US Global Mail vs Traveling Mailbox.

- Traveling Mailbox
