# USPS Form 1583 and online notarization
Short answer: No, USPS doesn't require a notary. Since May 1, 2024, you can sign Form 1583 on a live video call with the mail center's staff or before a U.S.-commissioned notary. Traveling Mailbox, Stable and US Global Mail verify you without a notary; iPostal1's online notary costs $25 and PostScan Mail's partner notary $20. [source](https://about.usps.com/postal-bulletin/2024/pb22648/html/updt_001.htm) [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-do-i-complete-the-usps-form-1583/) [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html)

Form 1583, "Application for Delivery of Mail Through Agent," is the form that lets a virtual mailbox company receive your mail. Whether you need a notary depends on the provider, not on USPS.

## Does USPS require a notary for Form 1583?
A USPS rule change took effect on May 1, 2024. The applicant must sign in one of two ways:
"sign or confirm his or her signature in the physical or virtual (in real-time audio and video) presence of the CMRA owner or manager or authorized employee, or acknowledge his or her signature in the physical or virtual (in real-time audio and video) presence of a notary public commissioned in a United States state, territory, possession, or the District of Columbia." [source](https://about.usps.com/postal-bulletin/2024/pb22648/html/updt_001.htm)
So a live video call with the mail center's own staff is enough under USPS rules. A notary is one option, not a requirement, and if you do use one, the notary must hold a U.S. commission [source](https://about.usps.com/postal-bulletin/2024/pb22648/html/updt_001.htm). The current form says the same thing [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf).

## Which providers need a notary?

| Provider | Notary needed? | Cost to sign | How it works |
| Traveling Mailbox | No | Included | Fill out the form in your account, then do a video appointment where staff check your IDs and you e-sign. "A notary is not required." [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-do-i-complete-the-usps-form-1583/) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953) |
| Stable | No | Included | Stable pre-fills the form and checks your IDs and an ID verification photo, which takes "about 1 business day or less" [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8236356-why-are-my-ids-being-verified-for-the-usps-1583) |
| US Global Mail | No | Included | Pre-filled form. "No need to find a notary separately — we'll complete your identity verification online." [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/usps-form-1583/?via=michelle) |
| Earth Class Mail (LegalZoom) | Optional | LegalZoom calls its notary option a "free notarization service" (2026-11-21) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/personal/virtual-mail-overview.html) | Verify yourself online (ID photos, a selfie, e-sign) or use a partner online notary. Without a Social Security number, you have to use the notary [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/25619300469143-Activate-your-Virtual-Mail-service). Billing "starts upon account creation" whether or not the form is approved [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360035551454-Acceptable-Identification-for-USPS-1583-Non-SSN-Holders) |
| iPostal1 | Yes, unless you sign in person at the mail center | $25 online notary | Many mail centers let you sign in person (some charge). Customers outside the U.S. must use the online notary [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) |
| PostScan Mail | Yes | $20 partner online notary | Notarize online or in person, then submit through the platform [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) |
| Anytime Mailbox | Yes | — | Upload two IDs, then "complete and notarize" the form. The "Use Online Notary" button routes you to a video call with a licensed notary [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq) |
| PhysicalAddress.com | Yes, unless you sign at one of its locations | Not published | After signup it emails a pre-filled form and a link to a partner online notary that "supports international clients." You can also sign with a notary or in person at one of its locations. Mail is not scanned, forwarded or uploaded until the form is completed [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-do-i-sign-up-for-physicaladdress-com/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/what-is-the-usps-1583/) |

## Which IDs do you need for Form 1583?
You need two IDs: one with your photo and one showing your current address [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq). PostScan Mail's list is typical:

- Photo ID: U.S. driver's license or state ID, passport or passport card, permanent resident card, certificate of naturalization, U.S. military or university ID, and a few others [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html)
- Address ID: driver's license (if you didn't use it as your photo ID), voter or vehicle registration, vehicle or home insurance policy, lease, mortgage or deed of trust [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html)
Not accepted: Social Security cards, credit cards and birth certificates [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/faq). One license can't count as both IDs [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).

## Things that trip people up

- Form 1583 doesn't forward your mail. It only authorizes the mail center. You still have to file a change of address or update your senders [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953).
- Every name needs its own form. Traveling Mailbox requires a form and two IDs "for each name that mail will be received under" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953). PostScan charges $5 a month per extra recipient [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).
- Switching locations means a new form. Traveling Mailbox requires a new Form 1583 for every recipient when you move to a different location [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/do-i-need-a-new-usps-form-1583-when-switching-addresses/).

## An independent online notary
If your provider requires a notarized form, some send you to their own partner and others let you bring a form that was notarized separately. Confirm which yours accepts before you pay.
BlueNotary is an online notary that says it can notarize Form 1583 over a live video session: you upload the form and an ID, then meet a commissioned online notary. It says a notary acknowledgment can take less than 10 minutes [source](https://bluenotary.us/usps-form-1583-the-essential-guide-for-mailbox-services/). Its fee schedule lists on-demand notarization at $25 for one stamp [source](https://help.bluenotary.us/en/article/fee-schedule-for-business-individuals-1kg94y4/).
Notarize, which now operates under the Proof name, also offers online notarization of Form 1583: you upload the form, verify your identity, and meet a notary on a live video call. Its Form 1583 page lists the first notary seal at $25 and says signers complete their notarization in less than 10 minutes on average, with notaries available 24/7 [source](https://forms.notarize.com/pages/form/ps-1583).

# Virtual mailbox vs PO Box
Short answer: A USPS PO Box is usually cheaper, $31 to $170 per six months for the smallest box depending on ZIP Code, but you collect mail in person and the address reads "PO Box." A virtual mailbox, from $9.99 a month at iPostal1, gives a street address with a PMB number, accepts packages and scans your mail. [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/Notice123.htm) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php)

A PO Box is usually cheaper, but you have to go to the Post Office to check it, and the address says "PO Box." A virtual mailbox costs more, gives you a street address with a "PMB" number, and scans your mail so you can read it from anywhere. Here's how the costs and the rules compare, from USPS's own price list and mail manual.

## Side by side

| | USPS PO Box | Virtual mailbox |
| Smallest-box / entry price | $31 to $170 per 6 months for the smallest box, set by ZIP Code [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/Notice123.htm) | iPostal1 $9.99/mo or $99/yr [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php); PostScan Mail from $10/mo or $100/yr [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html); Traveling Mailbox $15/mo [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Address format | "PO Box 1234," or at some Post Offices the Post Office's street address with "#1234" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) | Provider's street address with "PMB 1234" or "#1234" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) |
| UPS, FedEx and other private carriers | Only at Post Offices that offer the street-addressing option, and only if you sign up for it [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) | Yes, packages are accepted (for example, Traveling Mailbox "can receive any size package") [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| Reading mail remotely | No scanning; you collect mail in person | Envelope scans on arrival; contents scanned on request [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Sign-up | PS Form 1093, two IDs shown in person at the Post Office [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) | PS Form 1583 and two IDs, notarized or verified by the provider (details) |
| Forwarding | A PO Box "may not be used when the primary purpose is to have the USPS forward or transfer mail to another address free of charge" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) | Paid forwarding anywhere; e.g. postage + $2 per shipment at Traveling Mailbox [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |

## How much does a PO Box cost?
USPS prices a PO Box by box size and by the "fee group" of its ZIP Code. Areas served by a competing private mailbox provider are "Competitive" (groups C30 to C44); the rest are "Market Dominant" (groups 1 to 7) [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/Notice123.htm). Prices per 6-month period, effective October 4, 2026:

| Box size (front opening) | Market Dominant locations | Competitive locations |
| 1 (3" × 5.5") | $31 to $81 | $80 to $170 |
| 2 (5" × 5.5") | $41 to $118 | $103 to $225 |
| 3 (11" × 5.5") | $60 to $206 | $161 to $395 |
| 4 (11" × 11") | $90 to $355 | $193 to $452 |
| 5 (22.5" × 12") | $156 to $553 | $270 to $677 |

Fees: USPS Notice 123 price list, "PO Box Service," semi-annual tables [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/Notice123.htm). Box dimensions: DMM 508.4.1.3 [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). To find your ZIP Code's fee group, USPS points to its PO Box page or your local Post Office [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/po-boxes.htm).

- Per year, the smallest box runs $62 to $340 (two 6-month periods), depending on where you live [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/Notice123.htm).
- New customers at Competitive locations get 13 months for a 12-month payment and pay no deposit for the first two keys [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).
- Keys and locks: $6 deposit per key, $14 per extra or replacement key after the first two, $30 lock replacement or late-payment fee [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/Notice123.htm).
- Three-month terms exist at some Post Offices if you set up automatic renewal (smallest box: $21 to $50 Market Dominant, $46 to $98 Competitive) [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/Notice123.htm) [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).
- Free PO Boxes (Group E) exist only for people whose address USPS won't deliver to, under specific conditions [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).
- Refunds: cancel in the first 3 months of a 6-month period and you get half back; after that, nothing [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).

## The street-address option at some Post Offices
At Competitive locations, you can sign a customer agreement to use the Post Office's street address with your box number, written like "123 Main Street #4567." With that option you can also get packages from private carriers at the box, within USPS size and weight limits (70 lb, 130 inches length plus girth) [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). If your Post Office offers it, this gives you most of what a basic virtual mailbox address does, except scanning and forwarding.

## Where neither address works

- Your LLC's registered office: Texas says a registered office "cannot solely be the address of a mailbox service" [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/corp/formationfaqs.shtml). More in virtual mailbox for an LLC.
- The IRS physical address line: Form SS-4 tells you not to enter a P.O. box as the physical location on line 5 [source](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iss4).
- A bank's home or business street address: federal rules require a street address for individuals and a physical location for companies [source](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1020/subpart-B/section-1020.220), and some banks refuse PO boxes and virtual addresses in those fields [source](https://support.mercury.com/hc/en-us/articles/28769699533588-Company-address-requirements). See can I use a virtual mailbox for my bank account?
Both work as a mailing address in most of those places, and the IRS uses your SS-4 mailing address "on all tax returns" [source](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iss4).

## Should you choose a PO Box or a virtual mailbox?

- PO Box: you live near the Post Office, get mostly letters, and want the lowest price. Check whether your Post Office offers the street-address option if you get UPS or FedEx deliveries [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).
- Virtual mailbox: you travel, live abroad, or want mail scanned and forwarded. A full-time traveler can't check a PO Box; see mail for full-time RVers and living abroad.
- Lowest-cost virtual options: see the cheapest virtual mailbox, PostScan Mail pricing and Traveling Mailbox pricing.

- iPostal1
- Traveling Mailbox
- US Global Mail

# Virtual Post Mail pricing
Virtual Post Mail (VPM) sells three different things: a regular virtual mailbox ($20 to $90 a month), a leased office address called TruLease, and a residential address called TruResidence. The mailbox plans are the ones most people need, and they come with a free registered agent in California, Delaware, Florida, Nevada and Texas. Here's every published price, as of November 22, 2026.

## Virtual mailbox plans

| | Starter | Plus | Business | Premium |
| Price | $20/mo | $35/mo | $60/mo | $90/mo |
| Envelope scans (incoming mail) | 25 | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Extra mail piece | $0.50 | Free | Free | Free |
| Content scans included (up to 30 pages each) | 10 | 50 | 100 | 150 |
| Users | 1 | 5 | 10 | 20 |
| Recipients (names you get mail under) | 2 | 5 | 10 | 20 |
| Extra recipient | $10/mo | $10/mo | $10/mo | $5/mo |
| Free package storage | 15 days | 15 days | 15 days | 30 days |
| Automated check deposit | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| HIPAA BAA | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Free registered agent | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

Source: VPM virtual mailbox pricing page [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/). The page lists only monthly prices. It advertises no setup fees, no contracts, no cancellation fees and a 30-day money-back guarantee [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/).

## Fees on every plan

| Fee | Price |
| Extra content scan | $3 per scan over the included ones (covers the first 30 pages), then $0.25 per page |
| Check deposit by mail | $10 per deposit, including one check and USPS First-Class with tracking; $1.50 per additional check in the same deposit |
| Forwarding | Varies with destination, weight and size |
| Mail storage | 30 days free |
| Shredding | "No additional fee" |
| Junk mail | Obvious junk is sorted out automatically and doesn't count toward your quota |

Source: VPM virtual mailbox pricing page and its FAQ section [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/). VPM's check deposit uses your bank's mail-in deposit service; it doesn't offer electronic deposits [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/). Mail pickup isn't offered on any mailbox plan [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/).

## What it costs at real mail volumes
Plan price + $0.50 per piece over 25 (Starter only) + $3 per content scan over the included number [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/). Junk is excluded.

| Pieces / month | Opened and scanned | Starter $20 | Plus $35 |
| 20 | 5 | $20 | $35 |
| 40 | 10 | $20 + 15 × $0.50 = $27.50 | $35 |
| 40 | 15 | $20 + 15 × $0.50 + 5 × $3 = $42.50 | $35 |

The jump from Starter to Plus pays off once you open more than about 12 letters a month, or get more than 55 pieces. For a cheaper flat plan with more envelopes included, Traveling Mailbox's $15 Basic covers 40 envelopes and 35 page scans [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) (see Traveling Mailbox pricing).

## The free registered agent: what's covered

- States: California, Nevada, Delaware, Florida and Texas [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/registered-agent/pricing/).
- Conditions: your mailbox address has to be in the same state as the registered agent service, the business must be registered in that state, and the business must be added as a recipient on your mailbox. Extra recipient fees apply if that puts you over your plan's free recipients [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/registered-agent/pricing/).
- What VPM does: receives "legal, tax, and corporate compliance documents for the company," and scans served documents the same day. "We do not handle any filings on your behalf" [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/registered-agent/).
For comparison: Stable charges $25/month per state for its registered agent add-on, and a Stable plan is required [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing). iPostal1 charges $99/year with any business plan [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php). US Global Mail says it doesn't offer registered agent service [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022325-what-can-or-can-t-the-us-global-mail-address-be-used-for). Why a mailbox by itself can't be your registered office is covered in virtual mailbox for an LLC.

## TruLease and TruResidence: when a mailbox isn't enough
VPM says plainly that its mailbox address "is not a physical address," and that "a virtual mailbox won't work for banking, lease agreements, or utility bills" [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/). It sells two pricier products for those uses:

| Product | Price | What you get |
| TruLease Standard | $700/mo, 1-year contract, billed monthly | Office lease (1 tenant), $1,800 security deposit, proof of funds for 12 months' rent required; CA or FL offices [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/trulease/pricing/) |
| TruLease Annual | $400/mo, $4,800 billed annually | Office lease, no security deposit or proof of funds; CA, DE or FL offices [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/trulease/pricing/) |
| TruRes Essentials | $600/mo, month-to-month | Residential address in CA or SD, 2 recipients, mail processed weekly; leasing is an add-on [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/truresidence/pricing/) |
| TruRes Premium+ | $300/mo, $3,600 billed annually | Residential address in CA, FL, NV, SD or TX, 5 recipients; leasing is an add-on [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/truresidence/pricing/) |

TruLease requires incorporation documents, an EIN, proof the signer is authorized, and a notarized Form 1583 [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/trulease/pricing/). TruResidence's optional lease adds a $1,200 deposit and rent that "varies by address" [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/truresidence/pricing/). VPM says TruLease "does NOT guarantee outcomes" for any particular use [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/trulease/pricing/).
Before paying $300 or more a month, read can I use a virtual mailbox for my bank account?: some banks only want a home address for the owner, which you may already have.

## Form 1583
VPM requires "a notarized Form 1583 and two IDs" before it processes mail; documents are processed within 1 business day [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/). You only need the form for the mailbox owner and/or one company to start, but USPS can ask for forms from any listed recipient [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/). Online notary options are on our Form 1583 page.

# Earth Class Mail pricing, now LegalZoom Virtual Mail
If you look up Earth Class Mail's prices today, you end up on LegalZoom. The plans start at $39 a month, but only 5 pieces of mail a month are included at that price, and every extra piece costs $3. Here is the full fee schedule as LegalZoom published it on November 21, 2026.

## What changed: the brand and the web address

- The pricing page moved. earthclassmail.com/pricing now sends you (HTTP 301) to LegalZoom's "LZ Virtual Mail" page [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html).
- It's the same company. LegalZoom's page says, "Earth Class Mail is now part of LegalZoom" [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html). Help articles and the cancellation policy are still on help.earthclassmail.com [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034846614-Cancellation-FAQ-s).
- The prices haven't changed since our November 19 check. The plan prices and per-item fees on November 21 matched our November 19 comparison table ($39 / $59 / $119 MailBox plans) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html).
- The address network: "53 real street addresses across 44 states," and you can't pick up mail in person. "Our service is entirely virtual" [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html).

## Business plans

| Startup MailRoom | $179/mo | 80 | 25 | 5 |

All from LegalZoom's business Virtual Mail page [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html). Every plan says "auto-renews." Junk mail doesn't count toward the item limit, and scanning is free for documents of 20 pages or less [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html). We didn't see an annual-billing price on the page.

## What it costs at real mail volumes
Plan price plus $3 for each item over the allowance [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html). Junk mail is left out of the count, and forwarding and check deposits are extra.

See Stable vs Earth Class Mail for a provider that includes 30 pieces at its entry price.

## Signing up and canceling

- Billing starts right away. "Billing starts upon account creation and is not dependent on the completion or approval of USPS Form 1583" [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360035551454-Acceptable-Identification-for-USPS-1583-Non-SSN-Holders).
- Form 1583: LegalZoom says, "If a notary is required, we make the process seamless with our free notarization service" [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/personal/virtual-mail-overview.html). If you don't have a Social Security number, you go through the notary session with a foreign passport, Matricula Consular or NEXUS card as your photo ID [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360035551454-Acceptable-Identification-for-USPS-1583-Non-SSN-Holders).
- Canceling at the end of the billing cycle is free. A $50 fee applies only if you choose 6 more months of account access. During those 6 months, received mail is $3 per item, and shipments are $5 domestic or $10 international, plus postage and $1 per item [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034846614-Cancellation-FAQ-s).
- Mail after you close: mail is shredded for 6 months, then returned to sender. Earth Class Mail says "USPS rules do not allow for mail forwarding" after you cancel. Reopening within 3 months costs $99. You can't pause an account [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034846614-Cancellation-FAQ-s).

## Who Earth Class Mail fits
Teams that want company-run processing facilities, AI summaries and API integrations, and that get enough mail to justify Essentials or higher [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html). For a single person with a few letters a month, a $39 plan with a $3 overage is expensive next to the plans on our cheapest virtual mailbox page.

# Getting a U.S. virtual mailbox while living abroad
You can open a U.S. virtual mailbox from another country, but the USPS Form 1583 step works differently for you. Your ID, your proof of address and the person who witnesses your signature all have to meet USPS rules, and each provider adds its own. Here's what USPS says and what seven providers require, checked November 21, 2026.

## What USPS requires, wherever you live

- Who can witness your signature: the mail center (CMRA) owner, manager or an authorized employee, in person or "in real-time audio and video," or "a notary public commissioned in a United States state, territory, possession, or the District of Columbia" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). A notary commissioned only in another country isn't on that list, which is why providers steer overseas customers to a video call or a U.S. online notary.
- Photo ID: a passport counts, and USPS defines it as "a U.S. passport, U.S. passport card, or foreign passport." A Mexican Matricula Consular card is also listed [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/608.htm).
- Address ID: a lease, mortgage or deed of trust; a voter or vehicle registration card; a home or vehicle insurance policy; Form I-94; or a second acceptable photo ID [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/608.htm).
- Not accepted: Social Security cards, birth certificates and credit cards [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/608.htm).
- Your address must match. The mail center has to confirm you live at the permanent address on the form, and "if information on the application does not match the identification, the CMRA must deny the application" [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). The form asks for a country, so a foreign home address is expected [source](https://about.usps.com/forms/ps1583.pdf).

## How each provider handles overseas customers

| Provider | How you sign from abroad | Cost to sign | ID rules worth knowing |
| Traveling Mailbox | Video call with their team, including for customers "living outside of the United States." Takes "as little as 5 to 10 minutes" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953) | Included. Asked whether the form must be notarized, the company answers "No!" [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953) | Lists passport and alien registration card among accepted IDs [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953) |
| US Global Mail | Verified online during setup, with a pre-filled form [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/usps-form-1583/?via=michelle) | Included ("No need to find a notary separately") [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/usps-form-1583/?via=michelle) | Proof of address "from any country"; for Box 9, "international addresses are allowed" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/usps-form-1583/?via=michelle) |
| Stable | ID photos and a verification selfie, reviewed by Stable in "about 1 business day or less" [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8236356-why-are-my-ids-being-verified-for-the-usps-1583). Says it works with "many business owners and founders located outside of the United States" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Included [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8236356-why-are-my-ids-being-verified-for-the-usps-1583) | Your address ID must show your street address and "cannot be a private mailbox" [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8236356-why-are-my-ids-being-verified-for-the-usps-1583) |
| Earth Class Mail (LegalZoom) | Without a Social Security number you must use their online notary partner, Proof. Self-verification isn't an option [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/25619300469143-Activate-your-Virtual-Mail-service) | LegalZoom calls it a "free notarization service" [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/personal/virtual-mail-overview.html) | Foreign passport, Matricula Consular or NEXUS. IDs must use the Latin alphabet, and notary sessions run in English or Spanish. Billing starts when you create the account, before the form is approved [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360035551454-Acceptable-Identification-for-USPS-1583-Non-SSN-Holders) |
| iPostal1 | "Customers living outside the U.S, who sign up for a U.S. address MUST use our online notary service" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | $25 [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | Foreign passport listed as a photo ID [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) |
| Anytime Mailbox | Online notary partner by video, "for domestic and international applicants" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583) | "A nominal fee" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583) | "Foreign IDs are accepted as long as they correspond to one of the abovementioned IDs and are in English" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583) |
| PostScan Mail | Notarize online or in person, then upload [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) | $20 partner online notary [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) | "Foreign driver's licenses, national ID cards, foreign university ID cards, etc., are not acceptable." Documents must be "in English or English-translated" [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) |

## The address-proof problem, and how people solve it
Your passport is usually the easy part. The second document is harder, because it has to show the home address you put on the form [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm). Here's what the rules allow:

- A foreign lease or home insurance policy fits the USPS list [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/608.htm). Check language rules first: Anytime Mailbox and PostScan want English (or an English translation at PostScan) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html), and Earth Class Mail wants the Latin alphabet [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360035551454-Acceptable-Identification-for-USPS-1583-Non-SSN-Holders).
- A second photo ID can serve as the address ID under USPS rules [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/608.htm). Whether a given provider accepts, for example, a second passport in place of a lease is up to that provider.
- Form I-94 is on the USPS list of address IDs [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/608.htm). Not every provider's own list includes it (Earth Class Mail's non-SSN list doesn't, for example) [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360035551454-Acceptable-Identification-for-USPS-1583-Non-SSN-Holders).
- A national ID card isn't on the USPS photo-ID list, and PostScan explicitly rejects it [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/608.htm) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).

## Getting mail to you overseas

| Provider | International forwarding fee |
| Traveling Mailbox | Postage + $2 per shipment. Ships "anywhere in the world" by USPS, FedEx or UPS [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| US Global Mail | No handling fee. Carrier rates the company says are discounted up to 80% off retail (USPS excepted). Repacking $5 per box or $2 per letter [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022385-how-much-does-it-cost-to-ship-my-mail) |
| Earth Class Mail | $5 per shipment + postage + $1 per item [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| PostScan Mail | The pricing page lists one forwarding fee with no separate international rate: $2.00 for the first item, $0.50 each after that, plus shipping. Customs forms and duties may apply to packages [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) |
| iPostal1 | Live rates set by each mail center. Certain locations advertise up to 80% off international shipping [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) |
| Stable | Ships "anywhere in the world" at the cost of postage [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |

For letters, a per-shipment fee keeps a monthly international box cheap. Twenty letters cost $2 in fees at Traveling Mailbox and $25 at Earth Class Mail ($5 + 20 × $1), postage extra at both [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html). Better still, ask for open-and-scan and only ship what you need on paper.

## Quick picks

- No notary, quick video call from any time zone: Traveling Mailbox [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953)
- Proof of address from your country explicitly allowed: US Global Mail [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/usps-form-1583/?via=michelle)
- A cheap address in a specific U.S. city, and a $25 notary is fine: iPostal1 [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php)

- Traveling Mailbox
- US Global Mail
- iPostal1

# Mail for full-time RVers and travelers
Once you've sold the house, mail needs a fixed address to land at and a way to reach you on the road. There are three real options: a virtual mailbox that forwards in batches, USPS Premium Forwarding, and USPS General Delivery. Here's what each costs and where each falls short, from USPS and provider pages checked November 21, 2026.

## The three options

| | Virtual mailbox (CMRA) | USPS Premium Forwarding (Residential) | USPS General Delivery |
| What it is | A private street address. Staff scan the envelopes and ship mail to you when you ask [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) | USPS boxes up mail addressed to your primary address and ships it to a temporary address once a week by Priority Mail [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward-premium.htm) | Mail held at one Post Office for you to collect in person [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) |
| Who it's for | Anyone who signs USPS Form 1583 with two IDs [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) | Residential customers who still have a primary address. Temporary only [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward-premium.htm) | "Transients and customers not permanently located," as a temporary means of delivery [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) |
| Cost | Plan fee plus a forwarding fee and postage (see below) | $26.40 to enroll online ($28.70 at a Post Office), plus $29.70 for each week [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward-premium.htm) | DMM 508.6 lists no fee [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) |
| How long | As long as you pay | At least 2 weeks and at most 1 year [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) | Each piece is held no more than 30 days [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) |
| See your mail before it ships? | Yes, envelope scans | No. Everything comes in the weekly box [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward-premium.htm) | No |
| Catches | "Some states and institutions may have restrictions" on these addresses [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) (see South Dakota below) | Domestic addresses only. Not available for APO/FPO/DPO or Guam [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward-premium.htm) | Normally offered at only one facility per Post Office, and you can use only one. The postmaster can refuse without ID, or if your mail volume can't be accommodated [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm) |

What a year of Premium Forwarding costs: $26.40 + 52 × $29.70 = $1,570.80 if you enroll online [source](https://www.usps.com/manage/forward-premium.htm). It also only works while you still have a primary address for USPS to forward from, so it suits a long trip more than full-time life on the road [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).

## What forwarding costs at each virtual mailbox
On the road, what matters is the fee every time you have a batch shipped to a campground or a friend's house. Here's one monthly batch of 20 letters, before postage:

| Provider | Forwarding fee rule | 20 letters in one box | Free physical storage |
| Traveling Mailbox | Postage + $2 per shipment, not per piece [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | $2 | Envelopes 30 days, then shredded unless you pay $1 per envelope per month to hold them [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) |
| US Global Mail | No handling fee. Optional repacking is $2 per letter or $5 per box [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) | $0 (repacking, if you ask for it, is extra) | 30 days on Scale, then $0.05 per item per day [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) |
| Stable | "Add cost of postage" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | $0 + postage | 30 days, then securely disposed of [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) |
| PostScan Mail | $2.00 for the first item, $0.50 each after that, plus shipping [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) | $11.50 | 14 days (30 with an annual plan), then $0.05 per envelope per day [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Earth Class Mail (LegalZoom) | $1.25 per shipment + $1 per item + postage [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) | $21.25 | Letters 30 days, then $1.50 per month [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| iPostal1 | Real-time rates set by each mail center [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | Varies by location | — |

The storage window sets your rhythm. With 30 days free at most of these, a monthly batch fits. At PostScan Mail on a monthly plan, letters start costing $0.05 a day after 14 days [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html). At Stable, mail you haven't forwarded within 30 days is destroyed [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing), so scan or forward anything you need to keep. Automatic shipping of all mail is a Scale and Custom plan feature at Stable [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing).

## Using a mailbox address as your legal residence: South Dakota's rules
Many full-timers pick a "domicile" state and use a mail-forwarding address there. Each state sets its own rules for driver's licenses. South Dakota publishes its rules for full-time travelers. Its Department of Public Safety requires:

- A completed Residency Affidavit, signed in front of a notary or a South Dakota driver license examiner [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=49c27bd087a26250b81f0f280cbb3563)
- A receipt for one night's stay at a South Dakota hotel, motel, campground or RV park within the last year [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=709bcdfa47406e10237fbd51026d43a9)
- Your South Dakota personal mailbox contract, plus one document no more than a year old showing your PMB address (a receipt from the PMB business or a piece of mail) [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=709bcdfa47406e10237fbd51026d43a9)
Two lines in the affidavit matter when you choose a provider. You swear that "My personal mailbox service (PMB) is a mail forwarding service, and not a virtual only mail service," and that you don't "stay, live in, or maintain a residence in any another state" [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=49c27bd087a26250b81f0f280cbb3563). The manual adds: "if you maintain a residence in another state, you do not qualify as a full-time traveler" [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=709bcdfa47406e10237fbd51026d43a9). The affidavit also warns that a South Dakota license or ID means you'll be called for jury duty in South Dakota [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=49c27bd087a26250b81f0f280cbb3563).
South Dakota's forms don't define "virtual only mail service." Earth Class Mail and Stable both list a Sioux Falls address [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing), but whether either counts as a "mail forwarding service" for the affidavit is something to confirm with SD DPS (DPSLicensingInfo@state.sd.us, 605-773-6883, the contacts listed in the manual) before you rely on it [source](https://www.sd.gov/sys_attachment.do?sys_id=709bcdfa47406e10237fbd51026d43a9). A driver's license is also only one part of domicile. Taxes, voting and insurance each have their own rules, which we don't cover here.
Other states: iPostal1 says customers have used its addresses "for their DMV needs" but that "the laws vary by state and change periodically" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php). Check your own state's DMV before you sign up.

## A setup that works for most full-timers

- Pick a provider with a per-shipment forwarding fee (not per item) if you forward in batches: Traveling Mailbox ($2 per box) [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953), or US Global Mail or Stable (postage only) [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022318-us-global-mail-features-explained) [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing).
- Sign Form 1583 on a video call if you can. Traveling Mailbox, Stable and US Global Mail don't need a notary. See Form 1583 and online notarization.
- File a USPS change of address or update your senders yourself. Form 1583 doesn't move your mail [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/the-usps-form-1583?ref=3953).
- Have mail sent to a campground or a Post Office General Delivery window in a town you'll be in for a while. Call the destination Post Office first to ask which facility and ZIP Code to use [source](https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/508.htm).

- Traveling Mailbox
- US Global Mail

# Stable vs Earth Class Mail for a startup
Both sell business-grade mail scanning to startups, but they charge in very different ways. Earth Class Mail (now LegalZoom Virtual Mail) has the lower sticker price and includes few pieces of mail. Stable costs more up front and includes six times as much. Which one is cheaper depends almost entirely on how much mail you get. Checked November 21, 2026.

## Side by side

| | Stable | Earth Class Mail / LegalZoom |
| Entry plan | Grow: $59/mo monthly, or $49/mo billed yearly [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Starter MailBox: $39/mo, auto-renews [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Next plan up | Scale: $99/mo monthly, or $83/mo billed yearly [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Essentials MailBox: $59/mo [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Mail included (entry plan) | 30 pieces/month on monthly billing, 360/year on yearly. Junk mail isn't counted [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | 5 items/month digitized. Junk mail isn't counted [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Over the limit | $3 per piece [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | $3 per item [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Opening and scanning | Free open-and-scan on every plan [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Free for documents of 20 pages or less, then $0.15 per page [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Recipients (names) | Unlimited [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | 2 on Starter; $5/mo per extra [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Logins | 1 user included; $20/mo per extra on Grow (3 paid users max), $30/mo on Scale [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | 1 seat on Starter (up to 2); $19/mo per extra seat [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Forwarding | Cost of postage [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | $1.25 per shipment + postage + $1 per item [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Free physical storage | Mail 30 days, packages 15 days, then disposed of [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Letters 30 days, then $1.50/mo. Packages 10 days, then $15 per lb per month [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Check deposit | Separate purchase: "volume-based plans as low as $3/check" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | $10 per check, or $39/mo for 5 checks plus $2 each after that [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Registered agent | Add-on, $25/mo per state [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | Sold separately by LegalZoom. The price isn't listed on the Virtual Mail page |
| Addresses | 39 cities listed on the pricing page [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | 53 street addresses in 44 states [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Form 1583 | No notary. Stable verifies your IDs in about 1 business day [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8236356-why-are-my-ids-being-verified-for-the-usps-1583) | Self-verify online or use the partner notary. LegalZoom calls it a "free notarization service" [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/25619300469143-Activate-your-Virtual-Mail-service) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/personal/virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Startup discount | 50% off Grow for 1 year if revenue is under $1M or you're using the address to form a company, subject to approval [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | None listed on the pricing page [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html) |
| Refund / cancel | 30-day money-back guarantee [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | No fee to cancel at the end of the cycle. Billing starts when you create the account, even before Form 1583 is approved [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360034846614-Cancellation-FAQ-s) [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/360035551454-Acceptable-Identification-for-USPS-1583-Non-SSN-Holders) |

## Monthly cost at three mail volumes
Monthly billing, entry plans, one user, nothing forwarded or deposited. Pieces of mail that aren't junk [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html).

| Mail / month | Stable Grow | ECM Starter | ECM Essentials |
| 5 pieces | $59 | $39 | $59 |
| 15 pieces | $59 | $39 + 10 × $3 = $69 | $59 (tie) |
| 30 pieces | $59 | $39 + 25 × $3 = $114 | $59 + 5 × $3 = $74 |

With the 50% startup discount, Grow drops to about $29.50 on monthly billing, or $24.50 a month on yearly billing, for the first year. That assumes the discount applies to whichever billing interval you pick, which the page doesn't spell out [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing). At 12 or more real pieces a month, Earth Class Mail Starter costs more than Stable Grow at full price: $39 + 7 × $3 = $60 at 12 pieces, against $59 (at 11 pieces it's $57).

## Which to pick

- Very little mail (a handful of IRS and state letters): Earth Class Mail Starter at $39 is the cheaper of the two [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html).
- 15 or more pieces a month, or several company names on one box: Stable. Unlimited recipients and 30 included pieces make Grow cheaper [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing).
- You also need a registered agent: Stable lists it at $25/mo per state, alongside your mail in the same dashboard [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing).
- Paper checks: it depends on your volume. Earth Class Mail charges $10 per check without the subscription [source](https://www.legalzoom.com/business/business-operations/lz-virtual-mail-overview.html), while Stable's rate starts "as low as $3" [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing). See check deposit fees.

- Stable
- Earth Class Mail / LegalZoom Virtual Mail

# Anytime Mailbox pricing: why it ranges so widely
Anytime Mailbox doesn't have one price list. Each location is run by an independent mail center operator who sets their own plans and per-item fees. So "from $9.99" can mean 15 or 100 items a month, and $0.18 or $1.00 per scanned page. On November 20, 2026 we read the "starting from" price of every U.S. location on Anytime Mailbox's state pages, and the full plans at five of them.

## What Anytime Mailbox itself says

- "Our cheapest virtual mailbox plans are $4.99. On average, our plans cost $9.99 per month. Some of our vanity addresses can cost up to $50" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/)
- "All service plans show what the included services are for each plan before you sign up, and what the fees are for any additional actions you request beyond your chosen plan from your mail center operator" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/)
- Each location page names its "Mail Center Operator" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd)

## Starting prices across all U.S. locations
The state pages list 2,095 U.S. locations with a "Starting from" price [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/l/usa). 2,089 quote a monthly price. Six quote only a yearly price (covered below). For the 2,089 monthly prices:

| Starting price | Locations | Share |
| Under $8.00 | 26 | 1.2% |
| $8.00–$9.99 | 1,001 | 47.9% |
| $10.00–$14.99 | 652 | 31.2% |
| $15.00–$19.99 | 214 | 10.2% |
| $20.00–$50.00 | 167 | 8.0% |
| Over $50.00 | 29 | 1.4% |

- The median is $10.99. Exactly $9.99 is the most common price, at 944 locations.
- We found only one $4.99 location: Arlington, VA (1550 Wilson Blvd) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd). The next cheapest was $5.99, in Fort Walton Beach, FL.
- The highest monthly starting price was $99.99, in Denver (Fiddlers Green Cir). 29 locations start above the "up to $50" mentioned in the FAQ.
Method: we parsed the location cards on each of Anytime Mailbox's U.S. state pages on 2026-11-20. Counts are a snapshot, and the site's own location count can differ slightly from the number of cards shown.

### Cheapest and median starting price by state

| State | Locations (monthly-priced) | Cheapest | Median | Highest |
| California | 396 | $7.99 | $9.99 | $75.00 |
| Texas | 290 | $7.99 | $11.99 | $59.99 |
| Florida | 242 | $5.99 | $10.49 | $69.00 |
| Georgia | 100 | $7.99 | $10.99 | $49.99 |
| New York | 96 | $8.99 | $11.99 | $84.99 |
| Nevada | 47 | $7.99 | $9.99 | $49.99 |
| Massachusetts | 22 | $8.99 | $11.99 | $49.99 |
| Delaware | 18 | $6.99 | $9.99 | $15.99 |
| Wyoming | 6 | $7.99 | $9.99 | $19.99 |

Source: each state's location list, e.g. Texas, Florida, Delaware. Florida's median falls between two locations, which is why it isn't a typical price ending.

## Same price, different plan: five real locations
The starting price tells you little about what's included. Here are the cheapest plans at five locations, copied from their Anytime Mailbox pages:

| Location (operator) | Cheapest plan | Mail included | Open & scan | Forwarding | Recipients |
| Arlington, VA (TKO Suites) | Bronze $4.99/mo or $56.99/yr | 15/mo | $1.00 per page | "No handling fees" | 1 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd) |
| Austin, TX, 9th St (Virtual Mail Hub) | "Just an Address" $7.99/mo or $79.90/yr | None: $1.44 per incoming item | $0.18 each | $5.00 each | 1 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/austin-605-w-9th-street) |
| Omaha, NE (Advance Tax Solutions) | Bronze $9.99/mo or $109.99/yr | 30/mo | $0.50 per page | $5.00 per shipping bundle | 1 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue) |
| Washington, DC, H St NE (Gold Spot Pack and Ship) | Bronze $9.99/mo or $109.99/yr | 30/mo | $0.50 per page | $3.00 each | 1 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/washington-712-h-street-ne) |
| Astoria, NY (Astorias Hub) | Bronze $9.99/mo or $109.99/yr | 15/mo | 10 pages/mo included | Unlimited | 5 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/astoria-2509-astoria-boulevard) |

What stands out:

- The $4.99 plan has the priciest scans. Opening one 3-page letter at Arlington costs $3.00. That's more than half the monthly fee [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd).
- "Just an Address" charges for every piece of mail. At Austin 9th St, 10 letters a month adds $14.40 to the $7.99 fee, for a total of $22.39. The $12.99 "Address Pro" plan at the same location includes 60 items and 60 scans [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/austin-605-w-9th-street).
- Plan names aren't standard. "Bronze" means 15 items in Arlington and Astoria, but 30 in Omaha and DC [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue).
- Yearly billing doesn't always save the same amount. Omaha's $109.99 a year compares with $119.88 for 12 monthly payments. Arlington's $56.99 compares with $59.88 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd).

## The yearly-only locations
Six U.S. locations show only a yearly price, so their "starting from" number looks very high next to monthly prices. Examples are Brooklyn (495 Henry St) and Beverly Hills (Santa Monica Blvd), both at $399.99, and Overland Park, KS at $319.99. At 495 Henry St, the single plan is "Gold" at $399.99 a year. It includes 240 items a month, $0.25 per scanned page, $2.00 per forward and 5 recipients [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/brooklyn-495a-henry-street). That's about $33 a month, not $400.

## Fees that aren't on the location card

- Form 1583 notarization. Anytime Mailbox uses an online notary partner "for a nominal fee," or you can see your operator in person [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583). We couldn't find a published amount.
- Overage, storage, shredding and check deposit are set per plan by the operator and shown under "Full Details" before sign-up [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/). They aren't on a central price list.

## How to pick an Anytime Mailbox location without overpaying

- Estimate your mail: items a month, and how many you'll want opened.
- Compare the full plan at two or three nearby locations, not the "starting from" price.
- Multiply the per-page or per-item scan fee by your usual openings. That's where cheap plans get expensive.
- Check whether you need more than one recipient name, since many Bronze plans include just one [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/washington-712-h-street-ne).
Comparing with iPostal1, which publishes one price list for all locations? See iPostal1 vs Anytime Mailbox and iPostal1 pricing explained.

- Anytime Mailbox locations

# Best virtual mailbox for an LLC (and what it can't do)
Short answer: A virtual mailbox works as an LLC's mailing address, and it can go on line 4 (mailing address) of IRS Form SS-4. It can't be the registered office on its own: Texas, Florida and California require a registered agent at a real in-state street address. Pair the mailbox with a registered agent service. [source](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iss4) [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/corp/formationfaqs.shtml) [source](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/605.0113)

An LLC deals with up to three addresses: a registered office where its registered agent accepts lawsuits, a principal office, and a mailing address. A virtual mailbox is built for the last one. It can't be the registered office unless someone there actually serves as your registered agent. Here's what the states and the IRS ask for, and which providers fill the gap. Checked November 20, 2026. This is a summary of published rules, not legal advice.

## Can a virtual mailbox be your LLC's registered office?

- Texas: "An entity's registered office must be a physical address in Texas where the registered agent can be personally served with process during business hours. It cannot solely be the address of a mailbox service or telephone answering service." [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/corp/formationfaqs.shtml) The Certificate of Formation instructions say the same, citing BOC § 5.201 [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/corp/instructions/201.shtml).
- Florida: every LLC must keep a registered office and a registered agent "whose business address is identical to the address of the registered office" [source](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/605.0113). The articles must give the agent's "street address in this state" [source](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/605.0201).
- California: the Secretary of State's FAQ says the agent for service of process must be an individual who lives in California, or a registered "1505" corporate agent. The agent's name and "physical street address" are public record [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/business-programs/business-entities/faqs).
In practice, that means your registered agent is either you (at a real street address in the state, open during business hours) or a registered agent company. A mail-scanning address doesn't fill this role on its own.

## Can a virtual mailbox be your LLC's mailing address?

- Texas asks for an initial mailing address in the certificate of formation, which the Comptroller uses for tax mail. It "may be a post office box or street address" [source](https://www.sos.texas.gov/corp/instructions/201.shtml).
- Florida asks for "the street and mailing addresses of the company's principal office" [source](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/605.0201). Whether a commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA) address is accepted as the principal street address isn't stated in the statute.
- IRS (Form SS-4, EIN): line 4 is the mailing address, and "generally, this address will be used on all tax returns." Line 5 is the physical address, only if different, and you shouldn't enter a P.O. box there [source](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iss4). A virtual mailbox address works as a mailing address on line 4.
State rules vary. US Global Mail says a virtual or PMB address "can be used to open an LLC but there are some states that do not allow it," and names Washington and California as requiring physical addresses [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022325-what-can-or-can-t-the-us-global-mail-address-be-used-for). We haven't confirmed that against those states' filing rules. iPostal1 likewise says "laws vary by state" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php). Check your state's filing instructions before you file.

## Will banks accept a virtual mailbox address?
US Global Mail says most banks accept its address. It adds that "some banks have recently started asking for a personal address, which is not a CMRA" address [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022325-what-can-or-can-t-the-us-global-mail-address-be-used-for). We found no published bank-by-bank rules, so ask your bank before you apply.

## Plans that let you receive mail in a business name

| Provider | Cheapest business-capable plan | Registered agent add-on | Form 1583 |
| iPostal1 | Virtual Business Address $14.99/mo, 30 items, 1 company name. The $9.99 plan is personal only [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php) [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | $99/yr, 25 states + DC listed [source](https://ipostal1.com/) | $25 online notary or in person [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) |
| Stable | Grow $49/mo billed yearly, 360 pieces a year, unlimited recipients. Early-stage discount: 50% off Grow for a year if you use the address to incorporate or have under $1M revenue, subject to approval [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | $25/mo per state [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing) | No notary; Stable verifies IDs [source](https://support.usestable.com/en/articles/8236356-why-are-my-ids-being-verified-for-the-usps-1583) |
| Virtual Post Mail | Starter $20/mo, 2 recipients; the business must be added as a recipient [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/registered-agent/pricing/) | Free with every mailbox plan in CA, DE, FL, NV and TX, if the mailbox is in the same state [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/registered-agent/pricing/) | Notarized, plus two IDs [source](https://www.virtualpostmail.com/virtual-mailbox/pricing/) |
| PhysicalAddress.com | Plan 30 from $7.98/mo; starting prices are higher in some cities. It advertises the address for personal or business use and includes unlimited recipients [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/locations/) | "Free Registered Agent Service with Account." It does not publish a state-by-state list on that page [source](https://physicaladdress.com/registered-agent-service/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/) | Notarized, or signed at one of its locations; online notary fee not published [source](https://physicaladdress.com/knowledge-base/how-do-i-sign-up-for-physicaladdress-com/) |
| Earth Class Mail (LegalZoom Virtual Mail) | Starter MailBox $39/mo, 5 items digitized, 2 recipients [source](https://www.earthclassmail.com/pricing) | Says you "must still maintain a registered agent"; add-on price isn't listed on that page [source](https://www.earthclassmail.com/pricing) | Self-verify online or online notary [source](https://help.earthclassmail.com/hc/en-us/articles/25619300469143-Activate-your-Virtual-Mail-service) |
| Traveling Mailbox | Basic $15/mo; business names can be added to any plan [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | None listed on pricing page | No notary; video call [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-do-i-complete-the-usps-form-1583/) |
| US Global Mail | Occasional $21/mo billed annually, or $25/mo monthly. Scale is $49/mo billed annually, or $65/mo monthly. Prices are marked "*varies by address" [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/pricing/?via=michelle) | "We currently don't offer Registered Agent Service" [source](https://support.usglobalmail.com/en/articles/11022325-what-can-or-can-t-the-us-global-mail-address-be-used-for) | No separate notary [source](https://www.usglobalmail.com/usps-form-1583/?via=michelle) |
| Anytime Mailbox | Set per location; check whether the plan allows a business name [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) | — | Notarized; online partner [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583) |

Stable's and US Global Mail's prices depend on monthly vs yearly billing. The figures above are the lowest shown on each pricing page, and the existing comparison table has both billing options.

## Cheapest compliant setups

- You'll be your own registered agent at a home or office address in the state: add the cheapest business mailbox for everything else. Traveling Mailbox Basic is $15 [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) and iPostal1 Virtual Business Address is $14.99 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php). Keep in mind your agent address becomes public record [source](https://www.sos.ca.gov/business-programs/business-entities/faqs).
- You want a registered agent and mailbox on one bill: PhysicalAddress.com includes a registered agent with the account and starts at $7.98 a month, though it does not list which states that covers [source](https://physicaladdress.com/registered-agent-service/) [source](https://physicaladdress.com/pricing/). iPostal1 Virtual Business Address plus the registered agent add-on is $14.99 × 12 + $99 = about $279 a year for one covered state before scans, or $149 + $99 = $248 on yearly billing [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php) [source](https://ipostal1.com/). Stable Grow plus one state's agent is $49 + $25 = $74 a month on yearly billing [source](https://www.usestable.com/pricing).

- iPostal1 Virtual Business Address
- Stable
- Virtual Post Mail
- Traveling Mailbox

# iPostal1 pricing, explained
The $9.99 iPostal1 plan is real, but it gets you 30 envelope images a month at a Standard address, for personal mail only. Opening a letter costs $2.25, and a business name means the $14.99 plan. Below is every published tier and fee, copied from iPostal1's pricing pages on November 20, 2026.

## The three plan families
iPostal1 sells three kinds of plans. Each has four tiers that differ only by how many mail items you get a month [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php).

| Mail items / month | Virtual Mailing Address (personal) | Virtual Business Address | Virtual Office (phone + fax) |
| 30 | $9.99/mo or $99/yr [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $14.99/mo or $149/yr [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php) | n/a |
| 60 | $14.99/mo or $149/yr [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $19.99/mo or $199/yr [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php) | $39.99/mo or $399/yr, local number [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php) |
| 120 | $24.99/mo or $249/yr [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $29.99/mo or $299/yr [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php) | $49.99/mo local, or $59.99/mo toll-free [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php) |
| 240 | $39.99/mo or $399/yr [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | $44.99/mo or $449/yr [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php) | $69.99/mo or $699/yr, toll-free [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php) |

The yearly price works out to ten months of the monthly price. iPostal1 calls it "2 Months Free" [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php). All three families have no contract, and you can change plans every month [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).

## Personal vs business: the $5 difference that matters

- Virtual Mailing Address plans are "for personal use only." They include up to 6 recipient names but "no company name" [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
- Virtual Business Address plans add 1 company name (still up to 6 recipients) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php). iPostal1 says to use these to "register your business" [source](https://ipostal1.com/).
- Virtual Office plans add a local or toll-free phone number and a fax number. Calls are metered: inbound calls to a local number cost $0.015 a minute, forwarding to a U.S. number costs $0.02 a minute, and voicemail beyond 250 free minutes costs $0.01 a minute [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php).
If mail will arrive in an LLC's name, the real entry price is $14.99, not $9.99. See using a virtual mailbox for an LLC.

## Why your address may cost more than $9.99
iPostal1 says roughly 90% of its locations are "Standard" addresses that start at $9.99 a month. Addresses "in prestigious buildings or in locations where costs and demand are higher" cost more [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php):

| Address type | Surcharge (as published) | 30-item personal plan would be |
| Standard | none | $9.99 |
| Select | +$10 | $19.99 if the surcharge is monthly |
| Premium | +$20 | $29.99 if the surcharge is monthly |
| Prestige | +$30 | $39.99 if the surcharge is monthly |

The FAQ doesn't say whether the surcharge is per month or whether it changes on yearly billing [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php). Check the price shown for your chosen address at checkout.

## Pay-per-use fees (all plan families)
These are the same on all three U.S. pricing pages. iPostal1 notes they don't apply to Canadian locations [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).

| Service | Price |
| Envelope image of every item | Included [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Mail items over your plan's limit | $0.35 per item [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Open and scan, or shred (1 envelope = 1 order) | $2.25 for up to 10 pages, then $0.25 per page [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Prepaid scan/shred bundles (no expiry, non-refundable) | $10 for 5 · $18 for 10 · $30 for 20 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Discard (recycle) an item | Included [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Forwarding | Real-time shipping price for the carrier you pick. Consolidating letters is free; $1.95 per package or letter-pack consolidated [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Check deposit by mail (most locations) | $4.95 for up to 5 checks, plus check scans and trackable shipping [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Photos of a package's invoice / contents | $2.95 / $3.95 / both $5.95 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Extra shipping insurance | $4 per $100 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Receive a fax | $2 for up to 6 pages, then $0.25/page [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Pickup at the mail center | "Some locations charge a nominal fee" [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Send mail (letters / postcards) | From $0.85 / from $1.19 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |
| Registered agent add-on (business plans; 25 states + DC listed) | $99 per year [source](https://ipostal1.com/) |
| AI and live call answering add-on | From $49 a month [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) |

## Free storage, then storage fees

- Letters, letter-packs and packages under 12×12×12 in.: 30 days free. Packages up to 24×17×12 in.: 10 days. Bigger packages: 5 days [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
- After that, letters, large envelopes, magazines and postcards cost $1.10 per item per month. Packages cost $1.10 per pound (actual or dimensional weight, whichever is greater) per month, per 10 days or per 5 days, depending on size [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).

## One-time costs

- Form 1583: the online notary costs $25. You can also sign in person at many mail centers, and some charge "a small fee" for that. Customers living outside the U.S. must use the online notary [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php). Why some other providers skip the notary entirely: Form 1583 rules.
- Refunds: a full refund within the first 30 days "upon request, if account not used." Plans renew unless you cancel before the billing date [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
- Prices are "plus applicable taxes" [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).

## What a typical month costs
Say you get 25 items a month at a Standard address, open 4 letters (under 10 pages each) and recycle the rest:

- Personal 30-item plan: $9.99 + 4 × $2.25 = $18.99 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
- Same usage with the 10-pack bundle ($1.80 per order): $9.99 + 4 × $1.80 = $17.19, once you've paid $18 up front [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
- Business 30-item plan: $14.99 + $9.00 = $23.99 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php).
- First month: add $25 for the online notary, unless you sign in person [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).
If you open most of your mail, a plan with scans included can cost less. Traveling Mailbox Basic is $15 with 35 page scans [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953). See the cheapest virtual mailbox and iPostal1 vs Anytime Mailbox.

- iPostal1 plans and locations

# iPostal1 vs Anytime Mailbox
These two have the biggest location networks, and both start around $9.99. The real difference is how they price. iPostal1 has one national fee schedule. At Anytime Mailbox, each mail center operator writes their own plans. So the answer to "which is cheaper" depends on the specific address you choose and how much mail you open. Checked November 20, 2026.

## Side by side

| | iPostal1 | Anytime Mailbox |
| Locations (as advertised) | 4,250+ [source](https://ipostal1.com/) | 2,500+ [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) |
| Who sets prices | iPostal1, one price list. Addresses cost more if they're Select (+$10), Premium (+$20) or Prestige (+$30) [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | The mail center operator at each location [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) |
| Entry price | $9.99/mo for 30 items, personal use only. $14.99 to receive mail in a business name [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-business-address-plans-pricing.php) | Lowest U.S. location $4.99. Median starting price $10.99 across 2,089 monthly-priced U.S. locations (our count) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd) |
| Opening and scanning a letter | $2.25 per envelope up to 10 pages, then $0.25/page. Bundles bring it to $1.50–$2.00 per order [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Set by the location. Examples: $0.18 each (Austin 9th St), $0.50/page (Omaha, DC), $1.00/page (Arlington), or 10 pages a month included (Astoria) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/austin-605-w-9th-street) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/astoria-2509-astoria-boulevard) |
| Mail over the plan limit | $0.35 per item [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Set per plan; shown under "Full Details" [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) |
| Forwarding | Live shipping rates. Letter consolidation free, $1.95 per package consolidated [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Examples: "No handling fees" (Arlington), $3.00 each (DC), $5.00 per bundle (Omaha) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/washington-712-h-street-ne) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue) |
| Recipients on entry plan | Up to 6 names [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Often 1 (Arlington, Omaha, DC); 5 at Astoria [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/washington-712-h-street-ne) [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/astoria-2509-astoria-boulevard) |
| Free storage | 30 days for letters and small packages [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Set per location |
| Check deposit | $4.95 for up to 5 checks, plus scans and shipping (most locations) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php) | Listed as a service on location pages; fee set by the operator [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd) |
| Form 1583 | $25 online notary, or sign in person at many mail centers (some charge) [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php) | Online notary partner "for a nominal fee," or in person with the operator [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/usps-form-1583) |
| Business add-ons | Registered agent $99/yr in 25 states + DC; phone/fax plans from $39.99/mo [source](https://ipostal1.com/) [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-office-plans-pricing.php) | Virtual business address and business formation pages; pricing per location [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/) |

## Worked examples
These use published prices only, at Standard iPostal1 addresses and the actual Anytime Mailbox locations named. Postage isn't included.

### Light user: 12 letters a month, open 2 (3 pages each)

- iPostal1 personal 30-item plan: $9.99 + 2 × $2.25 = $14.49 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php)
- Anytime Mailbox, Arlington VA Bronze (15 items): $4.99 + 6 pages × $1.00 = $10.99 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd)
- Anytime Mailbox, Omaha NE Bronze (30 items): $9.99 + 6 pages × $0.50 = $12.99 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue)

### Heavier user: 28 letters a month, open 10 (3 pages each)

- iPostal1 personal 30-item plan: $9.99 + 10 × $2.25 = $32.49. Prepaying with the 10-pack ($18) instead gives $27.99 [source](https://ipostal1.com/virtual-mailing-address-plans-pricing.php).
- Anytime Mailbox, Omaha Bronze: $9.99 + 30 pages × $0.50 = $24.99 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/omaha-6311-ames-avenue)
- Anytime Mailbox, Arlington: 28 items is over Bronze's 15. Silver is $14.99 for 60 items, + $10.00 for 10 letters at "$1.00 each" = $24.99 [source](https://www.anytimemailbox.com/s/arlington-1550-wilson-blvd)
Both examples assume letters of 10 pages or fewer. Add the one-time Form 1583 cost in month one: $25 at iPostal1 if you use its online notary [source](https://ipostal1.com/faq-mailbox-account.php).

## Which should you pick?

### Pick iPostal1 if…
you want the same fees wherever your address is, need several recipient names on a cheap plan, or want a registered agent and mailbox on one login.

### Pick Anytime Mailbox if…
you'll compare a few locations' full plans. A good operator can be cheaper than iPostal1's $2.25 per scan, especially if you open a lot of short letters.

### Pick neither if…
you'd rather skip the notary. Traveling Mailbox, Stable and US Global Mail do Form 1583 without one (details).

- iPostal1
- Anytime Mailbox

# Traveling Mailbox vs PostScan Mail
PostScan Mail is cheaper if you just want envelope images. Traveling Mailbox is cheaper as soon as you want letters opened, and it skips the notary. Here's every published fee from both, checked November 19, 2026.

| | Traveling Mailbox | PostScan Mail |
| Entry plan | Basic $15/mo [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | Starter "as low as $10/mo," or $8.33/mo billed annually; price varies by location [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Mail included | 40 envelopes/mo, junk mail doesn't count [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | 30 items/mo, and junk mail counts [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) |
| Opening and scanning | 35 page scans/mo included; $0.50 per extra page [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | $2.00 per envelope up to 10 pages, then $0.25 per page. Standard ($20+) includes 5 free [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Extra mail | $0.25 per envelope over the allowance [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | $0.50 per item over the limit [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Forwarding | Postage + $2 per shipment, not per item [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | $2.00 first item + $0.50 each additional, plus shipping [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Shredding | Free [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | $1.00 per item for the first 10 pages [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Free mail storage | 30 days, then $1 per envelope per month to hold [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | 14 days (30 on annual), then $0.05 per envelope per day [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Check deposit | $4.95 per check + postage [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | Not listed on the pricing page |
| Recipients on entry plan | 3 [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953) | 1 (extra: $5/mo each) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |
| Form 1583 | Video call with staff; no notary [source](https://kb.travelingmailbox.com/how-do-i-complete-the-usps-form-1583/) | Notarized; partner online notary $20 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html) |
| Local pickup | Not mentioned on the pricing page | Free at most locations [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html) |

## Worked example
Take 25 letters a month, with 8 opened (about 3 pages each) and 5 shredded:

- Traveling Mailbox Basic: $15. 25 envelopes and 24 pages are inside the allowance, and shredding is free [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).
- PostScan Mail Starter: $10 + 8 × $2.00 for open-and-scan + 5 × $1.00 for shredding = $31. On Standard at $20 (5 free scans), it's $20 + 3 × $2.00 + $5 = $31 [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
Add the $20 notary at PostScan in your first month [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/faq.html).

## When PostScan Mail wins

- You want an address in a particular city and to pick up mail in person, which is free at most PostScan locations [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).
- You rarely open mail and want the lowest monthly bill.
- You need extras like HIPAA compliance ($25/mo billed annually) [source](https://www.postscanmail.com/pricing.html).

## When Traveling Mailbox wins

- You want most mail opened and scanned.
- You'd rather skip the notary.
- You forward in batches, since it's $2 per shipment no matter how many pieces are in it [source](https://travelingmailbox.com/pricing?ref=3953).

- Traveling Mailbox
- PostScan Mail
